 #6707 
 Snowball RLVR matrix closes; frozen-router E10 reaches 0.918 pass@16

 Epic title: RL data curation, experiments & ablations

 Summary: Ongoing area of investment, picking up after the July Commitment and Hero Run work in this milestone.

 Benjamin Feuer closed out the full Snowball 67B-A2B non-agentic reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) experiment matrix in #7786 this week, posting verdicts for every arm alongside an experiment index and synthesis document. The newest cohort, E10, was a four-arm frozen-router ablation at 32k context. Its AdamW control produced the campaign's strongest learning curve: reward climbed from 0.743 to +0.530 and pass@16 from 0.688 to 0.918 over nine steps, with stable gradient norms and rising advantages direct evidence that the router-bias corruption tracked in MarinSkyRL #309 had been the binding constraint on earlier arms. Every 32k arm, however, died around step 10 11 from the same failure mode: a stochastic max-length rollout VRAM-spikes one rank, which silently drops, and the remaining 63 ranks hang a 1-element ALLREDUCE for the full 1,800-second watchdog. The failure is optimizer-independent and sequence-length-driven; MuonH OOM'd at step 5 on-device, and expert-parallel was chronically gradient-unstable with raw gradient norm spiking to 204 at step 9. hero-v1, the campaign's first full-budget continuation of E6, confirmed the RLVR-MATH dataset effect at 32k and scale reward from 0.744 to 0.334 and pass@16 reaching 0.621 through step 8 but terminated at step 31 of the same rank-drop, and its resume died on a transient S3 checkpoint read timeout. The hero-v2 proposal supersedes it with four changes: 24k context to cap the worst-case sequence at roughly 23k tokens instead of 31k, MuonH as the optimizer to match pretraining, truncated importance sampling (TIS) plus training-inference token ordering (TITO), and frozen router. Four MarinSkyRL fixes merged in support: rank-drop fast-fail #331 , resume read-amplification reduction #332 , launcher retry budget #333 , and TITO alignment-metric inheritance #336 . The proposal is posted but not yet authorized. On the data side, the normalized post-training pool specification #7799 moved to design-doc stage, with Russell Power noting that the datasets need first-hand inspection before requirements settle. #8060 was filed to rerun E6 with MuonH, framed as an onboarding exercise for learning the RL framework and Iris. Separately, Romain Yon closed out the Grug eager-versus-grouped divergence investigation #7903 : the first mismatch was localized to BF16 accumulation order at the final index_add_ combine, and an FP32 accumulation correction was merged into MarinSkyRL #276 . The correction is 3.84% slower at the combine boundary with 252 MB additional peak allocation, accepted for grouped-reduction stability; the live-routing route-aware residual one action log probability exceeding tolerance by 0.07% remains formally unresolved.

 #6708 
 SkyRL artifact merges; legacy in-process RL engine deleted

 Epic title: RL framework of the future

 Summary: Ongoing area of investment, picking up after the July Commitment and Hero Run work in this milestone.

 Russell Power 's SkyRL artifact PR #7883 merged on August 7 after a week open for review. Pretraining, SFT, group-relative policy optimization (GRPO), and evaluation are now expressible as a single typed Marin artifact graph, with SkyRL kept as an isolated external runtime pinned by commit and profile. The artifact owns immutable model and data locators, a semantic role topology, checkpoint roots, and a validated terminal policy; the iceball-micro experiment validates the full graph on a random-init Qwen3-0.6B-size model, with resilience evidence from a planned-preemption resume and a stalled-worker recovery. The PR closes #7797 . The supporting framework changes that #7883 consumes landed in sequence. MarinSkyRL #284 consolidated the distribution into one root package and frozen lock on August 3. #296 then wired Iris training tasks to install from that frozen distribution at the exact pinned commit, replacing the custom image build, on August 5. On the Marin side, #8063 externalized the TPU vLLM stack into an isolated uvx environment and deleted the legacy in-process marin.rl engine entirely on August 8 the engine had no live consumers, and its in-process vLLM path was the reason the TPU inference forks had to co-resolve in the workspace lock. Dropping them decouples the workspace torch version from the TPU stack. #7920 was filed to retire the remaining SkyRL custom image paths now that the image-free routes are live: the maintained path publishes immutable H100 and GB200 vLLM wheels with source provenance, and the frozen environment passed a 30-step dense FSDP gate on H100 and a Grug rollout-to-FSDP2 checkpoint/resume gate on GB200. Three campaign retrospective issues #6654 , #6655 , and #6656 plus the Iris launch workflow #6629 were closed as informational records of the campaigns they document.

 #6867 
 TPU vLLM stack leaves the workspace; GPU wheels pinned by SHA-256

 Epic title: [Epic] July Grug Inference tasks

 Summary: DoD: Support full size GrugMoE model on both TPUs and GPUs. Stretch: Inference is fast enough on GPUs.

 0/3 sub-issues closed

 The vLLM and TPU-inference forks no longer co-resolve in the root uv workspace. #8063 moved TPU serving to an isolated uvx environment pinned by SHA in marin.external_dependencies , matching how Evalchemy, Harbor, and MarinSkyRL are already pinned through config/update-external.py . Co-resolving the forks had held the workspace at torch==2.11.0 ; dropping them decouples the workspace torch version from the TPU stack. This closes #8022 , where the source pin did not pin the precompiled wheel. Last week's multinode vLLM parity work also landed: Romain Yon 's #7758 runs GrugMoE pipeline-parallel (PP) inference across Iris tasks through native vLLM, without Ray. The leader Iris task starts vLLM's API, scheduler, and local data-parallel (DP) and expert-parallel (EP) workers; each follower starts a bare MultiprocExecutor for its pipeline stage. The parity matrix covers PP1/TP1/DP8/EP8 on one 8xH100 node and PP2/TP1/DP8/EP8 across two gang-scheduled nodes, both scoring the same 64 GPU goldens, requiring exact same-rank recomputation, and logging cross-rank spread as a diagnostic rather than a hard assertion. TPU-side parity for the June 67B checkpoint is still in draft #7556 . Russell Power filed #7954 on reducing chat-template confusion between pre-training and post-training, and Mark Muchane proposed sharing broker session bring-up between the GPU serve path and the converter pool #8024 to remove roughly 40 lines of duplicated Iris lifecycle code.

Matt Wittmann was the largest single source, authoring the NVIDIA Collective Communications Library (NCCL) 2.30.7 bump #8038 and the expert-parallel sharding carry-over #7932 , and filing detailed root-cause analysis across dozens of comments on the silent collective wedge #7344 and the single-rank illegal-instruction failure #7956 . Tinuade Adeleke landed the shared Common Crawl Web ARChive (WARC) retrieval layer #7917 and hand-reviewed 15 extracted DOCX records across four languages. Gustavo Sandoval filed five safety-evaluation issues in a single day #7931 , running allenai/safety-eval on marin-8b-instruct, identifying misinformation as the largest gap versus Olmo 3, and demonstrating that refusal is removable in roughly ten fine-tuning steps. Two Discord threads carried work that GitHub did not. In #evals , boreas opened a first PR to marin-community/evalchemy adding chat-mode GSM8K under perturbation and was paired into a reciprocal review with another new contributor on the SciCode proposal #7658 . In #architecture , Mayank posted a linear-attention implementation benchmarking at ~29B tokens/day on a 1B model against 32B for softmax on 4x TPU v6e, dropping to 17B/day once causal convolution is applied; markhart0034 flagged the inference-time state cost that the training throughput number hides. In #questions , Ricardo Olmedo asked whether intermediate Snowball checkpoints at 70B, 220B, 660B, and 2T tokens could be released for joint pre-training and fine-tuning scaling-law research. Four people introduced themselves: a software engineer previously at Datadog who found Marin through inference lectures, Thom from Common Crawl offering to connect on crawling, standards, and datasets, a Yale statistics PhD student interested in open-source post-training, and one more looking to contribute. The Common Crawl arrival intersects directly with the focus-crawl PDF pipeline #8023 and the WARC layer that shipped this week. Jungwoo Park, first author of Monet which pushes fine-grained expert counts to 262,144 per layer, joined the server without posting an introduction. Reading shared in the server stayed close to active work: Gonzalo Benegas posted the MarinDNA blog write-up, and papers on verification as a scaling axis, capability shaping via token-level data filtering, and variance-controlled off-policy RL circulated across the RL and safety channels.

 Top 15 runs (by FLOPs) this week (completed, running, crashed)

 The week's largest compute expenditure remains the 67B-A2B 10T run , still running on 1,024 TPU v4 chips (803k chip-hours to date). It has processed 7.65T tokens and sits at 1.305 train loss and 0.669 eval bits per byte (BPB). Separately, a long-context cooldown of the same 67B architecture finished this week, extending context from 8k to 65,536 tokens at step 102k. It landed at 0.650 eval BPB (Paloma macro 0.725), closing out the intermediate cooldown tracked in #6811 . 
 On GB200s, Larry Dial ran a systematic learning-rate sweep for the August hero configuration #7856 . Ten of the top-15 runs this week are d2048 and d1536 LR-sweep cells at 300x and 600x over-training ratios, each on 16 GB200 chips. The sweep produced a power-law fit for optimal LR: lr = 34.3 tokens -0.346 hidden -0.345 batch 0.5 (R&sup2; = 0.978). The key finding is that optimal LR rises with token budget (roughly 1.0x at 30x over-training to 1.2 1.4x at 600x), and at the target d6144 / 15T scale the new law prescribes about 1.07x the current heuristic a modest correction. A companion iso-FLOP sweep #8003 confirmed the August hero architecture sits on top of the existing May compute-optimal baseline across three converged budgets (1e18 1e19 FLOPs), with a more token-heavy optimum (T* proportional to C 0.54 vs the prior 0.46). 
 Multi-rack GB200 training was dominated by the investigation into silent collective wedges at 8+ racks ( #7344 , 39 comments this week). Matt Wittmann ran a series of targeted reproductions including the crashed moe-hero-ep-8rack (360B-parameter MoE, 512 GB200 GPUs) and FSDP 12-rack diagnostic run (768 GPUs) and root-caused the hang to an NVIDIA Collective Communications Library (NCCL) 2.28.9 proxy-op slot leak on aarch64 (Grace). A weak compare-exchange in the proxy-op return path silently orphans freed slots until a rank's 2,048-slot partition is exhausted, at which point the rank deadlocks with no error or timeout. The fix is NCCL 2.30.7+, landing via PR #8038 . In the Fully Sharded Data Parallel (FSDP) vs Expert Parallel (EP) ablation ( #8046 ), EP with capacity factor 2.5 produced 35% worse Paloma macro loss than FSDP at matched throughput, though Larry Dial noted that swapping to FSDP dropless at eval time may close much of that gap.

... 453 def _resolve_receiver_alignment(receiver_alignment: int | None) -> int:
... 454     """Row alignment the receiver buffer's expert groups start on.
... 455 
... 456     ``None`` is the unaligned layout: groups are packed back to back and the cuDNN
... 457     weight-gradient wrapper copies both of its operands into an aligned buffer itself. Any other
... 458     value lays the groups out aligned at the source and deletes those copies, which is only
... 459     sound if the value is a multiple of what that kernel requires.
... 460     """
... 461     if receiver_alignment is None:
... 462         return 1
... 463     if receiver_alignment < 1:
... 464         raise ValueError(f"receiver_alignment must be positive, got {receiver_alignment}")
... 465     if receiver_alignment % RAGGED_CUDNN_RECEIVER_ALIGNMENT != 0:
... 466         raise ValueError(
... 467             f"receiver_alignment={receiver_alignment} must be a multiple of "
... 468             f"{RAGGED_CUDNN_RECEIVER_ALIGNMENT}, the cuDNN grouped weight-gradient group alignment"
... 469         )
... 470     return receiver_alignment

     4	"""Compute-scaling LR heuristic and the EP64 hero config builder.
     5	
     6	``MoeHeuristic`` is the Aug hero LR-sweep refit (issues #7856 / #8003, R^2=0.978): it sets compute-optimal MuonH /
     7	Adam learning rates, epsilon, and beta2 from the token budget and batch size. ``build_hero_configs``
     8	pairs it with the fixed hero model spec so a launcher gets both configs back from a single
     9	``(num_train_steps, batch_size)`` call, keeping the hero self-contained.
    10	
    11	The hero model is d6144 with 48 layers and 384 routed experts. Each expert has width 3,072, and
    12	the router selects eight experts per token. Expert parallelism moves tokens with the ragged
    13	all-to-all transport at a 1.15 receiver capacity factor.
    14	"""
    15	
    16	import math
    17	from dataclasses import dataclass
    18	
    19	from experiments.grug.moe_hero_ep.model import GrugModelConfig
    20	from experiments.grug.moe_hero_ep.optimizer import GrugMoeMuonHConfig
    21	
    22	
    23	@dataclass(frozen=True)
    24	class MoeHeuristic:
    25	    """Aug hero LR-sweep MuonH refit (issues #7856 / #8003, seq_len=8192, R^2=0.978).
    26	
    27	    adam_lr  = lr_coeff * tokens^lr_tokens_exp * hidden_dim^lr_dim_exp * sqrt(tokens_per_batch)
    28	    muonh_lr = muonh_ratio * adam_lr
    29	    epsilon  = epsilon_coeff * sqrt(tokens / tokens_per_batch)
    30	    beta2    = clip(beta2_base^(tokens_per_batch / beta2_reference_tpb), min_beta2, max_beta2)
    31	
    32	    LR exponents/coefficient are the per-cell paloma-optimal fit: muonh_lr =
    33	    34.35 * tokens^-0.346 * hidden^-0.345 * batch^0.5 at seq_len=8192, folded into the
    34	    sqrt(tokens_per_batch) form (lr_coeff = 34.35 / (muonh_ratio * sqrt(8192))). Prior
    35	    May-Recipe fit (#5951): lr_coeff=0.06602, lr_tokens_exp=-0.395, lr_dim_exp=-0.150.
    36	    """
    37	
    38	    lr_coeff: float = 0.087571
    39	    lr_tokens_exp: float = -0.3461
    40	    lr_dim_exp: float = -0.3448
    41	    muonh_ratio: float = 13 / 3
    42	    epsilon_coeff: float = 9.676e-18
    43	    beta1: float = 0.90
    44	    beta2_base: float = 0.999
    45	    beta2_reference_tpb: int = 131_072
    46	    min_lr_ratio: float = 0.05
    47	    lr_schedule: str = "linear"
    48	    max_learning_rate: float = 0.05
    49	    min_beta2: float = 0.95
    50	    max_beta2: float = 0.9999
    51	
    52	    def _adam_lr(self, tokens_per_batch: int, tokens: float, hidden_dim: int) -> float:
    53	        adam_lr = (
    54	            self.lr_coeff * (tokens**self.lr_tokens_exp) * (hidden_dim**self.lr_dim_exp) * math.sqrt(tokens_per_batch)
    55	        )
    56	        return min(self.max_learning_rate, adam_lr)
    57	
    58	    def _learning_rate(self, tokens_per_batch: int, tokens: float, hidden_dim: int) -> float:
    59	        return min(self.max_learning_rate, self.muonh_ratio * self._adam_lr(tokens_per_batch, tokens, hidden_dim))
    60	
    61	    def _epsilon(self, tokens_per_batch: int, tokens: float) -> float:
    62	        return self.epsilon_coeff * math.sqrt(tokens / tokens_per_batch)
    63	
    64	    def _beta2(self, tokens_per_batch: int) -> float:
    65	        exponent = tokens_per_batch / self.beta2_reference_tpb
    66	        return max(self.min_beta2, min(self.max_beta2, self.beta2_base**exponent))
    67	
    68	    def build_optimizer_config(
    69	        self, *, num_train_steps: int, batch_size: int, hidden_dim: int, seq_len: int
    70	    ) -> GrugMoeMuonHConfig:
    71	        """MuonH optimizer with LR / beta2 / epsilon scaled to this token budget (1pct-noclip schedule)."""
    72	        tokens_per_batch = batch_size * seq_len
    73	        tokens = float(num_train_steps * tokens_per_batch)
    74	        return GrugMoeMuonHConfig(
    75	            learning_rate=self._learning_rate(tokens_per_batch, tokens, hidden_dim),
    76	            adam_lr=self._adam_lr(tokens_per_batch, tokens, hidden_dim),
    77	            min_lr_ratio=self.min_lr_ratio,
    78	            lr_schedule=self.lr_schedule,
    79	            beta1=self.beta1,
    80	            beta2=self._beta2(tokens_per_batch),
    81	            epsilon=self._epsilon(tokens_per_batch, tokens),
    82	        )
    83	
    84	
    85	_HERO_HIDDEN = 6144
    86	HERO_MODEL = GrugModelConfig(
    87	    vocab_size=128_256,
    88	    hidden_dim=_HERO_HIDDEN,
    89	    intermediate_dim=_HERO_HIDDEN // 2,
    90	    shared_expert_intermediate_dim=_HERO_HIDDEN // 2,
    91	    num_shared_experts=2,
    92	    num_experts=384,
    93	    num_experts_per_token=8,
    94	    num_layers=48,
    95	    num_heads=48,
    96	    num_kv_heads=12,
    97	    local_kv_heads=12,
    98	    global_kv_heads=6,
    99	    head_dim=128,
   100	    max_seq_len=4096,
   101	    sliding_window=2048,
   102	    global_every=4,
   103	    capacity_factor=1.15,
   104	    initializer_std=0.5 / math.sqrt(_HERO_HIDDEN),
   105	    qk_mult=1.3,
   106	    sconv=True,
   107	    # The wide 128x64 forward tile gains 0.28 MFU at the hero's 24k-restore operating point
   108	    # (mfu24-ctrl-a5/b 23.06/23.05 vs mfu24-tile-a/b 23.32/23.37, same-night interleaved).
   109	    attention_implementation="gpu_fa4_cute_wide",
   110	    moe_implementation="ragged_all_to_all",
   111	    pooled_transport_capacity_factor=1.15,  # pooled-wave only
   112	    num_expert_waves=3,  # pooled-wave only
   113	    expert_chunks=1,
   114	    report_capacity_overflow=True,
   115	    rope_fused=True,
   116	    latent_dim=_HERO_HIDDEN // 2,
   117	)
   118	
   119	
   120	def build_hero_configs(*, num_train_steps: int, batch_size: int) -> tuple[GrugModelConfig, GrugMoeMuonHConfig]:
   121	    """The fixed EP64 hero model plus its compute-scaled MuonH optimizer."""
   122	    model = HERO_MODEL
   123	    optimizer = MoeHeuristic().build_optimizer_config(
   124	        num_train_steps=num_train_steps,
   125	        batch_size=batch_size,
   126	        hidden_dim=model.hidden_dim,
   127	        seq_len=model.max_seq_len,
   128	    )
   129	    return model, optimizer

    61	def with_transport_remat_mode(model: GrugModelConfig) -> GrugModelConfig:
    62	    """Give the ragged transport the layer-carry offload that its scheduling posture depends on.
    63	
    64	    Staging the carry on pinned host lowered the measured HBM peak by 36 GiB, which is what makes
    65	    the latency-hiding scheduler fit. The other transports are unmeasured with the offload, which
    66	    is the only reason they do not take it.
    67	
    68	    The scheduler reads the remat mode, so a launcher that skips this keeps the scheduling
    69	    posture it was measured under, exactly as it did before the mode existed.
    70	    """
    71	    if model.moe_implementation != RAGGED_MOE_IMPLEMENTATION:
    72	        return model
    73	    return dataclasses.replace(model, remat_mode="offload_carry")
    74

    70	HERO_EP_RUNTIME_ENV = {
    71	    "LD_PRELOAD": "libjemalloc.so.2",
    72	    "MALLOC_CONF": "background_thread:true,dirty_decay_ms:0,muzzy_decay_ms:0,narenas:2",
    73	    "JAX_ENABLE_PGLE": "false",
    74	    "XLA_PJRT_GPU_HOST_MEMORY_LIMIT_GB": "192",
    75	    "XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_ALLOCATOR": "cuda_async",
    76	    # `cuda_async` reads this fraction as the mempool release threshold, and PJRT sizes the
    77	    # collective pool at the remaining `(1 - fraction) x 184.3 GiB`. 0.75 sets a 138.2 GiB
    78	    # threshold and leaves ~46 GiB for collectives, above the ~28.5 GiB NCCL, cuBLAS, and the
    79	    # CUDA context hold outside the allocator. A higher fraction strands memory the step never
    80	    # uses, because the startup preallocation probe commits the whole threshold at once: 0.83
    81	    # pins 153.0 GiB in the pool and leaves under 3 GiB free on the device, so the arena
    82	    # allocation below has no room to remap into.
    83	    "XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_MEM_FRACTION": "0.75",
    84	}
    85	XLA_COLLECTIVE_OVERLAP_FLAG = "--xla_gpu_experimental_parallel_collective_overlap_limit"
    86	DEFAULT_COLLECTIVE_OVERLAP_LIMIT = 4
    87	DEFAULT_DROPLESS_MOE_IMPLEMENTATION: MoeImplementation = "sonic_cute"
    88	# Full inline norm watch failed with overlap 4. Overlap 1 completed the selected full-watch gate.
    89	INLINE_WATCH_COLLECTIVE_OVERLAP_LIMIT = 1
    90	# The ragged transport wants the opposite scheduling posture from the fixed and pooled ones. Its
    91	# dispatch and combine form one long dependent chain, so admitting several concurrent collectives
    92	# only contends for the SMs the transport itself needs.
    93	RAGGED_COLLECTIVE_OVERLAP_LIMIT = 1
    94	# The layer-carry offload, the latency-hiding scheduler, and an overlap limit above 1 corrupt
    95	# training together, and no pair of the three does: the reloaded residual races its consumer in
    96	# backward, so a restored run reports a first-step loss near 9.5 instead of its checkpoint's
    97	# (#8317). Overlap 4 gained 0.07 MFU, so the offload forces this value rather than defaulting it.
    98	OFFLOAD_CARRY_COLLECTIVE_OVERLAP_LIMIT = 1
    99	RAGGED_MOE_IMPLEMENTATION = "ragged_all_to_all"
   100	# TODO(https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/5675): Re-enable XLA GPU
   101	# command buffers after the CUDA graph failure is fixed.
   102	XLA_DISABLE_GPU_COMMAND_BUFFER_FLAG = "--xla_gpu_enable_command_buffer="
   103	_RAGGED_REQUIRED_XLA_FLAG_NAMES = frozenset(flag.partition("=")[0] for flag in RAGGED_REQUIRED_XLA_FLAGS)
   104	PJRT_DISTRIBUTION = "jax-cuda13-pjrt"
   105	_FP32_POLICY = jmp.get_policy("params=float32,compute=float32,output=float32")

   108	class WatchMode(StrEnum):
   109	    """Where a watched training step computes gradient and parameter statistics."""
   110	
   111	    INLINE = "inline"
   112	    DIAGNOSTIC = "diagnostic"
   113	
   114	
   115	class MasterParamMode(StrEnum):
   116	    """Where the authoritative fp32 weights live.
   117	
   118	    DEVICE keeps them as the device params themselves, with no separate master copy;
   119	    FP32_PINNED_HOST keeps a pinned-host fp32 master while the device params are its bf16 cast.
   120	    """
   121	
   122	    DEVICE = "device"
   123	    FP32_PINNED_HOST = "fp32_pinned_host"
   124	
   125	
   126	class TrainingDataMode(StrEnum):
   127	    """Source of training batches."""
   128	
   129	    MIXTURE = "mixture"
   130	    SYNTHETIC = "synthetic"
   131	
   132	
   133	class ResidentDonation(StrEnum):
   134	    """Donation policy for the device-resident expert momentum leaves (diagnostic).
   135	
   136	    DONATED donates the whole train state into the step, the original behavior. EXCLUDED passes
   137	    the resident momentum leaves as a separate, non-donated argument, so XLA can neither alias
   138	    them to an output nor reuse their buffers as scratch, and adds a per-step canary checksum of
   139	    each resident leaf (``debug/resident_ck_in`` / ``debug/resident_ck_out``). This discriminates
   140	    the k=1 NaN hypotheses: S1 (donation-enabled buffer reuse clobbers the leaf under the async
   141	    offload schedule) from S2 (a stray transport write lands in the leaf's address range
   142	    regardless of donation). EXCLUDED costs one extra device copy of each resident leaf per step
   143	    (the un-donated input and the fresh output coexist: +10.87 GiB transient per leaf at d6144
   144	    EP64, predicted peak ~134 GiB at k=1 -- near the 138.2 GiB threshold; watch for #8490
   145	    allocator churn).
   146	    """
   147	
   148	    DONATED = "donated"
   149	    EXCLUDED = "excluded"
   150	
   151	
   152	def restore_template_from(state):
   153	    """ShapeDtypeStructs carrying each leaf's concrete sharding, releasing the leaves.
   154	
   155	    `jax.eval_shape` drops the `pinned_host` memory kind that `initial_state` puts on
   156	    offloaded optimizer state, which is most of a hero checkpoint. Reading the sharding off a
   157	    built state keeps it.
   158	    """
   159	    template = jax.tree.map(
   160	        lambda leaf: (
   161	            jax.ShapeDtypeStruct(leaf.shape, leaf.dtype, sharding=leaf.sharding) if isinstance(leaf, jax.Array) else leaf
   162	        ),
   163	        state,
   164	    )
   165	    jax.tree.map(lambda leaf: leaf.delete() if isinstance(leaf, jax.Array) else None, state)
   166	    gc.collect()
   167	    return template
   168	
   169	
   170	def checkpoint_stores_master(candidate: str) -> bool:
   171	    """Whether checkpoint ``candidate``'s manifest lists fp32 master parameters.
   172	
   173	    A missing manifest raises ``FileNotFoundError``, which restore treats like any other
   174	    unreadable candidate.
   175	    """
   176	    manifest = read_manifest(candidate)
   177	    if manifest is None:
   178	        raise FileNotFoundError(f"{candidate} has no manifest.json, so its layout cannot be read")
   179	    markers = (MASTER_PARAMS_KEY, f"{LEGACY_STATE_KEY}/{MASTER_PARAMS_KEY}")
   180	    return any(path == marker or path.startswith(marker + "/") for path in manifest.array_paths for marker in markers)
   181	
   182	
   183	def template_for_candidate_layout(
   184	    state: "GrugTrainState", candidate: str, run_mode: MasterParamMode
   185	) -> "GrugTrainState":
   186	    """Pick the template restore reads checkpoint ``candidate`` with.
   187	
   188	    Restore reads only the leaves the template names and takes each dtype from storage, checking
   189	    neither against the checkpoint, so reading a master-bearing checkpoint with the run's own
   190	    master-less template would silently return the bf16 compute copy. When the layouts match the
   191	    template is ``state`` itself. A master-bearing checkpoint read by a master-less run migrates
   192	    in process: the run's device fp32 ``params`` template is presented under ``master_params``, so
   193	    the checkpoint's authoritative fp32 master loads directly into it and the bf16 copy goes
   194	    unread; ``take_master_as_params`` then moves it back, and the next save writes the new layout.
   195	    """
   196	    has_master = checkpoint_stores_master(candidate)
   197	    if has_master == (run_mode != MasterParamMode.DEVICE):
   198	        return state
   199	    if not has_master:
   200	        raise ValueError(
   201	            f"checkpoint {candidate} stores no master parameters, but this run trains with {run_mode}. "
   202	            "Synthesizing a master from stored weights is not a conversion this supports."
   203	        )
   204	    logger.info("Checkpoint %s stores a pinned-host fp32 master; restoring it as the parameters.", candidate)
   205	    return dataclasses.replace(state, params=None, master_params=state.params)
   206	
   207	
   208	def take_master_as_params(state: "GrugTrainState") -> "GrugTrainState":
   209	    """Move a master restored through ``template_for_candidate_layout`` into ``params``."""
   210	    if state.master_params is None:
   211	        return state
   212	    return dataclasses.replace(state, params=state.master_params, master_params=None)
   213	
   214	
   215	def _apply_hero_ep_runtime_defaults(
   216	    *,
   217	    inline_watch_enabled: bool,
   218	    moe_implementation: MoeImplementation | None,
   219	    remat_mode: RematMode,
   220	    processes_per_task: int = 1,
   221	) -> None:
   222	    env_defaults = dict(HERO_EP_RUNTIME_ENV)
   223	    if processes_per_task > 1:
   224	        # With one process per GPU, the per-process CUPTI sessions collide with each
   225	        # other and with CoreWeave's DCGM, so PGLE cannot profile and its recompile
   226	        # machinery only adds failure modes. Default it off; an explicit env wins.
   227	        env_defaults["JAX_ENABLE_PGLE"] = "false"
   228	    for name, value in env_defaults.items():
   229	        os.environ.setdefault(name, value)
   230	    xla_flags = os.environ.get("XLA_FLAGS", "").split()
   231	    ragged = moe_implementation == RAGGED_MOE_IMPLEMENTATION
   232	    if ragged:
   233	        overlap_limit = RAGGED_COLLECTIVE_OVERLAP_LIMIT
   234	    elif inline_watch_enabled:
   235	        overlap_limit = INLINE_WATCH_COLLECTIVE_OVERLAP_LIMIT
   236	    else:
   237	        overlap_limit = DEFAULT_COLLECTIVE_OVERLAP_LIMIT
   238	    # The scheduler's longer buffer live ranges fit on the ragged transport only once the layer
   239	    # carry leaves HBM. Without that offload its first-step NCCL allocations fail.
   240	    latency_hiding = not ragged or remat_mode == "offload_carry"
   241	    flag_defaults = (
   242	        f"{XLA_COLLECTIVE_OVERLAP_FLAG}={overlap_limit}",
   243	        f"--xla_gpu_enable_latency_hiding_scheduler={'true' if latency_hiding else 'false'}",
   244	        # The scheduler sizes the single `jit_train_step` temp arena against this percentage of
   245	        # its memory budget, roughly `133.6 GiB x percentage`. The pool holds 138.2 GiB and
   246	        # persistent state occupies 18.1 GiB of it, so an arena above 120.2 GiB cannot be served
   247	        # from pool free space and forces a fresh mapping against the ~17 GiB of physical memory
   248	        # outside the pool. The default 95 asks for 125.7 GiB and fails that way. 85 sizes the
   249	        # arena at 113.6 GiB, leaving enough slack for per-node variation in fragmentation. A
   250	        # lower percentage costs throughput, because a smaller arena makes `HloRematerialization`
   251	        # recompute more of the step.
   252	        "--xla_gpu_memory_limit_slop_factor=85",
   253	        XLA_DISABLE_GPU_COMMAND_BUFFER_FLAG,
   254	    )
   255	    explicit_names = {flag.partition("=")[0] for flag in xla_flags}
   256	    xla_flags.extend(flag for flag in flag_defaults if flag.partition("=")[0] not in explicit_names)
   257	    if remat_mode == "offload_carry":
   258	        # Not overridable, unlike the defaults above, including the scheduler flag it pairs with.
   259	        # Both flags can be inherited from another recipe, but only this one fails silently: a
   260	        # wrong overlap limit corrupts training, while an inherited scheduler setting either
   261	        # aborts in NCCL's first-step allocation and names itself, or runs the slower posture.
   262	        xla_flags = [f for f in xla_flags if f.partition("=")[0] != XLA_COLLECTIVE_OVERLAP_FLAG]
   263	        xla_flags.append(f"{XLA_COLLECTIVE_OVERLAP_FLAG}={OFFLOAD_CARRY_COLLECTIVE_OVERLAP_LIMIT}")
   264	    if ragged:
   265	        # Unlike the defaults above, these are not overridable. Selecting the host-launched
   266	        # one-shot kernel needs both flags cleared together plus a splits-per-peer count this
   267	        # branch no longer carries, so honoring a partial override would run a configuration
   268	        # nothing here measures. Drop any conflicting entry rather than relying on which
   269	        # occurrence XLA's parser keeps.
   270	        xla_flags = [f for f in xla_flags if f.partition("=")[0] not in _RAGGED_REQUIRED_XLA_FLAG_NAMES]
   271	        xla_flags.extend(RAGGED_REQUIRED_XLA_FLAGS)
   272	    os.environ["XLA_FLAGS"] = " ".join(xla_flags)
   273	
   274	
   275	def verify_ragged_pjrt() -> None:
   276	    """Raise unless this process runs Marin's patched GPU PJRT plugin."""
   277	    try:
   278	        installed = importlib.metadata.version(PJRT_DISTRIBUTION)
   279	    except importlib.metadata.PackageNotFoundError as missing:
   280	        raise RuntimeError(
   281	            f"{PJRT_DISTRIBUTION} is not installed, so this process has no GPU PJRT plugin at all."
   282	        ) from missing
   283	    expected_prefix = f"{jax.__version__}+marin."
   284	    if not installed.startswith(expected_prefix):
   285	        raise RuntimeError(
   286	            f"{RAGGED_MOE_IMPLEMENTATION} needs Marin's patched {PJRT_DISTRIBUTION} "
   287	            f"({expected_prefix}*), found {installed}. The patched wheel is aarch64-only and the "
   288	            "expert MLP is SM100-specialized; run the ragged transport on GB200."
   289	        )
   290	    # The prefix check accepts any marin build, so wheel-substitution arms need the exact
   291	    # version in the run-phase log to prove which plugin this process actually carries.
   292	    logger.info("%s version at runtime: %s", PJRT_DISTRIBUTION, installed)

   294	
   295	@dataclass(frozen=True)
   296	class GrugTrainerConfig:
   297	    """Runtime knobs for grug training."""
   298	
   299	    trainer: TrainerConfig = field(default_factory=lambda: TrainerConfig(use_explicit_mesh_axes=True))
   300	    data_seed: int | None = None
   301	    log_every: int = 1
   302	    ema_beta: float | None = None  # EMA coefficient for eval/checkpoint model; None disables EMA.
   303	    z_loss_weight: float = 1e-4  # Weight on final-logit logsumexp z-loss stabilization term.
   304	    # Keep disabled except on model sizes where Grace-Blackwell host offload has been measured.
   305	    # The d6144 EP64 runs used it; d5120 required a 135 GiB pinned-host arena and regressed.
   306	    offload_opt_state: bool = False
   307	    # With offload_opt_state, keep the first N 4D expert momentum shards on device instead of
   308	    # pinned host. Each costs its own HBM (10.87 GiB at d6144 EP64) and saves its two per-step
   309	    # host round-trip copies in the optimizer tail. 0 offloads everything, as before.
   310	    # See `_opt_state_offload_mask` for which leaves "first N" names and why that is stable.
   311	    opt_state_resident_expert_leaves: int = 0
   312	    # Diagnostic donation policy for the resident leaves; only meaningful with
   313	    # opt_state_resident_expert_leaves > 0. DONATED is bit-identical to the previous behavior.
   314	    # See `ResidentDonation` for what EXCLUDED changes and its +10.87 GiB/leaf transient cost.
   315	    opt_state_resident_donation: ResidentDonation = ResidentDonation.DONATED
   316	    master_param_mode: MasterParamMode = MasterParamMode.DEVICE
   317	    training_data_mode: TrainingDataMode = TrainingDataMode.MIXTURE
   318	    # Inline watch computes statistics on every step and uses the watch interval only for logging.
   319	    # This keeps one training executable resident. A diagnostic watch repeats forward and backward
   320	    # in a separate executable, which costs compute but shortens gradient liveness.
   321	    watch_mode: WatchMode = WatchMode.INLINE
   322	    # A short throughput gate leaves this off. A compute-optimal run needs it: the loop already
   323	    # restores from the latest committed checkpoint, so without a writer an interrupted run
   324	    # restarts at step 0.
   325	    save_checkpoints: bool = False
   326	
   327	    # Grug builds its own compact (replica_dcn, data, expert, model) mesh instead of using
   328	    # the Trainer's logical axis mapping; `data` absorbs whatever these two leave free.
   329	    # Defaults reproduce the historical layout: no expert parallelism and full replication
   330	    # across slices (replica_axis_size=None -> jax.process_count()), i.e. parameters
   331	    # replicated per slice and sharded only over the intra-slice `data` axis. For a model
   332	    # too large to replicate within one slice, set replica_axis_size=1 (FSDP across every
   333	    # slice) and expert_axis_size>1 (expert parallelism over the intra-slice devices).
   334	    expert_axis_size: int = 1
   335	    replica_axis_size: int | None = None
   336	    sharding_dump_path: str | None = None
   337	
   338	
   339	@dataclass(frozen=True)
   340	class GrugEvalConfig:
   341	    """Perplexity eval settings for grug training."""
   342	
   343	    eval_batch_size: int = 512
   344	    steps_per_eval: int | None = 1000
   345	    max_eval_batches: int | None = None
   346	    prefix: str = "eval"
   347	    eval_current: bool = True
   348	    eval_ema: bool = True
   349	    compute_bpb: bool = True
   350	    # For expert-parallel runs, also evaluate under the dropless local backend on an
   351	    # expert-collapsed mesh, logging a separate `eval_dropless` macro loss alongside the
   352	    # as-trained (with-drop) eval. No-op when the mesh has no expert parallelism.
   353	    dropless_eval: bool = False
   354	    # Local MoE kernel used after collapsing the expert axis. ``sonic`` is the Hopper Triton path;
   355	    # ``sonic_cute`` is the Blackwell QuACK/CUTLASS path.
   356	    dropless_eval_moe_implementation: MoeImplementation = DEFAULT_DROPLESS_MOE_IMPLEMENTATION
   357	    # Run the evals once after the first optimization step, for a baseline at the start of the loss
   358	    # curve. The periodic cadence first fires at `steps_per_eval`, thus it leaves that start bare.
   359	    eval_at_first_step: bool = False
   360	
   361	
   362	@dataclass(frozen=True)
   363	class GrugRunConfig:
   364	    """Top-level config for grug training."""

     4	"""Compute-scaling LR heuristic and the EP64 hero config builder.
     5	
     6	``MoeHeuristic`` is the Aug hero LR-sweep refit (issues #7856 / #8003, R^2=0.978): it sets compute-optimal MuonH /
     7	Adam learning rates, epsilon, and beta2 from the token budget and batch size. ``build_hero_configs``
     8	pairs it with the fixed hero model spec so a launcher gets both configs back from a single
     9	``(num_train_steps, batch_size)`` call, keeping the hero self-contained.
    10	
    11	The hero model is d6144 with 48 layers and 384 routed experts. Each expert has width 3,072, and
    12	the router selects eight experts per token. Expert parallelism moves tokens with the ragged
    13	all-to-all transport at a 1.15 receiver capacity factor.
    14	"""
    15	
    16	import math
    17	from dataclasses import dataclass
    18	
    19	from experiments.grug.moe_hero_ep.model import GrugModelConfig
    20	from experiments.grug.moe_hero_ep.optimizer import GrugMoeMuonHConfig
    21	
    22	
    23	@dataclass(frozen=True)
    24	class MoeHeuristic:
    25	    """Aug hero LR-sweep MuonH refit (issues #7856 / #8003, seq_len=8192, R^2=0.978).
    26	
    27	    adam_lr  = lr_coeff * tokens^lr_tokens_exp * hidden_dim^lr_dim_exp * sqrt(tokens_per_batch)
    28	    muonh_lr = muonh_ratio * adam_lr
    29	    epsilon  = epsilon_coeff * sqrt(tokens / tokens_per_batch)
    30	    beta2    = clip(beta2_base^(tokens_per_batch / beta2_reference_tpb), min_beta2, max_beta2)
    31	
    32	    LR exponents/coefficient are the per-cell paloma-optimal fit: muonh_lr =
    33	    34.35 * tokens^-0.346 * hidden^-0.345 * batch^0.5 at seq_len=8192, folded into the
    34	    sqrt(tokens_per_batch) form (lr_coeff = 34.35 / (muonh_ratio * sqrt(8192))). Prior
    35	    May-Recipe fit (#5951): lr_coeff=0.06602, lr_tokens_exp=-0.395, lr_dim_exp=-0.150.
    36	    """
    37	
    38	    lr_coeff: float = 0.087571
    39	    lr_tokens_exp: float = -0.3461
    40	    lr_dim_exp: float = -0.3448
    41	    muonh_ratio: float = 13 / 3
    42	    epsilon_coeff: float = 9.676e-18
    43	    beta1: float = 0.90
    44	    beta2_base: float = 0.999
    45	    beta2_reference_tpb: int = 131_072
    46	    min_lr_ratio: float = 0.05
    47	    lr_schedule: str = "linear"
    48	    max_learning_rate: float = 0.05
    49	    min_beta2: float = 0.95
    50	    max_beta2: float = 0.9999
    51	
    52	    def _adam_lr(self, tokens_per_batch: int, tokens: float, hidden_dim: int) -> float:
    53	        adam_lr = (
    54	            self.lr_coeff * (tokens**self.lr_tokens_exp) * (hidden_dim**self.lr_dim_exp) * math.sqrt(tokens_per_batch)
    55	        )
    56	        return min(self.max_learning_rate, adam_lr)
    57	
    58	    def _learning_rate(self, tokens_per_batch: int, tokens: float, hidden_dim: int) -> float:
    59	        return min(self.max_learning_rate, self.muonh_ratio * self._adam_lr(tokens_per_batch, tokens, hidden_dim))
    60	
    61	    def _epsilon(self, tokens_per_batch: int, tokens: float) -> float:
    62	        return self.epsilon_coeff * math.sqrt(tokens / tokens_per_batch)
    63	
    64	    def _beta2(self, tokens_per_batch: int) -> float:
    65	        exponent = tokens_per_batch / self.beta2_reference_tpb
    66	        return max(self.min_beta2, min(self.max_beta2, self.beta2_base**exponent))
    67	
    68	    def build_optimizer_config(
    69	        self, *, num_train_steps: int, batch_size: int, hidden_dim: int, seq_len: int
    70	    ) -> GrugMoeMuonHConfig:
    71	        """MuonH optimizer with LR / beta2 / epsilon scaled to this token budget (1pct-noclip schedule)."""
    72	        tokens_per_batch = batch_size * seq_len
    73	        tokens = float(num_train_steps * tokens_per_batch)
    74	        return GrugMoeMuonHConfig(
    75	            learning_rate=self._learning_rate(tokens_per_batch, tokens, hidden_dim),
    76	            adam_lr=self._adam_lr(tokens_per_batch, tokens, hidden_dim),
    77	            min_lr_ratio=self.min_lr_ratio,
    78	            lr_schedule=self.lr_schedule,
    79	            beta1=self.beta1,
    80	            beta2=self._beta2(tokens_per_batch),
    81	            epsilon=self._epsilon(tokens_per_batch, tokens),
    82	        )
    83	
    84	
    85	_HERO_HIDDEN = 6144
    86	HERO_MODEL = GrugModelConfig(
    87	    vocab_size=128_256,
    88	    hidden_dim=_HERO_HIDDEN,
    89	    intermediate_dim=_HERO_HIDDEN // 2,
    90	    shared_expert_intermediate_dim=_HERO_HIDDEN // 2,
    91	    num_shared_experts=2,
    92	    num_experts=384,
    93	    num_experts_per_token=8,
    94	    num_layers=48,
    95	    num_heads=48,
    96	    num_kv_heads=12,
    97	    local_kv_heads=12,
    98	    global_kv_heads=6,
    99	    head_dim=128,
   100	    max_seq_len=4096,
   101	    sliding_window=2048,
   102	    global_every=4,
   103	    capacity_factor=1.15,
   104	    initializer_std=0.5 / math.sqrt(_HERO_HIDDEN),
   105	    qk_mult=1.3,
   106	    sconv=True,
   107	    # The wide 128x64 forward tile gains 0.28 MFU at the hero's 24k-restore operating point
   108	    # (mfu24-ctrl-a5/b 23.06/23.05 vs mfu24-tile-a/b 23.32/23.37, same-night interleaved).
   109	    attention_implementation="gpu_fa4_cute_wide",
   110	    moe_implementation="ragged_all_to_all",
   111	    pooled_transport_capacity_factor=1.15,  # pooled-wave only
   112	    num_expert_waves=3,  # pooled-wave only
   113	    expert_chunks=1,
   114	    report_capacity_overflow=True,
   115	    rope_fused=True,
   116	    latent_dim=_HERO_HIDDEN // 2,
   117	)
   118	
   119	
   120	def build_hero_configs(*, num_train_steps: int, batch_size: int) -> tuple[GrugModelConfig, GrugMoeMuonHConfig]:
   121	    """The fixed EP64 hero model plus its compute-scaled MuonH optimizer."""
   122	    model = HERO_MODEL
   123	    optimizer = MoeHeuristic().build_optimizer_config(
   124	        num_train_steps=num_train_steps,
   125	        batch_size=batch_size,
   126	        hidden_dim=model.hidden_dim,
   127	        seq_len=model.max_seq_len,
   128	    )
   129	    return model, optimizer

    61	def with_transport_remat_mode(model: GrugModelConfig) -> GrugModelConfig:
    62	    """Give the ragged transport the layer-carry offload that its scheduling posture depends on.
    63	
    64	    Staging the carry on pinned host lowered the measured HBM peak by 36 GiB, which is what makes
    65	    the latency-hiding scheduler fit. The other transports are unmeasured with the offload, which
    66	    is the only reason they do not take it.
    67	
    68	    The scheduler reads the remat mode, so a launcher that skips this keeps the scheduling
    69	    posture it was measured under, exactly as it did before the mode existed.
    70	    """
    71	    if model.moe_implementation != RAGGED_MOE_IMPLEMENTATION:
    72	        return model
    73	    return dataclasses.replace(model, remat_mode="offload_carry")

     4	"""Ragged all-to-all expert-parallel Grug MoE backend.
     5	
     6	Axis names used in the shape annotations:
     7	
     8	    Tlocal  tokens on this shard
     9	    K       routed experts per token
    10	    TK      routed assignments on this shard, Tlocal * K
    11	    H       hidden size
    12	    I       expert intermediate size
    13	    I2      gate and up projections fused, 2 * I
    14	    E       experts in the model
    15	    Elocal  experts held by this shard
    16	    Echunk  experts in one sequential chunk, Elocal / chunks
    17	    C       rows in one chunk's receiver buffer: the per-chunk capacity, plus the group-alignment
    18	            slack when the receiver layout is aligned
    19	    S       shards on the expert axis
    20	"""
    21

    23	import logging
    24	import math
    25	from collections.abc import Callable
    26	from typing import Protocol

    34	from levanter.grug._moe.common import CapacityOverflow, _interleave_gate_up
    35	from levanter.grug._moe.cudnn_wgrad_cute import _GROUP_ALIGNMENT
    36	from levanter.grug._moe.sonic import sonic_gather_sum, sonic_gather_sum_available
    37	from levanter.grug._moe.ep_common import (
    38	    _align_up_rows,

    47	# QuACK's grouped GEMMs are written for SM100 and ship only with the CUDA 13 GPU extra.
    48	_SM100_COMPUTE_CAPABILITY = 10.0
    49	
    50	# Sequential local-expert chunks per MoE layer when a caller does not name one; capacity splits
    51	# evenly across chunks. Falls back to a single chunk when the local expert count is not divisible.
    52	RAGGED_DEFAULT_EXPERT_CHUNKS = 2
    53	
    54	# Receiver-buffer row alignment that lets the cuDNN grouped weight-gradient kernel read the
    55	# transport's buffer directly. Its wrapper otherwise copies both operands into this layout on
    56	# every chunk of every layer, which is the whole cost the alignment removes.
    57	RAGGED_CUDNN_RECEIVER_ALIGNMENT = _GROUP_ALIGNMENT
    58	
    59	# Named dispatch products a remat policy can keep for the backward instead of recomputing.
    60	# Both are local (pre-collective) values: saving them deletes the recompute of the expert
    61	# argsort and the bincount without pinning any transport buffer. Sizes at the hero shape
    62	# (65,536 tokens x top-8 per device): sorted_indices s32[TK] = 2.1 MB/layer, group_sizes
    63	# s32[E] = 1.5 KB/layer.
    64	RAGGED_SORTED_INDICES_REMAT_NAME = "grug_moe_ragged_sorted_indices"
    65	RAGGED_GROUP_SIZES_REMAT_NAME = "grug_moe_ragged_group_sizes"
    66	RAGGED_DISPATCH_REMAT_SAVE_NAMES = (
    67	    RAGGED_SORTED_INDICES_REMAT_NAME,
    68	    RAGGED_GROUP_SIZES_REMAT_NAME,
    69	)
    70	
    71	# Selects the device-initiated ragged all-to-all kernel. The second entry is scoped to that op, so
    72	# every other collective keeps NCCL's host-launched kernels.
    73	RAGGED_REQUIRED_XLA_FLAGS = (
    74	    "--xla_gpu_experimental_ragged_all_to_all_use_device_kernel=true",
    75	    "--xla_enable_nccl_symmetric_buffers_for_collectives=raggedalltoall",
