    78	
    79	class _ExpertMlp(Protocol):
    80	    """Runs the expert MLP over a receiver buffer laid out expert-major.
    81	
    82	    Implementations take both views of the buffer's group sizes: the physical sizes, which charge
    83	    trailing padding to the last expert, and the active sizes, which count only the rows each
    84	    group occupies. Which one a kernel reads depends on whether it covers the whole buffer or
    85	    works from segment boundaries, so both are always passed and a kernel discards the one it
    86	    does not use.
    87	
    88	    Under an aligned receiver layout the active sizes are the aligned group extents, so a group
    89	    covers its arrivals followed by that layout's unwritten (zero) slack. Every kernel here is a
    90	    grouped GEMM over rows, so those rows contribute zero and produce zero.
    91	    """
    92	
    93	    def __call__(
    94	        self,
    95	        x_dispatch: Float[Array, "C H"],
    96	        moe_w13_local: Float[Array, "Echunk H I2"],
    97	        moe_w2_local: Float[Array, "Echunk I H"],
    98	        physical_group_sizes: Int[Array, "Echunk"],
    99	        active_group_sizes: Int[Array, "Echunk"],
   100	        activation_fn: Callable[[jax.Array], jax.Array],
   101	    ) -> Float[Array, "C H"]: ...
   102	
   103	
   104	def _ragged_dot_expert_mlp(
   105	    x_dispatch: Float[Array, "C H"],
   106	    moe_w13_local: Float[Array, "Echunk H I2"],
   107	    moe_w2_local: Float[Array, "Echunk I H"],
   108	    physical_group_sizes: Int[Array, "Echunk"],
   109	    active_group_sizes: Int[Array, "Echunk"],
   110	    activation_fn: Callable[[jax.Array], jax.Array],
   111	) -> Float[Array, "C H"]:
   112	    """Portable expert MLP over XLA's `ragged_dot`, which covers the whole receiver buffer."""
   113	    del active_group_sizes
   114	    w13_out = ragged_dot(x_dispatch, moe_w13_local, physical_group_sizes)
   115	    moe_dim = moe_w2_local.shape[1]
   116	    gate, up = jnp.split(w13_out, [moe_dim], axis=-1)
   117	    return ragged_dot(activation_fn(gate) * up, moe_w2_local, physical_group_sizes)
   118	
   119	
   120	def _cute_expert_mlp(
   121	    x_dispatch: Float[Array, "C H"],
   122	    moe_w13_local: Float[Array, "Echunk H I2"],
   123	    moe_w2_local: Float[Array, "Echunk I H"],
   124	    physical_group_sizes: Int[Array, "Echunk"],
   125	    active_group_sizes: Int[Array, "Echunk"],
   126	    activation_fn: Callable[[jax.Array], jax.Array],
   127	) -> Float[Array, "C H"]:
   128	    """Expert MLP on QuACK's SM100 grouped GEMMs plus cuDNN grouped weight gradients.
   129	
   130	    The grouped kernels are driven by segment boundaries, so they take the active sizes and
   131	    mask the receiver buffer's trailing padding rather than charging it to the last expert.
   132	    """
   133	    del activation_fn, physical_group_sizes
   134	
   135	    # QuACK, cuDNN Frontend, and CUTLASS DSL are installed only with the CUDA 13 GPU extra.
   136	    from levanter.grug._moe.sonic_cute import _expert_mlp_cudnn  # noqa: PLC0415
   137	
   138	    return _run_cute_expert_mlp(_expert_mlp_cudnn, x_dispatch, moe_w13_local, moe_w2_local, active_group_sizes)
   139	
   140	
   141	def _cute_expert_mlp_prealigned(
   142	    x_dispatch: Float[Array, "C H"],
   143	    moe_w13_local: Float[Array, "Echunk H I2"],
   144	    moe_w2_local: Float[Array, "Echunk I H"],
   145	    physical_group_sizes: Int[Array, "Echunk"],
   146	    active_group_sizes: Int[Array, "Echunk"],
   147	    activation_fn: Callable[[jax.Array], jax.Array],
   148	) -> Float[Array, "C H"]:
   149	    """`_cute_expert_mlp` for a receiver buffer already in the cuDNN kernel's aligned layout.
   150	
   151	    ``active_group_sizes`` are the aligned group extents here, so each group already starts on
   152	    an aligned row and the rows inside a group past its arrivals are the buffer's zeros. The
   153	    weight gradients therefore go to the pre-aligned cuDNN entry point, which is the same kernel
   154	    call on the same bytes with the alignment copy of both operands deleted.
   155	    """
   156	    del activation_fn, physical_group_sizes
   157	
   158	    from levanter.grug._moe.sonic_cute import _expert_mlp_cudnn_prealigned  # noqa: PLC0415
   159	
   160	    return _run_cute_expert_mlp(
   161	        _expert_mlp_cudnn_prealigned, x_dispatch, moe_w13_local, moe_w2_local, active_group_sizes
   162	    )
   163	
   164	
   165	def _run_cute_expert_mlp(
   166	    expert_mlp_cudnn,
   167	    x_dispatch: Float[Array, "C H"],
   168	    moe_w13_local: Float[Array, "Echunk H I2"],
   169	    moe_w2_local: Float[Array, "Echunk I H"],
   170	    active_group_sizes: Int[Array, "Echunk"],
   171	) -> Float[Array, "C H"]:
   172	    """Interleave the gate/up weights and call one of `sonic_cute`'s expert-MLP primitives."""
   173	    moe_dim = moe_w2_local.shape[1]
   174	    w13_interleaved = _interleave_gate_up(moe_w13_local, moe_dim)
   175	    cumulative_group_sizes = jnp.concatenate(
   176	        [jnp.zeros((1,), jnp.int32), jnp.cumsum(active_group_sizes).astype(jnp.int32)]
   177	    )
   178	    return expert_mlp_cudnn(x_dispatch, w13_interleaved, moe_w2_local, active_group_sizes, cumulative_group_sizes)
   179	
   180	
   181	@functools.cache
   182	def _quack_grouped_gemm_available() -> bool:
   183	    if jax.default_backend() != "gpu":
   184	        return False
   185	    if float(jax.devices("gpu")[0].compute_capability) < _SM100_COMPUTE_CAPABILITY:
   186	        return False
   187	    try:
   188	        import levanter.grug._moe.sonic_cute  # noqa: F401,PLC0415
   189	        from levanter.grug._moe.cudnn_wgrad_cute import _cudnn_modules  # noqa: PLC0415
   190	
   191	        _ = _cudnn_modules()  # check if compatible cudnn is available
   192	    except (ImportError, AttributeError) as exc:
   193	        logger.warning(
   194	            "SM100 GPU present but the QuACK/cuDNN grouped-GEMM kernels did not import (%s). "
   195	            "The ragged expert MLP falls back to ragged_dot, which computes the same function "
   196	            "more slowly. Install levanter's `gpu` extra to use them.",
   197	            exc,
   198	        )
   199	        return False
   200	    return True
   201	
   202	
   203	def _select_expert_mlp(activation_fn: Callable[[jax.Array], jax.Array], *, receiver_alignment: int = 1) -> _ExpertMlp:
   204	    """Pick the fastest expert-MLP kernel this process can actually run.
   205	
   206	    QuACK's kernel fuses SwiGLU, so it only applies to SiLU. Everything else -- another
   207	    activation, a non-SM100 GPU, a TPU or CPU, or a build without the GPU extra -- runs the
   208	    portable `ragged_dot` path, which computes the same function.
   209	
   210	    ``receiver_alignment`` above one says the transport has already laid the receiver buffer out
   211	    on the cuDNN weight-gradient kernel's group alignment, which lets the cute path skip that
   212	    kernel's operand pre-pass. `ragged_dot` reads group sizes off the buffer either way.
   213	    """
   214	    if activation_fn is jax.nn.silu and _quack_grouped_gemm_available():
   215	        return _cute_expert_mlp_prealigned if receiver_alignment > 1 else _cute_expert_mlp
   216	    return _ragged_dot_expert_mlp
   217	
   218	
   219	def _unpermute_from_global_expert(
   220	    intermediate: Float[Array, "TK H"],
   221	    sorted_indices: Int[Array, "TK"],
   222	    combine_weights_local: Float[Array, "Tlocal K"],
   223	    *,
   224	    tokens_per_shard: int,
   225	    topk: int,
   226	) -> Float[Array, "Tlocal H"]:
   227	    """Weight each token's expert outputs by its routing weights and sum them."""
   228	    positions = jnp.argsort(sorted_indices)
   229	    if sonic_gather_sum_available():
   230	        # One kernel for the gather and the sum, materializing neither the unpermuted
   231	        # ``[TK, H]`` buffer nor the ``[T, K, H]`` view -- at top-8 that view is eight times
   232	        # the output. It accumulates in fp32 like the einsum below and keeps the routing
   233	        # weight in fp32 through the multiply, where the einsum has to cast it down to avoid
   234	        # promoting the larger operand, so the two agree to a single rounding.
   235	        return sonic_gather_sum(intermediate, positions.reshape(tokens_per_shard, topk), combine_weights_local)
   236	    unsorted = _sort_activations(intermediate, positions)
   237	    reshaped = unsorted.reshape(tokens_per_shard, topk, -1)
   238	    return jnp.einsum(
   239	        "tkd,tk->td", reshaped, combine_weights_local.astype(reshaped.dtype), preferred_element_type=jnp.float32
   240	    )
   241	
   242	
   243	@functools.partial(jax.custom_vjp, nondiff_argnums=(2,))
   244	def _gather_dispatch_rows(
   245	    x_local: Float[Array, "Tlocal H"], sorted_indices: Int[Array, "TK"], topk: int
   246	) -> Float[Array, "TK H"]:
   247	    """Build the expert-sorted dispatch buffer with one gather.
   248	
   249	    Equivalent to ``jnp.repeat(x_local, topk, axis=0)[sorted_indices]`` without
   250	    materializing the repeated buffer or running a data-sized permute. The backward pass
   251	    is the transpose: each token sums the cotangent rows of its ``topk`` sorted slots.
   252	    """
   253	    return x_local[sorted_indices // topk]
   254	
   255	
   256	def _gather_dispatch_rows_fwd(
   257	    x_local: Float[Array, "Tlocal H"], sorted_indices: Int[Array, "TK"], topk: int
   258	) -> tuple[Float[Array, "TK H"], Int[Array, "TK"]]:
   259	    return _gather_dispatch_rows(x_local, sorted_indices, topk), sorted_indices
   260	
   261	
   262	def _gather_dispatch_rows_bwd(
   263	    topk: int, sorted_indices: Int[Array, "TK"], cotangent: Float[Array, "TK H"]
   264	) -> tuple[Float[Array, "Tlocal H"], None]:
   265	    tokens_per_shard = sorted_indices.shape[0] // topk
   266	    positions = jnp.argsort(sorted_indices).reshape(tokens_per_shard, topk)
   267	    if sonic_gather_sum_available():
   268	        ones = jnp.ones((tokens_per_shard, topk), dtype=jnp.float32)
   269	        grad_x = sonic_gather_sum(cotangent, positions, ones)
   270	    else:
   271	        grad_x = jnp.sum(cotangent[positions], axis=1, dtype=jnp.float32)
   272	    return grad_x.astype(cotangent.dtype), None
   273	
   274	
   275	_gather_dispatch_rows.defvjp(_gather_dispatch_rows_fwd, _gather_dispatch_rows_bwd)
   276	
   277	
   278	def _loop_local_zeros(
   279	    rows: int, hidden_dim: int, dtype, tie: Int[Array, "..."], site: int = 0
   280	) -> Float[Array, "rows H"]:
   281	    """Zero buffer for an in-place ``ragged_all_to_all`` output slot, built so XLA never copies it.
   282	
   283	    ``ragged_all_to_all`` writes its result in place into the output-init operand. A literal
   284	    ``jnp.zeros`` init is a trace-time constant: it gets hoisted out of the layer scan (and
   285	    identical inits CSE together), so CopyInsertion must mint a fresh multi-GB device copy of
   286	    the pristine zeros into the a2a's output slot on every scan iteration. Deriving the zeros
   287	    from ``tie`` -- a per-site, per-iteration traced value -- keeps each init inside the loop
   288	    body and distinct from every other init, so it lowers to one write-only fill kernel whose
   289	    buffer the a2a updates directly.
   290	
   291	    ``tie`` must be a non-negative integer array (group or transfer sizes): with ``site >= 0``,
   292	    ``min(tie[0], -site) + site`` is exactly zero at runtime but not foldable at compile time.
   293	
   294	    ``site`` must be distinct per call site. Two sites can hold the SAME tie tensor without it
   295	    being obvious (dispatch send_sizes and return recv_sizes are one tensor in ep_common), and
   296	    same-shape same-tie fills CSE into one value with two destructive in-place a2a consumers --
   297	    which makes CopyInsertion mint back the multi-GB copy this helper exists to prevent.
   298	    """
   299	    zero = (jnp.minimum(tie.reshape(-1)[0], -site) + site).astype(dtype)
   300	    return jax.lax.broadcast(zero, (rows, hidden_dim))
   301	
   302	
   303	@functools.partial(jax.custom_vjp, nondiff_argnums=(0, 1))
   304	def _dispatch_ragged_a2a(
   305	    capacity: int,
   306	    source_rows: int,
   307	    chunk_source: Float[Array, "TK H"],
   308	    input_offsets: Int[Array, "U"],
   309	    send_sizes: Int[Array, "U"],
   310	    output_offsets: Int[Array, "U"],
   311	    recv_sizes: Int[Array, "U"],
   312	) -> Float[Array, "C H"]:
   313	    """Dispatch-direction ``ragged_all_to_all`` into a freshly zeroed receiver buffer.
   314	
   315	    Owning the output-init here (instead of taking a caller-built ``jnp.zeros``) lets both the
   316	    primal and the transposed direction build their inits with `_loop_local_zeros`. jax's
   317	    built-in transpose rule inits the swapped a2a with plain zeros, which XLA hoists out of
   318	    the layer loop and re-copies every iteration; the custom vjp below is that same rule with
   319	    the init construction replaced. Zeros stay load-bearing: receiver rows no peer writes must
   320	    read 0 downstream, and dropped source rows must read a 0 cotangent in the backward.
   321	    """
   322	    del source_rows
   323	    output_init = _loop_local_zeros(capacity, chunk_source.shape[1], chunk_source.dtype, send_sizes, site=1)
   324	    return jax.lax.ragged_all_to_all(
   325	        chunk_source, output_init, input_offsets, send_sizes, output_offsets, recv_sizes, axis_name="expert"
   326	    )
   327	
   328	
   329	def _dispatch_ragged_a2a_fwd(
   330	    capacity: int,
   331	    source_rows: int,
   332	    chunk_source: Float[Array, "TK H"],
   333	    input_offsets: Int[Array, "U"],
   334	    send_sizes: Int[Array, "U"],
   335	    output_offsets: Int[Array, "U"],
   336	    recv_sizes: Int[Array, "U"],
   337	) -> tuple[Float[Array, "C H"], tuple[jax.Array, jax.Array, jax.Array, jax.Array]]:
   338	    result = _dispatch_ragged_a2a(
   339	        capacity, source_rows, chunk_source, input_offsets, send_sizes, output_offsets, recv_sizes
   340	    )
   341	    return result, (input_offsets, send_sizes, output_offsets, recv_sizes)
   342	
   343	
   344	def _dispatch_ragged_a2a_bwd(
   345	    capacity: int,
   346	    source_rows: int,
   347	    residuals: tuple[jax.Array, jax.Array, jax.Array, jax.Array],
   348	    cotangent: Float[Array, "C H"],
   349	) -> tuple[Float[Array, "TK H"], None, None, None, None]:
   350	    del capacity
   351	    input_offsets, send_sizes, output_offsets, recv_sizes = residuals
   352	    # The transpose of a ragged all-to-all is the reverse ragged all-to-all: swap the send and
   353	    # recv roles and exchange the offset vectors across shards, exactly as jax's transpose rule
   354	    # does. Source rows that were clipped receive no cotangent and keep the init's zeros.
   355	    output_offsets_x = jax.lax.all_to_all(output_offsets, "expert", 0, 0, tiled=True)
   356	    input_offsets_x = jax.lax.all_to_all(input_offsets, "expert", 0, 0, tiled=True)
   357	    # Tie to this side's send_sizes, not recv_sizes: the return path's passthrough fill ties to
   358	    # its own send_sizes, which is the SAME tensor as this dispatch's recv_sizes, and two fills
   359	    # with identical shape and tie CSE back into one value with a destructive consumer --
   360	    # re-minting exactly the copy this construction removes.
   361	    init = _loop_local_zeros(source_rows, cotangent.shape[1], cotangent.dtype, send_sizes, site=2)
   362	    source_ct = jax.lax.ragged_all_to_all(
   363	        cotangent, init, output_offsets_x, recv_sizes, input_offsets_x, send_sizes, axis_name="expert"
   364	    )
   365	    return source_ct, None, None, None, None
   366	
   367	
   368	_dispatch_ragged_a2a.defvjp(_dispatch_ragged_a2a_fwd, _dispatch_ragged_a2a_bwd)
   369	
   370	
   371	@functools.partial(jax.custom_vjp, nondiff_argnums=(0,))
   372	def _return_ragged_a2a(
   373	    capacity: int,
   374	    out_dispatch: Float[Array, "C H"],
   375	    returned: Float[Array, "TK H"],
   376	    input_offsets: Int[Array, "U"],
   377	    send_sizes: Int[Array, "U"],
   378	    output_offsets: Int[Array, "U"],
   379	    recv_sizes: Int[Array, "U"],
   380	) -> Float[Array, "TK H"]:
   381	    """Return-direction ``ragged_all_to_all``: write expert outputs back over ``returned``.
   382	
   383	    Same construction as `_dispatch_ragged_a2a`: the primal is unchanged, and the custom vjp
   384	    replicates jax's transpose rule operation for operation, replacing only the transposed
   385	    a2a's zero init so it is built per-iteration instead of hoisted and copied.
   386	    """
   387	    del capacity
   388	    return jax.lax.ragged_all_to_all(
   389	        out_dispatch, returned, input_offsets, send_sizes, output_offsets, recv_sizes, axis_name="expert"
   390	    )
   391	
   392	
   393	def _return_ragged_a2a_fwd(
   394	    capacity: int,
   395	    out_dispatch: Float[Array, "C H"],
   396	    returned: Float[Array, "TK H"],
   397	    input_offsets: Int[Array, "U"],
   398	    send_sizes: Int[Array, "U"],
   399	    output_offsets: Int[Array, "U"],
   400	    recv_sizes: Int[Array, "U"],
   401	) -> tuple[Float[Array, "TK H"], tuple[jax.Array, jax.Array, jax.Array, jax.Array]]:
   402	    result = _return_ragged_a2a(
   403	        capacity, out_dispatch, returned, input_offsets, send_sizes, output_offsets, recv_sizes
   404	    )
   405	    return result, (input_offsets, send_sizes, output_offsets, recv_sizes)
   406	
   407	
   408	def _return_ragged_a2a_bwd(
   409	    capacity: int,
   410	    residuals: tuple[jax.Array, jax.Array, jax.Array, jax.Array],
   411	    cotangent: Float[Array, "TK H"],
   412	) -> tuple[Float[Array, "C H"], Float[Array, "TK H"], None, None, None, None]:
   413	    input_offsets, send_sizes, output_offsets, recv_sizes = residuals
   414	    output_offsets_x = jax.lax.all_to_all(output_offsets, "expert", 0, 0, tiled=True)
   415	    input_offsets_x = jax.lax.all_to_all(input_offsets, "expert", 0, 0, tiled=True)
   416	    init = _loop_local_zeros(capacity, cotangent.shape[1], cotangent.dtype, recv_sizes, site=3)
   417	    out_dispatch_ct = jax.lax.ragged_all_to_all(
   418	        cotangent, init, output_offsets_x, recv_sizes, input_offsets_x, send_sizes, axis_name="expert"
   419	    )
   420	    # Rows this a2a overwrote took their value from ``out_dispatch``, so the pass-through
   421	    # cotangent to ``returned`` is zeroed on exactly the written intervals. This mirrors jax's
   422	    # transpose rule op for op (interval marks, cumsum, integer select_n) so the behavior is
   423	    # bit-identical, including on degenerate empty-group offset patterns.
   424	    interval_marks = (
   425	        jnp.zeros(cotangent.shape[0], jnp.int32).at[output_offsets_x].set(1).at[output_offsets_x + recv_sizes].add(-1)
   426	    )
   427	    written = jnp.broadcast_to(jnp.cumsum(interval_marks)[:, None], cotangent.shape)
   428	    passthrough_zero = _loop_local_zeros(cotangent.shape[0], cotangent.shape[1], cotangent.dtype, send_sizes, site=4)
   429	    returned_ct = jax.lax.select_n(written, cotangent, passthrough_zero)
   430	    return out_dispatch_ct, returned_ct, None, None, None, None
   431	
   432	
   433	_return_ragged_a2a.defvjp(_return_ragged_a2a_fwd, _return_ragged_a2a_bwd)
   434	
   435	
   436	def _resolve_expert_chunks(expert_chunks: int | None, local_experts: int) -> int:
   437	    """Sequential chunk count for a bank of ``local_experts``.
   438	
   439	    ``None`` takes `RAGGED_DEFAULT_EXPERT_CHUNKS` and falls back to one chunk on a bank the
   440	    default does not divide, which is how a mesh holding a single local expert runs. An explicit
   441	    count is a measurement knob, so an indivisible one raises instead of quietly running -- and
   442	    reporting -- a different chunk count than the one that was asked for.
   443	    """
   444	    if expert_chunks is None:
   445	        return RAGGED_DEFAULT_EXPERT_CHUNKS if local_experts % RAGGED_DEFAULT_EXPERT_CHUNKS == 0 else 1
   446	    if expert_chunks < 1:
   447	        raise ValueError(f"expert_chunks must be positive, got {expert_chunks}")
   448	    if local_experts % expert_chunks != 0:
   449	        raise ValueError(f"expert_chunks={expert_chunks} must divide the local expert count={local_experts}")
   450	    return expert_chunks
   451	
   452	
   453	def _resolve_receiver_alignment(receiver_alignment: int | None) -> int:
   454	    """Row alignment the receiver buffer's expert groups start on.
   455	
   456	    ``None`` is the unaligned layout: groups are packed back to back and the cuDNN
   457	    weight-gradient wrapper copies both of its operands into an aligned buffer itself. Any other
   458	    value lays the groups out aligned at the source and deletes those copies, which is only
   459	    sound if the value is a multiple of what that kernel requires.
   460	    """
   461	    if receiver_alignment is None:
   462	        return 1
   463	    if receiver_alignment < 1:
   464	        raise ValueError(f"receiver_alignment must be positive, got {receiver_alignment}")
   465	    if receiver_alignment % RAGGED_CUDNN_RECEIVER_ALIGNMENT != 0:
   466	        raise ValueError(
   467	            f"receiver_alignment={receiver_alignment} must be a multiple of "
   468	            f"{RAGGED_CUDNN_RECEIVER_ALIGNMENT}, the cuDNN grouped weight-gradient group alignment"
   469	        )
   470	    return receiver_alignment
   471	
   472	
   473	def _moe_mlp_ep_ragged_a2a_local(
   474	    x_local: Float[Array, "Tlocal H"],
   475	    selected_experts_local: Int[Array, "Tlocal K"],
   476	    combine_weights_local: Float[Array, "Tlocal K"],
   477	    moe_w13_local: Float[Array, "Elocal H I2"],
   478	    moe_w2_local: Float[Array, "Elocal I H"],
   479	    *,
   480	    activation_fn: Callable[[jax.Array], jax.Array],
   481	    num_experts: int,
   482	    capacity_factor: float,
   483	    expert_chunks: int | None = None,
   484	    receiver_alignment: int | None = None,
   485	) -> tuple[Float[Array, "Tlocal H"], CapacityOverflow]:
   486	    local_experts = moe_w13_local.shape[0]
   487	    if num_experts % local_experts != 0:
   488	        raise ValueError(
   489	            f"num_experts={num_experts} must be divisible by local expert count={local_experts} in EP mode"
   490	        )
   491	
   492	    shard_id = jax.lax.axis_index("expert")
   493	    ep_size = num_experts // local_experts
   494	    tokens_per_shard = x_local.shape[0]
   495	    topk = selected_experts_local.shape[1]
   496	    assignments_per_shard = tokens_per_shard * topk
   497	    local_capacity = int(math.ceil(capacity_factor * assignments_per_shard))
   498	    local_capacity = max(local_experts, local_capacity)
   499	
   500	    # Local experts are processed in sequential chunks so only one chunk's buffers are live at a
   501	    # time: capacity splits evenly across chunks, so two chunks halve the [C, H] transport
   502	    # buffers and the expert MLP's [C, I2] gate-up intermediate that sit between them. It also
   503	    # makes drop clipping per-chunk, which is a routing difference, not just a memory one.
   504	    #
   505	    # What chunking does not change is what crosses the forward/backward boundary. The block's
   506	    # remat policy re-runs this function in the backward, so the lowered module carries every
   507	    # ragged all-to-all three times at any chunk count -- primal, backward recompute, transpose,
   508	    # verified in the lowered StableHLO: 12 ops at two chunks, 6 at one. The a2a outputs are
   509	    # transient inside a chunk, not residuals pinned across the block window.
   510	    chunks = _resolve_expert_chunks(expert_chunks, local_experts)
   511	    chunk_experts = local_experts // chunks
   512	    chunk_capacity = max(chunk_experts, int(math.ceil(local_capacity / chunks)))
   513	    hidden_dim = x_local.shape[1]
   514	
   515	    # Aligning the receiver's expert groups costs up to `alignment - 1` unwritten rows per group
   516	    # in the chunk. Those rows are buffer, not capacity: the clip below still admits
   517	    # `chunk_capacity` rows, so no assignment is accepted or dropped differently.
   518	    alignment = _resolve_receiver_alignment(receiver_alignment)
   519	    receiver_rows = chunk_capacity + (alignment - 1) * chunk_experts
   520	
   521	    with jax.named_scope("dispatch"):
   522	        flat_selected = selected_experts_local.reshape(-1)  # [TK]
   523	        sorted_indices = tree_checkpoint_name(jnp.argsort(flat_selected), RAGGED_SORTED_INDICES_REMAT_NAME)  # [TK]
   524	        group_sizes = tree_checkpoint_name(
   525	            jnp.bincount(flat_selected, length=num_experts).astype(jnp.int32), RAGGED_GROUP_SIZES_REMAT_NAME
   526	        )  # [E]
   527	        sorted_x = _gather_dispatch_rows(x_local, sorted_indices, topk)  # [TK, H]
   528	        all_group_sizes = jax.lax.all_gather(group_sizes, "expert")  # [S, E]
   529	
   530	    expert_mlp = _select_expert_mlp(activation_fn, receiver_alignment=alignment)
   531	    chunk_of_expert = (jnp.arange(num_experts, dtype=jnp.int32) % local_experts) // chunk_experts  # [E]
   532	    # Built per-iteration (not jnp.zeros) so the layer scan does not re-copy a hoisted
   533	    # constant into the in-place return a2a's output slot every step; see _loop_local_zeros.
   534	    # The zeros are load-bearing: rows no peer writes back must read 0 in the combine.
   535	    returned = _loop_local_zeros(assignments_per_shard, hidden_dim, x_local.dtype, group_sizes, site=5)  # [TK, H]
   536	    accepted_local = jnp.zeros((), dtype=jnp.int32)
   537	    for chunk_index in range(chunks):
   538	        with jax.named_scope(f"moe_chunk_{chunk_index}"):
   539	            chunk_all_group_sizes = jnp.where(chunk_of_expert[None, :] == chunk_index, all_group_sizes, 0)  # [S, E]
   540	            clipped_group_sizes = _clip_receiver_group_sizes(
   541	                chunk_all_group_sizes,
   542	                local_expert_size=local_experts,
   543	                receiver_capacity=chunk_capacity,
   544	            )
   545	            # Sender starts come from the full (unmasked) sizes, so each chunk reads its
   546	            # groups' accepted prefixes in place in the shared sorted buffer.
   547	            dispatch_params, return_params = _expert_granular_a2a_params(
   548	                all_group_sizes,
   549	                clipped_group_sizes,
   550	                shard_id,
   551	                local_expert_size=local_experts,
   552	                receiver_alignment=alignment,
   553	            )
   554	            # Serialize the chunks. Without this barrier, the scheduler can start the dispatch
   555	            # of every chunk at the same time. This causes the high memory use that the chunks
   556	            # prevent. A variant that overlaps one transport with the MLP stays within memory.
   557	            # But it does not increase the speed. The transport and the MLP compete for the
   558	            # same SMs.
   559	            chunk_source, _ = jax.lax.optimization_barrier((sorted_x, returned))
   560	            # Accepted rows are the prefix of each unclipped expert group and receiver offsets
   561	            # pack arrivals expert-major, so the received buffer feeds the grouped MLP
   562	            # directly: no sender compaction and no receiver-side permute.
   563	            x_dispatch = _dispatch_ragged_a2a(  # [C, H]
   564	                receiver_rows,
   565	                assignments_per_shard,
   566	                chunk_source,
   567	                *dispatch_params,
   568	            )
   569	            active_all = jnp.sum(  # [Elocal]
   570	                clipped_group_sizes.reshape(ep_size, ep_size, local_experts)[:, shard_id, :], axis=0
   571	            )
   572	            # The group extents the receiver buffer was actually laid out on -- the arrival counts
   573	            # under no alignment, and their rounded-up extents otherwise. The a2a rounds the same
   574	            # per-expert totals the same way, so the two layouts agree by construction.
   575	            active_group_sizes = _align_up_rows(
   576	                active_all[chunk_index * chunk_experts : (chunk_index + 1) * chunk_experts], alignment
   577	            )  # [Echunk]
   578	            total_valid = jnp.sum(active_group_sizes, dtype=jnp.int32)
   579	            physical_group_sizes = active_group_sizes.at[-1].add(receiver_rows - total_valid)  # [Echunk]
   580	            out_dispatch = expert_mlp(  # [C, H]
   581	                x_dispatch,
   582	                moe_w13_local[chunk_index * chunk_experts : (chunk_index + 1) * chunk_experts],
   583	                moe_w2_local[chunk_index * chunk_experts : (chunk_index + 1) * chunk_experts],
   584	                physical_group_sizes,
   585	                active_group_sizes,
   586	                activation_fn,
   587	            )
   588	            # The mirror of dispatch: valid prefixes land back at unclipped sorted positions.
   589	            # Chaining every chunk through one output buffer composes the disjoint writes;
   590	            # dropped rows keep the buffer's zeros, so the final gather-sum reads dropped
   591	            # slots as zero contributions with no expansion step.
   592	            returned = _return_ragged_a2a(
   593	                receiver_rows,
   594	                out_dispatch,
   595	                returned,
   596	                *return_params,
   597	            )
   598	            accepted_local = accepted_local + jnp.sum(clipped_group_sizes[shard_id], dtype=jnp.int32)
   599	
   600	    with jax.named_scope("combine"):
   601	        out_local = _unpermute_from_global_expert(
   602	            returned,
   603	            sorted_indices,
   604	            combine_weights_local,
   605	            tokens_per_shard=tokens_per_shard,
   606	            topk=topk,
   607	        ).astype(x_local.dtype)
   608	        dropped_local = jnp.sum(group_sizes, dtype=jnp.int32) - accepted_local
   609	        dropped_total = jax.lax.psum(dropped_local, _batch_axes(jax.sharding.get_abstract_mesh()))
   610	    return out_local, CapacityOverflow(sender=dropped_total, receiver=jnp.zeros_like(dropped_total))
     1	# Copyright The Levanter Authors
     2	# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
     3	
     4	"""Local Grug MoE backend using Tri Dao's QuACK SM100 kernels (SonicMoE) on B200.
     5	
     6	Dispatch/combine as in ``scatter``, but the expert MLP GEMMs run on QuACK's
     7	``GemmGatedSm100`` / ``GemmDefaultSm100`` via the vendored ``cutlass.jax.cutlass_call``
     8	shim. QuACK does all four activation-path grouped GEMMs (gate/up fwd fused with
     9	SwiGLU, down fwd, and the ``dh``/``dx`` backward matmuls); the SwiGLU backward is
    10	elementwise in JAX; the two weight-gradient GEMMs (``dw13``/``dw2``) stay on XLA
    11	``ragged_dot`` (a different varlen-k grouping). QuACK covers ~2/3 of the MoE FLOPs.
    12	
    13	``_expert_mlp_cudnn`` is the same forward with those two weight gradients moved onto cuDNN
    14	Frontend grouped Wgrad kernels, which is faster than ``ragged_dot`` at the hero shapes.
    15	"""
    16	
    17	import jax
    18	import jax.numpy as jnp
    19	import numpy as np
    20	from haliax.jax_utils import tree_checkpoint_name
    21	from haliax.nn.ragged_dot import ragged_dot
    22	from jaxtyping import Array, Float, Int
    23	
    24	from levanter.grug._moe.common import (
    25	    _CHECKPOINT_DISPATCH_INPUT,
    26	    _CHECKPOINT_DISPATCH_OUTPUT,
    27	    _chunk_capacity_drops,
    28	    _interleave_gate_up,
    29	    _prepare_moe_dispatch,
    30	    _swiglu_gate_up_backward,
    31	    _zero_dropped_assignments,
    32	    _zero_inactive_grouped_rows,
    33	)
    34	from levanter.grug._moe.cudnn_wgrad_cute import cudnn_grouped_wgrad, cudnn_grouped_wgrad_prealigned
    35	from levanter.grug._moe.quack_moe_cute import quack_gated_grouped_gemm, quack_grouped_gemm
    36	
    37	# QuACK activation-path GEMM configuration, tuned at the i3072 hero shapes on one GB200.
    38	# Tile (256, 256) beats the (256, 128) default by 1.235x on the gated GEMM and 1.094x on the
    39	# down GEMM. CLC persistence adds a further 1.049x / 1.120x at that tile. Under CLC the two
    40	# GEMMs prefer different clusters: the gated gate/up GEMM stays at (2, 1, 1), while the plain
    41	# grouped GEMMs -- down forward plus the backward dh/dx matmuls -- gain 1.055x at (2, 2, 1).
    42	# All of this is scheduling, so none of it changes the computed function.
    43	#
    44	# These reach `_expert_mlp_cudnn` only. `_expert_mlp` -- the local FSDP path, used by the
    45	# `fsdp-nodrop` and `fsdp-chunk4` ablation arms -- still calls the GEMMs at their defaults, as it
    46	# did before this tuning existed, so nothing regressed. It is untuned rather than deliberately
    47	# tuned differently: the measurements above were taken at the i3072 hero shapes and the FSDP arms
    48	# run d768, so the numbers do not transfer without re-measuring.
    49	# TODO: re-measure these at the FSDP ablation shapes and either extend the tuning to
    50	# `_expert_mlp` or record why the defaults win there.
    51	_QUACK_TILE_MN = (256, 256)
    52	_QUACK_USE_CLC = True
    53	_QUACK_GATED_KW = dict(tile_mn=_QUACK_TILE_MN, cluster_mnk=(2, 1, 1), use_clc_persistence=_QUACK_USE_CLC)
    54	_QUACK_GROUPED_KW = dict(tile_mn=_QUACK_TILE_MN, cluster_mnk=(2, 2, 1), use_clc_persistence=_QUACK_USE_CLC)
    55	
    56	
    57	@jax.custom_vjp
    58	def _expert_mlp(x_dispatch, w13_il, moe_w2, group_sizes, cu):
    59	    """y = down( swiglu( x @ w13_il ) ), grouped by experts. Activation-path GEMMs on QuACK.
    60	
    61	    ``group_sizes``/``cu`` are traced int arrays passed as explicit args (not closed
    62	    over — that leaks under shard_map; not nondiff_argnums — that rejects tracers).
    63	    """
    64	    _gu, h = quack_gated_grouped_gemm(x_dispatch, w13_il, cu, return_preact=True)
    65	    return quack_grouped_gemm(h, moe_w2, cu, b_major="n")
    66	
    67	
    68	def _expert_mlp_fwd(x_dispatch, w13_il, moe_w2, group_sizes, cu):
    69	    gu, h = quack_gated_grouped_gemm(x_dispatch, w13_il, cu, return_preact=True)
    70	    y = quack_grouped_gemm(h, moe_w2, cu, b_major="n")
    71	    return y, (x_dispatch, w13_il, moe_w2, gu, h, group_sizes, cu)
    72	
    73	
    74	def _expert_mlp_bwd(res, dy):
    75	    x_dispatch, w13_il, moe_w2, gu, h, group_sizes, cu = res
    76	    # down backward: dh via QuACK (transposed contraction), dw2 via XLA weight-grad
    77	    dh = quack_grouped_gemm(dy, moe_w2, cu, b_major="k")
    78	    (dw2,) = jax.vjp(lambda w: ragged_dot(h, w, group_sizes), moe_w2)[1](dy)
    79	    d_gu = _swiglu_gate_up_backward(gu, dh)
    80	    # gate/up backward: dx via QuACK, dw13 via XLA weight-grad
    81	    dx = quack_grouped_gemm(d_gu, w13_il, cu, b_major="k")
    82	    (dw13_il,) = jax.vjp(lambda w: ragged_dot(x_dispatch, w, group_sizes), w13_il)[1](d_gu)
    83	    # int-typed routing args get float0 zero cotangents
    84	    gs_ct = np.zeros(group_sizes.shape, dtype=jax.dtypes.float0)
    85	    cu_ct = np.zeros(cu.shape, dtype=jax.dtypes.float0)
    86	    return dx, dw13_il, dw2, gs_ct, cu_ct
    87	
    88	
    89	_expert_mlp.defvjp(_expert_mlp_fwd, _expert_mlp_bwd)
    90	
    91	
    92	def _build_expert_mlp_cudnn(grouped_wgrad):
    93	    """``_expert_mlp`` with the two weight-gradient GEMMs on ``grouped_wgrad``.
    94	
    95	    The forward output is masked past the last expert group: the grouped GEMMs write only
    96	    the rows inside ``cu``, and those trailing rows flow on through the unpermute and
    97	    combine, so they have to be zero rather than whatever the buffer held.
    98	
    99	    ``grouped_wgrad`` is which cuDNN entry point the weight gradients take, which is fixed per
   100	    caller: `cudnn_grouped_wgrad` pads the operands into the kernel's aligned layout, and
   101	    `cudnn_grouped_wgrad_prealigned` skips that copy for a caller whose ``group_sizes`` already
   102	    describe an aligned layout. Both compute the same function; the second is the same kernel
   103	    call on the same bytes without the pre-pass.
   104	    """
   105	
   106	    @jax.custom_vjp
   107	    def _expert_mlp_cudnn(x_dispatch, w13_il, moe_w2, group_sizes, cu):
   108	        _gu, h = quack_gated_grouped_gemm(x_dispatch, w13_il, cu, return_preact=True, **_QUACK_GATED_KW)
   109	        y = quack_grouped_gemm(h, moe_w2, cu, b_major="n", **_QUACK_GROUPED_KW)
   110	        return _zero_inactive_grouped_rows(y, cu)
   111	
   112	    def _expert_mlp_cudnn_fwd(x_dispatch, w13_il, moe_w2, group_sizes, cu):
   113	        gu, h = quack_gated_grouped_gemm(x_dispatch, w13_il, cu, return_preact=True, **_QUACK_GATED_KW)
   114	        y = quack_grouped_gemm(h, moe_w2, cu, b_major="n", **_QUACK_GROUPED_KW)
   115	        return _zero_inactive_grouped_rows(y, cu), (x_dispatch, w13_il, moe_w2, gu, h, group_sizes, cu)
   116	
   117	    def _expert_mlp_cudnn_bwd(res, dy):
   118	        x_dispatch, w13_il, moe_w2, gu, h, group_sizes, cu = res
   119	        # The cotangent's trailing rows are whatever the caller's buffer held; the grouped GEMMs
   120	        # contract every row they are handed, so they have to be cleared here too.
   121	        dy = _zero_inactive_grouped_rows(dy, cu)
   122	        dh = quack_grouped_gemm(dy, moe_w2, cu, b_major="k", **_QUACK_GROUPED_KW)
   123	        dw2 = grouped_wgrad(h, dy, group_sizes)
   124	        d_gu = _swiglu_gate_up_backward(gu, dh)
   125	        dx = quack_grouped_gemm(d_gu, w13_il, cu, b_major="k", **_QUACK_GROUPED_KW)
   126	        dx = _zero_inactive_grouped_rows(dx, cu)
   127	        dw13_il = grouped_wgrad(x_dispatch, d_gu, group_sizes)
   128	        gs_ct = np.zeros(group_sizes.shape, dtype=jax.dtypes.float0)
   129	        cu_ct = np.zeros(cu.shape, dtype=jax.dtypes.float0)
   130	        return dx, dw13_il, dw2, gs_ct, cu_ct
   131	
   132	    _expert_mlp_cudnn.defvjp(_expert_mlp_cudnn_fwd, _expert_mlp_cudnn_bwd)
   133	    return _expert_mlp_cudnn
   134	
   135	
   136	_expert_mlp_cudnn = _build_expert_mlp_cudnn(cudnn_grouped_wgrad)
   137	# For a receiver buffer whose expert groups already start on the kernel's aligned rows, with the
   138	# slack between them zero. The transport builds that layout, so the pad pass is pure copy traffic.
   139	_expert_mlp_cudnn_prealigned = _build_expert_mlp_cudnn(cudnn_grouped_wgrad_prealigned)
   140	
   141	
   142	def _moe_mlp_local_sonic_cute(
   143	    x: Float[Array, "T H"],
   144	    selected_experts: Int[Array, "T K"],
   145	    combine_weights: Float[Array, "T K"],
   146	    moe_w13: Float[Array, "E H I2"],
   147	    moe_w2: Float[Array, "E I H"],
   148	    *,
   149	    num_experts: int,
   150	) -> tuple[Float[Array, "T H"], Int[Array, ""]]:
   151	    x_dispatch, w_dispatch, token_dispatch, group_sizes = _prepare_moe_dispatch(
   152	        x, selected_experts, combine_weights, num_experts=num_experts
   153	    )
   154	    x_dispatch = tree_checkpoint_name(x_dispatch, _CHECKPOINT_DISPATCH_INPUT)
   155	    moe_dim = moe_w2.shape[1]
   156	    w13_il = _interleave_gate_up(moe_w13, moe_dim)
   157	    cu = jnp.concatenate([jnp.zeros((1,), jnp.int32), jnp.cumsum(group_sizes).astype(jnp.int32)])
   158	
   159	    with jax.named_scope("moe_up_down_quack"):
   160	        out_dispatch = tree_checkpoint_name(
   161	            _expert_mlp(x_dispatch, w13_il, moe_w2, group_sizes, cu), _CHECKPOINT_DISPATCH_OUTPUT
   162	        )
   163	
   164	    with jax.named_scope("scatter"):
   165	        out = jnp.zeros_like(x).at[token_dispatch].add(out_dispatch * w_dispatch[:, None], mode="drop")
   166	    return out, _zero_dropped_assignments()
   167	
   168	
   169	def _moe_mlp_local_sonic_cute_chunked(
   170	    x: Float[Array, "T H"],
   171	    selected_experts: Int[Array, "T K"],
   172	    combine_weights: Float[Array, "T K"],
   173	    moe_w13_local: Float[Array, "E Hlocal I2"],
   174	    moe_w2_local: Float[Array, "E I Hlocal"],
   175	    *,
   176	    num_experts: int,
   177	    chunk_sizes: tuple[int, ...],
   178	    data_axis_name: str,
   179	) -> tuple[Float[Array, "T H"], Int[Array, ""]]:
   180	    """Chunked variant that gathers only one chunk of the expert weights at a time.
   181	
   182	    The FSDP weights arrive H-sharded over ``data_axis_name`` (``moe_w13_local`` is [E, H/data, 2I],
   183	    ``moe_w2_local`` is [E, I, H/data]). Dispatch runs ONCE (``_prepare_moe_dispatch`` sorts every
   184	    local (token, expert) assignment by expert, so experts ``[lo, hi)`` are a contiguous segment of
   185	    the sorted buffer). For each static chunk we all-gather only that chunk's expert weights (a
   186	    ``1/chunks``-size collective, so chunk k+1's gather fits the scheduler's overlap-memory budget and
   187	    can hide under chunk k's GEMM), slice the matching token segment, run the QuACK grouped GEMM over
   188	    just that segment, and scatter-accumulate the outputs.
   189	
   190	    Segment handling (see the module docstring on ``_expert_mlp``): the QuACK kernel and the XLA
   191	    ``ragged_dot`` weight-grad path both index rows relative to row 0 of the buffer they are given, so
   192	    each chunk gets a segment-relative ``x_dispatch`` (sliced to start at ``cu[lo]``) with a rebased
   193	    ``cu_c``. Each chunk's segment length is a STATIC ``capacity`` that scales with its expert count
   194	    (``total_assignments * size / num_experts``, 1x balanced, drop overflow), so the per-chunk
   195	    capacities sum to ``total_assignments`` exactly as the uniform case does. ``chunk_sizes`` need not
   196	    be equal: e.g. ``(16, 16, 96)`` runs two small gathers, which start the expert GEMMs quickly,
   197	    followed by one large gather that overlaps them.
   198	    Rows past the chunk's real assignments are folded into the last expert group (so the kernel never
   199	    leaves ungrouped garbage rows) but weight-masked to zero, so they contribute nothing to the
   200	    forward output and route a zero cotangent back to the router in the combine backward.
   201	
   202	    """
   203	    if sum(chunk_sizes) != num_experts:
   204	        raise ValueError(f"chunk_sizes={chunk_sizes} must sum to num_experts={num_experts}")
   205	
   206	    x_dispatch, w_dispatch, token_dispatch, group_sizes = _prepare_moe_dispatch(
   207	        x, selected_experts, combine_weights, num_experts=num_experts
   208	    )
   209	    x_dispatch = tree_checkpoint_name(x_dispatch, _CHECKPOINT_DISPATCH_INPUT)
   210	    moe_dim = moe_w2_local.shape[1]
   211	    total_assignments, hidden = x_dispatch.shape
   212	
   213	    # Expert-group boundaries and a per-chunk static capacity proportional to the chunk's expert
   214	    # count. The capacities sum to total_assignments (as with equal chunks); a larger chunk holds
   215	    # proportionally more tokens.
   216	    bounds = [0]
   217	    for size in chunk_sizes:
   218	        bounds.append(bounds[-1] + size)
   219	    caps = [total_assignments * size // num_experts for size in chunk_sizes]
   220	    max_cap = max(caps)
   221	    cu = jnp.concatenate([jnp.zeros((1,), jnp.int32), jnp.cumsum(group_sizes).astype(jnp.int32)])
   222	
   223	    # Pad the sorted buffers by the LARGEST chunk capacity so every chunk's
   224	    # ``dynamic_slice(start=cu[lo], size=cap)`` never clamps its start index (which would silently
   225	    # shift the window and misgroup rows). Padding carries zero combine weight, so it never
   226	    # contributes to the output or its gradient.
   227	    x_pad = jnp.pad(x_dispatch, ((0, max_cap), (0, 0)))
   228	    w_pad = jnp.pad(w_dispatch, (0, max_cap))
   229	    token_pad = jnp.pad(token_dispatch, (0, max_cap))
   230	
   231	    out = jnp.zeros_like(x)
   232	    for c, cap in enumerate(caps):
   233	        lo = bounds[c]
   234	        hi = bounds[c + 1]
   235	        with jax.named_scope("gather_chunk"):
   236	            # Interleave on the local shard: it rewrites the last axis and the gather is along H, so
   237	            # the two commute, and this does 1/data-th of the elementwise work.
   238	            w13_local = _interleave_gate_up(moe_w13_local[lo:hi], moe_dim)
   239	            w13_il = jax.lax.all_gather(w13_local, data_axis_name, axis=1, tiled=True)
   240	            w2_chunk = jax.lax.all_gather(moe_w2_local[lo:hi], data_axis_name, axis=2, tiled=True)
   241	
   242	        start = cu[lo]
   243	        x_seg = jax.lax.dynamic_slice(x_pad, (start, 0), (cap, hidden))
   244	        token_seg = jax.lax.dynamic_slice(token_pad, (start,), (cap,))
   245	        w_seg = jax.lax.dynamic_slice(w_pad, (start,), (cap,))
   246	
   247	        # Real assignments for this chunk occupy segment rows [0, count); the rest are padding or
   248	        # rows belonging to later chunks. Mask their combine weight to zero.
   249	        count = cu[hi] - start
   250	        valid = jnp.arange(cap, dtype=jnp.int32) < jnp.minimum(count, cap)
   251	        w_seg = jnp.where(valid, w_seg, jnp.zeros_like(w_seg))
   252	
   253	        # Segment-relative group boundaries. Fold the leftover capacity into the last expert so the
   254	        # kernel writes every row (no ungrouped garbage); those extra rows are weight-masked above.
   255	        raw = jnp.clip(cu[lo : hi + 1] - start, 0, cap)
   256	        group_sizes_c = jnp.diff(raw)
   257	        group_sizes_c = group_sizes_c.at[-1].add(cap - raw[-1])
   258	        cu_c = jnp.concatenate([jnp.zeros((1,), jnp.int32), jnp.cumsum(group_sizes_c).astype(jnp.int32)])
   259	
   260	        with jax.named_scope("moe_up_down_quack_chunk"):
   261	            out_dispatch = tree_checkpoint_name(
   262	                _expert_mlp(x_seg, w13_il, w2_chunk, group_sizes_c, cu_c), _CHECKPOINT_DISPATCH_OUTPUT
   263	            )
   264	        with jax.named_scope("scatter_chunk"):
   265	            out = out.at[token_seg].add(out_dispatch * w_seg[:, None], mode="drop")
   266	    return out, _chunk_capacity_drops(cu, bounds, caps)
     1	# Copyright The Levanter Authors

     4	"""cuDNN Frontend grouped weight gradients through the CuTeDSL JAX bridge."""
     5	
     6	import functools
     7	import importlib
     8	from typing import Any, NamedTuple
     9	
    10	import jax
    11	import jax.numpy as jnp
    12	
    13	from levanter.cutlass_kernel_cache import cute_launcher_factory, cutlass_call
    14	
    15	# Row count each expert group is padded up to, so every group starts where the kernel's
    16	# tile loads expect it to.
    17	_GROUP_ALIGNMENT = 8
    18	# Vector width the feature (non-grouped) dimensions must divide, which is what the tensor
    19	# specs below declare to the kernel.
    20	_FEATURE_ALIGNMENT = 8
    21	_MMA_TILER_MN = (256, 256)
    22	_CLUSTER_SHAPE_MN = (2, 1)
    23	
    24	
    25	class _CudnnModules(NamedTuple):
    26	    """CuTeDSL and cuDNN Frontend entry points, imported only where the GPU extra exists."""
    27	
    28	    cutlass: Any
    29	    cute: Any
    30	    cutlass_jax: Any
    31	    kernel_type: Any
    32	    weight_mode: Any
    33	    input_order: Any
    34	
    35	
    36	@functools.cache
    37	def _cudnn_modules() -> _CudnnModules:
    38	    kernel_module = importlib.import_module("cudnn.gemm.cutedsl.grouped.wgrad.moe_grouped_gemm_wgrad")
    39	    utility_module = importlib.import_module("cudnn.gemm.cutedsl.grouped.moe_utils")
    40	    return _CudnnModules(
    41	        cutlass=importlib.import_module("cutlass"),
    42	        cute=importlib.import_module("cutlass.cute"),
    43	        cutlass_jax=importlib.import_module("cutlass.jax"),
    44	        kernel_type=kernel_module.MoEGroupedGemmWgradBF16Kernel,
    45	        weight_mode=utility_module.MoEWeightMode,
    46	        input_order=utility_module.WGradInputOrder,
    47	    )
    48	
    49	
    50	@cute_launcher_factory
    51	def _build_launcher(
    52	    modules,
    53	    *,
    54	    expert_count: int,
    55	    max_active_clusters: int,
    56	):
    57	    @modules.cute.jit
    58	    def launcher(stream, mat_a, mat_b, offsets, output, workspace):
    59	        kernel = modules.kernel_type(
    60	            acc_dtype=modules.cutlass.Float32,
    61	            use_2cta_instrs=True,
    62	            mma_tiler_mn=_MMA_TILER_MN,
    63	            cluster_shape_mn=_CLUSTER_SHAPE_MN,
    64	            accumulate_on_output=False,
    65	            expert_cnt=expert_count,
    66	            weight_mode=modules.weight_mode.DENSE,
    67	            input_order=modules.input_order.Tensor2D,
    68	        )
    69	        kernel(mat_a, mat_b, output, offsets, workspace, max_active_clusters, stream, None)
    70	
    71	    return launcher

    73	
    74	def pad_grouped_rows(values: jax.Array, group_sizes: jax.Array) -> tuple[jax.Array, jax.Array]:
    75	    """Insert zero rows so each contiguous expert group ends on an eight-row boundary."""
    76	    if values.ndim != 2:
    77	        raise ValueError(f"values must be rank 2, got shape={values.shape}")
    78	    if values.shape[0] == 0:
    79	        raise ValueError("values must contain at least one physical row")
    80	    if group_sizes.ndim != 1 or group_sizes.shape[0] == 0:
    81	        raise ValueError(f"group_sizes must be a nonempty vector, got shape={group_sizes.shape}")
    82	
    83	    group_sizes = group_sizes.astype(jnp.int32)
    84	    padded_group_sizes = ((group_sizes + _GROUP_ALIGNMENT - 1) // _GROUP_ALIGNMENT) * _GROUP_ALIGNMENT
    85	    active_offsets = jnp.cumsum(group_sizes, dtype=jnp.int32)
    86	    padded_offsets = jnp.cumsum(padded_group_sizes, dtype=jnp.int32)
    87	    active_starts = jnp.concatenate([jnp.zeros((1,), jnp.int32), active_offsets[:-1]])
    88	    padded_starts = jnp.concatenate([jnp.zeros((1,), jnp.int32), padded_offsets[:-1]])
    89	
    90	    # At most seven rows are inserted per group. Keep a static worst-case tail so the output shape
    91	    # does not depend on the runtime routing counts.
    92	    padded_capacity = values.shape[0] + (_GROUP_ALIGNMENT - 1) * group_sizes.shape[0]
    93	    padded_rows = jnp.arange(padded_capacity, dtype=jnp.int32)
    94	    expert_ids = jnp.sum(padded_rows[:, None] >= padded_offsets[None, :], axis=1, dtype=jnp.int32)
    95	    safe_expert_ids = jnp.minimum(expert_ids, group_sizes.shape[0] - 1)
    96	    rows_within_group = padded_rows - padded_starts[safe_expert_ids]
    97	    source_rows = active_starts[safe_expert_ids] + rows_within_group
    98	    valid = (expert_ids < group_sizes.shape[0]) & (rows_within_group < group_sizes[safe_expert_ids])
    99	    source_rows = jnp.clip(source_rows, 0, values.shape[0] - 1)
   100	    padded = jnp.where(valid[:, None], values[source_rows], jnp.zeros((), dtype=values.dtype))
   101	    return padded, padded_offsets
   102	
   103	
   104	def cudnn_grouped_wgrad(lhs: jax.Array, rhs: jax.Array, group_sizes: jax.Array) -> jax.Array:
   105	    """Compute per-expert ``lhs.T @ rhs`` for contiguous ragged row groups.
   106	
   107	    The operands are copied into an aligned layout first, which is what `pad_grouped_rows` costs.
   108	    A caller whose buffers already carry that layout should use `cudnn_grouped_wgrad_prealigned`.
   109	    """
   110	    lhs_padded, padded_offsets = pad_grouped_rows(lhs, group_sizes)
   111	    rhs_padded, _ = pad_grouped_rows(rhs, group_sizes)
   112	    return _grouped_wgrad(lhs_padded, rhs_padded, padded_offsets, expert_count=group_sizes.shape[0])
   113	
   114	
   115	def cudnn_grouped_wgrad_prealigned(lhs: jax.Array, rhs: jax.Array, group_sizes: jax.Array) -> jax.Array:
   116	    """`cudnn_grouped_wgrad` for operands already in the kernel's aligned layout.
   117	
   118	    The caller guarantees that group ``i`` occupies rows
   119	    ``[sum(group_sizes[:i]), sum(group_sizes[:i+1]))`` of both operands, that every entry of
   120	    ``group_sizes`` is a multiple of `_GROUP_ALIGNMENT` (so every group starts on an aligned
   121	    row), and that any row inside a group that carries no data is zero. Under that contract this
   122	    is `cudnn_grouped_wgrad` with the pad pass removed: `pad_grouped_rows` applied to such a
   123	    layout reproduces it row for row and returns ``cumsum(group_sizes)``, so the kernel sees
   124	    byte-identical operands and offsets either way.
   125	
   126	    Rows past the last group are never read, so the operands may be longer than the last offset.
   127	    """
   128	    return _grouped_wgrad(lhs, rhs, jnp.cumsum(group_sizes, dtype=jnp.int32), expert_count=group_sizes.shape[0])
   129	
   130	
   131	def _grouped_wgrad(lhs: jax.Array, rhs: jax.Array, offsets: jax.Array, *, expert_count: int) -> jax.Array:
   132	    """Call the kernel over row groups delimited by ``offsets``, the per-group end rows."""
   133	    if lhs.ndim != 2 or rhs.ndim != 2:
   134	        raise ValueError(f"lhs and rhs must be rank 2, got lhs={lhs.shape}, rhs={rhs.shape}")
   135	    if lhs.shape[0] != rhs.shape[0]:
   136	        raise ValueError(f"lhs and rhs row counts must match, got lhs={lhs.shape}, rhs={rhs.shape}")
   137	    if lhs.dtype != jnp.bfloat16 or rhs.dtype != jnp.bfloat16:
   138	        raise ValueError(f"cuDNN grouped Wgrad requires BF16 inputs, got lhs={lhs.dtype}, rhs={rhs.dtype}")
   139	    if lhs.shape[1] % _FEATURE_ALIGNMENT != 0 or rhs.shape[1] % _FEATURE_ALIGNMENT != 0:
   140	        raise ValueError(
   141	            f"cuDNN grouped Wgrad feature dimensions must divide {_FEATURE_ALIGNMENT}, "
   142	            f"got lhs={lhs.shape}, rhs={rhs.shape}"
   143	        )
   144	
   145	    modules = _cudnn_modules()
   146	    max_active_clusters = modules.cutlass.utils.HardwareInfo().get_max_active_clusters(
   147	        _CLUSTER_SHAPE_MN[0] * _CLUSTER_SHAPE_MN[1]
   148	    )
   149	    launcher = _build_launcher(
   150	        modules,
   151	        expert_count=expert_count,
   152	        max_active_clusters=max_active_clusters,
   153	    )
   154	    tensor_spec = modules.cutlass_jax.TensorSpec
   155	    call = cutlass_call(
   156	        launcher,
   157	        output_shape_dtype=(
   158	            jax.ShapeDtypeStruct((expert_count, lhs.shape[1], rhs.shape[1]), lhs.dtype),
   159	            jax.ShapeDtypeStruct((1,), jnp.uint8),
   160	        ),
   161	        input_spec=(
   162	            tensor_spec(mode=(1, 0), divisibility=(1, _FEATURE_ALIGNMENT), static=False),
   163	            tensor_spec(divisibility=(1, _FEATURE_ALIGNMENT), static=False),
   164	            tensor_spec(static=False),
   165	        ),
   166	        output_spec=(
   167	            tensor_spec(divisibility=(1, 1, _FEATURE_ALIGNMENT), static=False),
   168	            tensor_spec(static=False),
   169	        ),
   170	        use_static_tensors=False,
   171	    )
   172	    output, _workspace = call(lhs, rhs, offsets)
   173	    return output

     4	"""Local Grug MoE backend using Tri Dao's QuACK SM100 kernels (SonicMoE) on B200.
     5	
     6	Dispatch/combine as in ``scatter``, but the expert MLP GEMMs run on QuACK's
     7	``GemmGatedSm100`` / ``GemmDefaultSm100`` via the vendored ``cutlass.jax.cutlass_call``
     8	shim. QuACK does all four activation-path grouped GEMMs (gate/up fwd fused with
     9	SwiGLU, down fwd, and the ``dh``/``dx`` backward matmuls); the SwiGLU backward is
    10	elementwise in JAX; the two weight-gradient GEMMs (``dw13``/``dw2``) stay on XLA
    11	``ragged_dot`` (a different varlen-k grouping). QuACK covers ~2/3 of the MoE FLOPs.
    12	
    13	``_expert_mlp_cudnn`` is the same forward with those two weight gradients moved onto cuDNN
    14	Frontend grouped Wgrad kernels, which is faster than ``ragged_dot`` at the hero shapes.
    15	"""
    16	
    17	import jax
    18	import jax.numpy as jnp
    19	import numpy as np
    20	from haliax.jax_utils import tree_checkpoint_name
    21	from haliax.nn.ragged_dot import ragged_dot
    22	from jaxtyping import Array, Float, Int
    23	
    24	from levanter.grug._moe.common import (
    25	    _CHECKPOINT_DISPATCH_INPUT,
    26	    _CHECKPOINT_DISPATCH_OUTPUT,
    27	    _chunk_capacity_drops,
    28	    _interleave_gate_up,
    29	    _prepare_moe_dispatch,
    30	    _swiglu_gate_up_backward,
    31	    _zero_dropped_assignments,
    32	    _zero_inactive_grouped_rows,
    33	)
    34	from levanter.grug._moe.cudnn_wgrad_cute import cudnn_grouped_wgrad, cudnn_grouped_wgrad_prealigned
    35	from levanter.grug._moe.quack_moe_cute import quack_gated_grouped_gemm, quack_grouped_gemm
    36	
    37	# QuACK activation-path GEMM configuration, tuned at the i3072 hero shapes on one GB200.
    38	# Tile (256, 256) beats the (256, 128) default by 1.235x on the gated GEMM and 1.094x on the
    39	# down GEMM. CLC persistence adds a further 1.049x / 1.120x at that tile. Under CLC the two
    40	# GEMMs prefer different clusters: the gated gate/up GEMM stays at (2, 1, 1), while the plain
    41	# grouped GEMMs -- down forward plus the backward dh/dx matmuls -- gain 1.055x at (2, 2, 1).
    42	# All of this is scheduling, so none of it changes the computed function.
    43	#
    44	# These reach `_expert_mlp_cudnn` only. `_expert_mlp` -- the local FSDP path, used by the
    45	# `fsdp-nodrop` and `fsdp-chunk4` ablation arms -- still calls the GEMMs at their defaults, as it
    46	# did before this tuning existed, so nothing regressed. It is untuned rather than deliberately
    47	# tuned differently: the measurements above were taken at the i3072 hero shapes and the FSDP arms
    48	# run d768, so the numbers do not transfer without re-measuring.
    49	# TODO: re-measure these at the FSDP ablation shapes and either extend the tuning to
    50	# `_expert_mlp` or record why the defaults win there.
    51	_QUACK_TILE_MN = (256, 256)
    52	_QUACK_USE_CLC = True
    53	_QUACK_GATED_KW = dict(tile_mn=_QUACK_TILE_MN, cluster_mnk=(2, 1, 1), use_clc_persistence=_QUACK_USE_CLC)
    54	_QUACK_GROUPED_KW = dict(tile_mn=_QUACK_TILE_MN, cluster_mnk=(2, 2, 1), use_clc_persistence=_QUACK_USE_CLC)
    55	
    56	
    57	@jax.custom_vjp
    58	def _expert_mlp(x_dispatch, w13_il, moe_w2, group_sizes, cu):
    59	    """y = down( swiglu( x @ w13_il ) ), grouped by experts. Activation-path GEMMs on QuACK.
    60	
    61	    ``group_sizes``/``cu`` are traced int arrays passed as explicit args (not closed
    62	    over — that leaks under shard_map; not nondiff_argnums — that rejects tracers).
    63	    """
    64	    _gu, h = quack_gated_grouped_gemm(x_dispatch, w13_il, cu, return_preact=True)
    65	    return quack_grouped_gemm(h, moe_w2, cu, b_major="n")
    66	
    67	
    68	def _expert_mlp_fwd(x_dispatch, w13_il, moe_w2, group_sizes, cu):
    69	    gu, h = quack_gated_grouped_gemm(x_dispatch, w13_il, cu, return_preact=True)
    70	    y = quack_grouped_gemm(h, moe_w2, cu, b_major="n")
    71	    return y, (x_dispatch, w13_il, moe_w2, gu, h, group_sizes, cu)
    72	
    73	
    74	def _expert_mlp_bwd(res, dy):
    75	    x_dispatch, w13_il, moe_w2, gu, h, group_sizes, cu = res
    76	    # down backward: dh via QuACK (transposed contraction), dw2 via XLA weight-grad
    77	    dh = quack_grouped_gemm(dy, moe_w2, cu, b_major="k")
    78	    (dw2,) = jax.vjp(lambda w: ragged_dot(h, w, group_sizes), moe_w2)[1](dy)
    79	    d_gu = _swiglu_gate_up_backward(gu, dh)
    80	    # gate/up backward: dx via QuACK, dw13 via XLA weight-grad
    81	    dx = quack_grouped_gemm(d_gu, w13_il, cu, b_major="k")
    82	    (dw13_il,) = jax.vjp(lambda w: ragged_dot(x_dispatch, w, group_sizes), w13_il)[1](d_gu)
    83	    # int-typed routing args get float0 zero cotangents
    84	    gs_ct = np.zeros(group_sizes.shape, dtype=jax.dtypes.float0)
    85	    cu_ct = np.zeros(cu.shape, dtype=jax.dtypes.float0)
    86	    return dx, dw13_il, dw2, gs_ct, cu_ct
    87	
    88	
    89	_expert_mlp.defvjp(_expert_mlp_fwd, _expert_mlp_bwd)
    90	
    91	
    92	def _build_expert_mlp_cudnn(grouped_wgrad):
    93	    """``_expert_mlp`` with the two weight-gradient GEMMs on ``grouped_wgrad``.
    94	
    95	    The forward output is masked past the last expert group: the grouped GEMMs write only
    96	    the rows inside ``cu``, and those trailing rows flow on through the unpermute and
    97	    combine, so they have to be zero rather than whatever the buffer held.
    98	
    99	    ``grouped_wgrad`` is which cuDNN entry point the weight gradients take, which is fixed per
   100	    caller: `cudnn_grouped_wgrad` pads the operands into the kernel's aligned layout, and
   101	    `cudnn_grouped_wgrad_prealigned` skips that copy for a caller whose ``group_sizes`` already
   102	    describe an aligned layout. Both compute the same function; the second is the same kernel
   103	    call on the same bytes without the pre-pass.
   104	    """
   105	
   106	    @jax.custom_vjp
   107	    def _expert_mlp_cudnn(x_dispatch, w13_il, moe_w2, group_sizes, cu):
   108	        _gu, h = quack_gated_grouped_gemm(x_dispatch, w13_il, cu, return_preact=True, **_QUACK_GATED_KW)
   109	        y = quack_grouped_gemm(h, moe_w2, cu, b_major="n", **_QUACK_GROUPED_KW)
   110	        return _zero_inactive_grouped_rows(y, cu)
   111	
   112	    def _expert_mlp_cudnn_fwd(x_dispatch, w13_il, moe_w2, group_sizes, cu):
   113	        gu, h = quack_gated_grouped_gemm(x_dispatch, w13_il, cu, return_preact=True, **_QUACK_GATED_KW)
   114	        y = quack_grouped_gemm(h, moe_w2, cu, b_major="n", **_QUACK_GROUPED_KW)
   115	        return _zero_inactive_grouped_rows(y, cu), (x_dispatch, w13_il, moe_w2, gu, h, group_sizes, cu)
   116	
   117	    def _expert_mlp_cudnn_bwd(res, dy):
   118	        x_dispatch, w13_il, moe_w2, gu, h, group_sizes, cu = res
   119	        # The cotangent's trailing rows are whatever the caller's buffer held; the grouped GEMMs
   120	        # contract every row they are handed, so they have to be cleared here too.
   121	        dy = _zero_inactive_grouped_rows(dy, cu)
   122	        dh = quack_grouped_gemm(dy, moe_w2, cu, b_major="k", **_QUACK_GROUPED_KW)
   123	        dw2 = grouped_wgrad(h, dy, group_sizes)
   124	        d_gu = _swiglu_gate_up_backward(gu, dh)
   125	        dx = quack_grouped_gemm(d_gu, w13_il, cu, b_major="k", **_QUACK_GROUPED_KW)
   126	        dx = _zero_inactive_grouped_rows(dx, cu)
   127	        dw13_il = grouped_wgrad(x_dispatch, d_gu, group_sizes)
   128	        gs_ct = np.zeros(group_sizes.shape, dtype=jax.dtypes.float0)
   129	        cu_ct = np.zeros(cu.shape, dtype=jax.dtypes.float0)
   130	        return dx, dw13_il, dw2, gs_ct, cu_ct
   131	
   132	    _expert_mlp_cudnn.defvjp(_expert_mlp_cudnn_fwd, _expert_mlp_cudnn_bwd)
   133	    return _expert_mlp_cudnn
   134	
   135	
   136	_expert_mlp_cudnn = _build_expert_mlp_cudnn(cudnn_grouped_wgrad)
   137	# For a receiver buffer whose expert groups already start on the kernel's aligned rows, with the
   138	# slack between them zero. The transport builds that layout, so the pad pass is pure copy traffic.
   139	_expert_mlp_cudnn_prealigned = _build_expert_mlp_cudnn(cudnn_grouped_wgrad_prealigned)
   140

   300	    return jax.lax.broadcast(zero, (rows, hidden_dim))
