   303	@functools.partial(jax.custom_vjp, nondiff_argnums=(0, 1))
   304	def _dispatch_ragged_a2a(
   305	    capacity: int,
   306	    source_rows: int,
   307	    chunk_source: Float[Array, "TK H"],
   308	    input_offsets: Int[Array, "U"],
   309	    send_sizes: Int[Array, "U"],
   310	    output_offsets: Int[Array, "U"],
   311	    recv_sizes: Int[Array, "U"],
   312	) -> Float[Array, "C H"]:
   313	    """Dispatch-direction ``ragged_all_to_all`` into a freshly zeroed receiver buffer.
   314	
   315	    Owning the output-init here (instead of taking a caller-built ``jnp.zeros``) lets both the
   316	    primal and the transposed direction build their inits with `_loop_local_zeros`. jax's
   317	    built-in transpose rule inits the swapped a2a with plain zeros, which XLA hoists out of
   318	    the layer loop and re-copies every iteration; the custom vjp below is that same rule with
   319	    the init construction replaced. Zeros stay load-bearing: receiver rows no peer writes must
   320	    read 0 downstream, and dropped source rows must read a 0 cotangent in the backward.
   321	    """
   322	    del source_rows
   323	    output_init = _loop_local_zeros(capacity, chunk_source.shape[1], chunk_source.dtype, send_sizes, site=1)
   324	    return jax.lax.ragged_all_to_all(
   325	        chunk_source, output_init, input_offsets, send_sizes, output_offsets, recv_sizes, axis_name="expert"
   326	    )
   327	
   328	
   329	def _dispatch_ragged_a2a_fwd(
   330	    capacity: int,
   331	    source_rows: int,
   332	    chunk_source: Float[Array, "TK H"],
   333	    input_offsets: Int[Array, "U"],
   334	    send_sizes: Int[Array, "U"],
   335	    output_offsets: Int[Array, "U"],
   336	    recv_sizes: Int[Array, "U"],
   337	) -> tuple[Float[Array, "C H"], tuple[jax.Array, jax.Array, jax.Array, jax.Array]]:
   338	    result = _dispatch_ragged_a2a(
   339	        capacity, source_rows, chunk_source, input_offsets, send_sizes, output_offsets, recv_sizes
   340	    )
   341	    return result, (input_offsets, send_sizes, output_offsets, recv_sizes)
   342	
   343	
   344	def _dispatch_ragged_a2a_bwd(
   345	    capacity: int,
   346	    source_rows: int,
   347	    residuals: tuple[jax.Array, jax.Array, jax.Array, jax.Array],
   348	    cotangent: Float[Array, "C H"],
   349	) -> tuple[Float[Array, "TK H"], None, None, None, None]:
   350	    del capacity
   351	    input_offsets, send_sizes, output_offsets, recv_sizes = residuals
   352	    # The transpose of a ragged all-to-all is the reverse ragged all-to-all: swap the send and
   353	    # recv roles and exchange the offset vectors across shards, exactly as jax's transpose rule
   354	    # does. Source rows that were clipped receive no cotangent and keep the init's zeros.
   355	    output_offsets_x = jax.lax.all_to_all(output_offsets, "expert", 0, 0, tiled=True)
   356	    input_offsets_x = jax.lax.all_to_all(input_offsets, "expert", 0, 0, tiled=True)
   357	    # Tie to this side's send_sizes, not recv_sizes: the return path's passthrough fill ties to
   358	    # its own send_sizes, which is the SAME tensor as this dispatch's recv_sizes, and two fills
   359	    # with identical shape and tie CSE back into one value with a destructive consumer --
   360	    # re-minting exactly the copy this construction removes.
   361	    init = _loop_local_zeros(source_rows, cotangent.shape[1], cotangent.dtype, send_sizes, site=2)
   362	    source_ct = jax.lax.ragged_all_to_all(
   363	        cotangent, init, output_offsets_x, recv_sizes, input_offsets_x, send_sizes, axis_name="expert"
   364	    )
   365	    return source_ct, None, None, None, None
   366	
   367	
   368	_dispatch_ragged_a2a.defvjp(_dispatch_ragged_a2a_fwd, _dispatch_ragged_a2a_bwd)
   369	
   370	
   371	@functools.partial(jax.custom_vjp, nondiff_argnums=(0,))
   372	def _return_ragged_a2a(
   373	    capacity: int,
   374	    out_dispatch: Float[Array, "C H"],
   375	    returned: Float[Array, "TK H"],
   376	    input_offsets: Int[Array, "U"],
   377	    send_sizes: Int[Array, "U"],
   378	    output_offsets: Int[Array, "U"],
   379	    recv_sizes: Int[Array, "U"],
   380	) -> Float[Array, "TK H"]:
   381	    """Return-direction ``ragged_all_to_all``: write expert outputs back over ``returned``.
   382	
   383	    Same construction as `_dispatch_ragged_a2a`: the primal is unchanged, and the custom vjp
   384	    replicates jax's transpose rule operation for operation, replacing only the transposed
   385	    a2a's zero init so it is built per-iteration instead of hoisted and copied.
   386	    """
   387	    del capacity
   388	    return jax.lax.ragged_all_to_all(
   389	        out_dispatch, returned, input_offsets, send_sizes, output_offsets, recv_sizes, axis_name="expert"
   390	    )
   391	
   392	
   393	def _return_ragged_a2a_fwd(
   394	    capacity: int,
   395	    out_dispatch: Float[Array, "C H"],
   396	    returned: Float[Array, "TK H"],
   397	    input_offsets: Int[Array, "U"],
   398	    send_sizes: Int[Array, "U"],
   399	    output_offsets: Int[Array, "U"],
   400	    recv_sizes: Int[Array, "U"],
   401	) -> tuple[Float[Array, "TK H"], tuple[jax.Array, jax.Array, jax.Array, jax.Array]]:
   402	    result = _return_ragged_a2a(
   403	        capacity, out_dispatch, returned, input_offsets, send_sizes, output_offsets, recv_sizes
   404	    )
   405	    return result, (input_offsets, send_sizes, output_offsets, recv_sizes)
   406	
   407	
   408	def _return_ragged_a2a_bwd(
   409	    capacity: int,
   410	    residuals: tuple[jax.Array, jax.Array, jax.Array, jax.Array],
   411	    cotangent: Float[Array, "TK H"],
   412	) -> tuple[Float[Array, "C H"], Float[Array, "TK H"], None, None, None, None]:
   413	    input_offsets, send_sizes, output_offsets, recv_sizes = residuals
   414	    output_offsets_x = jax.lax.all_to_all(output_offsets, "expert", 0, 0, tiled=True)
   415	    input_offsets_x = jax.lax.all_to_all(input_offsets, "expert", 0, 0, tiled=True)
   416	    init = _loop_local_zeros(capacity, cotangent.shape[1], cotangent.dtype, recv_sizes, site=3)
   417	    out_dispatch_ct = jax.lax.ragged_all_to_all(
   418	        cotangent, init, output_offsets_x, recv_sizes, input_offsets_x, send_sizes, axis_name="expert"
   419	    )
   420	    # Rows this a2a overwrote took their value from ``out_dispatch``, so the pass-through
   421	    # cotangent to ``returned`` is zeroed on exactly the written intervals. This mirrors jax's
   422	    # transpose rule op for op (interval marks, cumsum, integer select_n) so the behavior is
   423	    # bit-identical, including on degenerate empty-group offset patterns.
   424	    interval_marks = (
   425	        jnp.zeros(cotangent.shape[0], jnp.int32).at[output_offsets_x].set(1).at[output_offsets_x + recv_sizes].add(-1)
   426	    )
   427	    written = jnp.broadcast_to(jnp.cumsum(interval_marks)[:, None], cotangent.shape)
   428	    passthrough_zero = _loop_local_zeros(cotangent.shape[0], cotangent.shape[1], cotangent.dtype, send_sizes, site=4)
   429	    returned_ct = jax.lax.select_n(written, cotangent, passthrough_zero)
   430	    return out_dispatch_ct, returned_ct, None, None, None, None
   431	
   432	
   433	_return_ragged_a2a.defvjp(_return_ragged_a2a_fwd, _return_ragged_a2a_bwd)
   434	
   435	
   436	def _resolve_expert_chunks(expert_chunks: int | None, local_experts: int) -> int:
   437	    """Sequential chunk count for a bank of ``local_experts``.
   438	
   439	    ``None`` takes `RAGGED_DEFAULT_EXPERT_CHUNKS` and falls back to one chunk on a bank the
   440	    default does not divide, which is how a mesh holding a single local expert runs. An explicit
   441	    count is a measurement knob, so an indivisible one raises instead of quietly running -- and
   442	    reporting -- a different chunk count than the one that was asked for.
   443	    """
   444	    if expert_chunks is None:
   445	        return RAGGED_DEFAULT_EXPERT_CHUNKS if local_experts % RAGGED_DEFAULT_EXPERT_CHUNKS == 0 else 1
   446	    if expert_chunks < 1:
   447	        raise ValueError(f"expert_chunks must be positive, got {expert_chunks}")
   448	    if local_experts % expert_chunks != 0:
   449	        raise ValueError(f"expert_chunks={expert_chunks} must divide the local expert count={local_experts}")
   450	    return expert_chunks
   451	
   452	
   453	def _resolve_receiver_alignment(receiver_alignment: int | None) -> int:
   454	    """Row alignment the receiver buffer's expert groups start on.
   455	
   456	    ``None`` is the unaligned layout: groups are packed back to back and the cuDNN
   457	    weight-gradient wrapper copies both of its operands into an aligned buffer itself. Any other
   458	    value lays the groups out aligned at the source and deletes those copies, which is only
   459	    sound if the value is a multiple of what that kernel requires.
   460	    """
   461	    if receiver_alignment is None:
   462	        return 1
   463	    if receiver_alignment < 1:
   464	        raise ValueError(f"receiver_alignment must be positive, got {receiver_alignment}")
   465	    if receiver_alignment % RAGGED_CUDNN_RECEIVER_ALIGNMENT != 0:
   466	        raise ValueError(
   467	            f"receiver_alignment={receiver_alignment} must be a multiple of "
   468	            f"{RAGGED_CUDNN_RECEIVER_ALIGNMENT}, the cuDNN grouped weight-gradient group alignment"
   469	        )
   470	    return receiver_alignment
   471	
   472	
   473	def _moe_mlp_ep_ragged_a2a_local(
   474	    x_local: Float[Array, "Tlocal H"],
   475	    selected_experts_local: Int[Array, "Tlocal K"],
   476	    combine_weights_local: Float[Array, "Tlocal K"],
   477	    moe_w13_local: Float[Array, "Elocal H I2"],
   478	    moe_w2_local: Float[Array, "Elocal I H"],
   479	    *,
   480	    activation_fn: Callable[[jax.Array], jax.Array],
   481	    num_experts: int,
   482	    capacity_factor: float,
   483	    expert_chunks: int | None = None,
   484	    receiver_alignment: int | None = None,
   485	) -> tuple[Float[Array, "Tlocal H"], CapacityOverflow]:
   486	    local_experts = moe_w13_local.shape[0]
   487	    if num_experts % local_experts != 0:
   488	        raise ValueError(
   489	            f"num_experts={num_experts} must be divisible by local expert count={local_experts} in EP mode"
   490	        )
   491	
   492	    shard_id = jax.lax.axis_index("expert")
   493	    ep_size = num_experts // local_experts
   494	    tokens_per_shard = x_local.shape[0]
   495	    topk = selected_experts_local.shape[1]
   496	    assignments_per_shard = tokens_per_shard * topk
   497	    local_capacity = int(math.ceil(capacity_factor * assignments_per_shard))
   498	    local_capacity = max(local_experts, local_capacity)
   499	
   500	    # Local experts are processed in sequential chunks so only one chunk's buffers are live at a
   501	    # time: capacity splits evenly across chunks, so two chunks halve the [C, H] transport
   502	    # buffers and the expert MLP's [C, I2] gate-up intermediate that sit between them. It also
   503	    # makes drop clipping per-chunk, which is a routing difference, not just a memory one.
   504	    #
   505	    # What chunking does not change is what crosses the forward/backward boundary. The block's
   506	    # remat policy re-runs this function in the backward, so the lowered module carries every
   507	    # ragged all-to-all three times at any chunk count -- primal, backward recompute, transpose,
   508	    # verified in the lowered StableHLO: 12 ops at two chunks, 6 at one. The a2a outputs are
   509	    # transient inside a chunk, not residuals pinned across the block window.
   510	    chunks = _resolve_expert_chunks(expert_chunks, local_experts)
   511	    chunk_experts = local_experts // chunks
   512	    chunk_capacity = max(chunk_experts, int(math.ceil(local_capacity / chunks)))
   513	    hidden_dim = x_local.shape[1]
   514	
   515	    # Aligning the receiver's expert groups costs up to `alignment - 1` unwritten rows per group
   516	    # in the chunk. Those rows are buffer, not capacity: the clip below still admits
   517	    # `chunk_capacity` rows, so no assignment is accepted or dropped differently.
   518	    alignment = _resolve_receiver_alignment(receiver_alignment)
   519	    receiver_rows = chunk_capacity + (alignment - 1) * chunk_experts
   520	
   521	    with jax.named_scope("dispatch"):
   522	        flat_selected = selected_experts_local.reshape(-1)  # [TK]
   523	        sorted_indices = tree_checkpoint_name(jnp.argsort(flat_selected), RAGGED_SORTED_INDICES_REMAT_NAME)  # [TK]
   524	        group_sizes = tree_checkpoint_name(
   525	            jnp.bincount(flat_selected, length=num_experts).astype(jnp.int32), RAGGED_GROUP_SIZES_REMAT_NAME
   526	        )  # [E]
   527	        sorted_x = _gather_dispatch_rows(x_local, sorted_indices, topk)  # [TK, H]
   528	        all_group_sizes = jax.lax.all_gather(group_sizes, "expert")  # [S, E]
   529	
   530	    expert_mlp = _select_expert_mlp(activation_fn, receiver_alignment=alignment)
   531	    chunk_of_expert = (jnp.arange(num_experts, dtype=jnp.int32) % local_experts) // chunk_experts  # [E]
   532	    # Built per-iteration (not jnp.zeros) so the layer scan does not re-copy a hoisted
   533	    # constant into the in-place return a2a's output slot every step; see _loop_local_zeros.
   534	    # The zeros are load-bearing: rows no peer writes back must read 0 in the combine.
   535	    returned = _loop_local_zeros(assignments_per_shard, hidden_dim, x_local.dtype, group_sizes, site=5)  # [TK, H]
   536	    accepted_local = jnp.zeros((), dtype=jnp.int32)
   537	    for chunk_index in range(chunks):
   538	        with jax.named_scope(f"moe_chunk_{chunk_index}"):
   539	            chunk_all_group_sizes = jnp.where(chunk_of_expert[None, :] == chunk_index, all_group_sizes, 0)  # [S, E]
   540	            clipped_group_sizes = _clip_receiver_group_sizes(
   541	                chunk_all_group_sizes,
   542	                local_expert_size=local_experts,
   543	                receiver_capacity=chunk_capacity,
   544	            )
   545	            # Sender starts come from the full (unmasked) sizes, so each chunk reads its
   546	            # groups' accepted prefixes in place in the shared sorted buffer.
   547	            dispatch_params, return_params = _expert_granular_a2a_params(
   548	                all_group_sizes,
   549	                clipped_group_sizes,
   550	                shard_id,
   551	                local_expert_size=local_experts,
   552	                receiver_alignment=alignment,
   553	            )
   554	            # Serialize the chunks. Without this barrier, the scheduler can start the dispatch
   555	            # of every chunk at the same time. This causes the high memory use that the chunks
   556	            # prevent. A variant that overlaps one transport with the MLP stays within memory.
   557	            # But it does not increase the speed. The transport and the MLP compete for the
   558	            # same SMs.
   559	            chunk_source, _ = jax.lax.optimization_barrier((sorted_x, returned))
   560	            # Accepted rows are the prefix of each unclipped expert group and receiver offsets
   561	            # pack arrivals expert-major, so the received buffer feeds the grouped MLP
   562	            # directly: no sender compaction and no receiver-side permute.
   563	            x_dispatch = _dispatch_ragged_a2a(  # [C, H]
   564	                receiver_rows,
   565	                assignments_per_shard,
   566	                chunk_source,
   567	                *dispatch_params,
   568	            )
   569	            active_all = jnp.sum(  # [Elocal]
   570	                clipped_group_sizes.reshape(ep_size, ep_size, local_experts)[:, shard_id, :], axis=0
   571	            )
   572	            # The group extents the receiver buffer was actually laid out on -- the arrival counts
   573	            # under no alignment, and their rounded-up extents otherwise. The a2a rounds the same
   574	            # per-expert totals the same way, so the two layouts agree by construction.
   575	            active_group_sizes = _align_up_rows(
   576	                active_all[chunk_index * chunk_experts : (chunk_index + 1) * chunk_experts], alignment
   577	            )  # [Echunk]
   578	            total_valid = jnp.sum(active_group_sizes, dtype=jnp.int32)
   579	            physical_group_sizes = active_group_sizes.at[-1].add(receiver_rows - total_valid)  # [Echunk]
   580	            out_dispatch = expert_mlp(  # [C, H]
   581	                x_dispatch,
   582	                moe_w13_local[chunk_index * chunk_experts : (chunk_index + 1) * chunk_experts],
   583	                moe_w2_local[chunk_index * chunk_experts : (chunk_index + 1) * chunk_experts],
   584	                physical_group_sizes,
   585	                active_group_sizes,
   586	                activation_fn,
   587	            )
   588	            # The mirror of dispatch: valid prefixes land back at unclipped sorted positions.
   589	            # Chaining every chunk through one output buffer composes the disjoint writes;
   590	            # dropped rows keep the buffer's zeros, so the final gather-sum reads dropped
   591	            # slots as zero contributions with no expansion step.
   592	            returned = _return_ragged_a2a(
   593	                receiver_rows,
   594	                out_dispatch,
   595	                returned,
   596	                *return_params,
   597	            )
   598	            accepted_local = accepted_local + jnp.sum(clipped_group_sizes[shard_id], dtype=jnp.int32)
   599	
   600	    with jax.named_scope("combine"):
   601	        out_local = _unpermute_from_global_expert(
   602	            returned,
   603	            sorted_indices,
   604	            combine_weights_local,
   605	            tokens_per_shard=tokens_per_shard,
   606	            topk=topk,
   607	        ).astype(x_local.dtype)
   608	        dropped_local = jnp.sum(group_sizes, dtype=jnp.int32) - accepted_local
   609	        dropped_total = jax.lax.psum(dropped_local, _batch_axes(jax.sharding.get_abstract_mesh()))
   610	    return out_local, CapacityOverflow(sender=dropped_total, receiver=jnp.zeros_like(dropped_total))

    13	def _sort_activations(inputs: Float[Array, "N *tail"], sort_indices: Int[Array, "N"]) -> Float[Array, "N *tail"]:
    14	    if inputs.shape[0] != sort_indices.shape[0]:
    15	        raise ValueError(f"Expected matching leading dims, got {inputs.shape[0]} and {sort_indices.shape[0]}")
    16	    return _sort_activations_custom(inputs, sort_indices)

    20	def _sort_activations_custom(
    21	    inputs: Float[Array, "N *tail"], sort_indices: Int[Array, "N"]
    22	) -> Float[Array, "N *tail"]:
    23	    return inputs[sort_indices, ...]

    27	    inputs: Float[Array, "N *tail"], sort_indices: Int[Array, "N"]
    28	) -> tuple[Float[Array, "N *tail"], Int[Array, "N"]]:
    29	    return _sort_activations_custom(inputs, sort_indices), sort_indices
    30	
    31	
    32	def _sort_activations_custom_bwd(
    33	    residuals: Int[Array, "N"], grads: Float[Array, "N *tail"]
    34	) -> tuple[Float[Array, "N *tail"], None]:
    35	    sort_indices = residuals
    36	    return _sort_activations_custom(grads, jnp.argsort(sort_indices)), None
    37	
    38	
    39	_sort_activations_custom.defvjp(_sort_activations_custom_fwd, _sort_activations_custom_bwd)

    42	def _ranks_within_groups(group_ids: Int[Array, "N"], *, num_groups: int) -> Int[Array, "N"]:
    43	    """Return the zero-based rank of each item in its group."""
    44	    order = jnp.argsort(group_ids, stable=True)
    45	    inverse_order = jnp.argsort(order)
    46	    counts = jnp.bincount(group_ids, length=num_groups).astype(jnp.int32)
    47	    starts = jnp.cumsum(counts) - counts
    48	    sorted_ranks = jnp.arange(group_ids.shape[0], dtype=jnp.int32) - starts[group_ids[order]]
    49	    return sorted_ranks[inverse_order]
    50	
    51	
    52	def _assignment_sources(
    53	    linear_indices: Int[Array, "N"],
    54	    *,
    55	    send_size: int,
    56	) -> Int[Array, "send"]:
    57	    """Map each fixed send slot to its source assignment."""
    58	    assignments = linear_indices.shape[0]
    59	    return (
    60	        jnp.full((send_size,), assignments, dtype=jnp.int32)
    61	        .at[linear_indices]
    62	        .set(jnp.arange(assignments, dtype=jnp.int32), mode="drop")
    63	    )
    64	
    65	
    66	def _token_sources(
    67	    assignment_sources: Int[Array, "send"],
    68	    *,
    69	    assignments: int,
    70	    topk: int,
    71	    tokens: int,
    72	) -> Int[Array, "send"]:
    73	    """Map send slots to token rows and use the padding row for empty slots."""
    74	    return jnp.where(
    75	        assignment_sources < assignments,
    76	        assignment_sources // topk,
    77	        tokens,
    78	    )
    79	
    80	
    81	def _prefix_cap_counts(counts: Int[Array, "E"], *, capacity: int) -> Int[Array, "E"]:
    82	    accepted = []
    83	    remaining = jnp.array(capacity, dtype=jnp.int32)
    84	    for expert in range(int(counts.shape[0])):
    85	        take = jnp.minimum(counts[expert], remaining)
    86	        accepted.append(take)
    87	        remaining = jnp.maximum(remaining - take, 0)
    88	    return jnp.stack(accepted, axis=0)
    89	
    90	
    91	def _clip_receiver_group_sizes(
    92	    global_group_sizes: Int[Array, "S E"],
    93	    *,
    94	    local_expert_size: int,
    95	    receiver_capacity: int,
    96	) -> Int[Array, "S E"]:
    97	    """Clip sender->expert group sizes so each receiver shard stays within capacity."""
    98	    num_senders = int(global_group_sizes.shape[0])
    99	    num_experts = int(global_group_sizes.shape[1])
   100	    if num_experts % local_expert_size != 0:
   101	        raise ValueError(f"num_experts={num_experts} must be divisible by local_expert_size={local_expert_size}")
   102	    num_receivers = num_experts // local_expert_size
   103	    if num_receivers != num_senders:
   104	        raise ValueError(f"sender/receiver shard mismatch: num_senders={num_senders}, num_receivers={num_receivers}")
   105	
   106	    clipped_by_receiver: list[jax.Array] = []
   107	    for receiver_index in range(num_receivers):
   108	        start = receiver_index * local_expert_size
   109	        stop = start + local_expert_size
   110	        receiver_counts = global_group_sizes[:, start:stop]
   111	        receiver_totals = jnp.sum(receiver_counts, axis=0, dtype=jnp.int32)
   112	        accepted_totals = _prefix_cap_counts(receiver_totals, capacity=receiver_capacity)
   113	        remaining = accepted_totals
   114	        accepted_rows: list[jax.Array] = []
   115	        for sender_index in range(num_senders):
   116	            # Greedy first-sender-wins: earlier shards get priority when capacity is scarce.
   117	            accepted = jnp.minimum(receiver_counts[sender_index], remaining)
   118	            accepted_rows.append(accepted)
   119	            remaining = remaining - accepted
   120	        clipped_by_receiver.append(jnp.stack(accepted_rows, axis=0))
   121	
   122	    return jnp.concatenate(clipped_by_receiver, axis=1)
   123	
   124	
   125	def _align_up_rows(values: Int[Array, "..."], alignment: int) -> Int[Array, "..."]:
   126	    """Round each row count up to a multiple of ``alignment``.
   127	
   128	    ``alignment == 1`` returns the input array itself, so a caller that leaves alignment off
   129	    emits no arithmetic at all and traces exactly the graph it traced before this existed.
   130	    """
   131	    if alignment < 1:
   132	        raise ValueError(f"alignment must be positive, got {alignment}")
   133	    if alignment == 1:
   134	        return values
   135	    return ((values + alignment - 1) // alignment) * alignment
   136	
   137	
   138	class ExpertA2aParams(NamedTuple):
   139	    """Offset/size vectors for one direction of an expert-granular ``ragged_all_to_all``."""
   140	
   141	    input_offsets: Int[Array, "U"]
   142	    send_sizes: Int[Array, "U"]
   143	    output_offsets: Int[Array, "U"]
   144	    recv_sizes: Int[Array, "U"]
   145	
   146	
   147	def _expert_granular_a2a_params(
   148	    all_group_sizes: Int[Array, "S E"],
   149	    clipped_group_sizes: Int[Array, "S E"],
   150	    shard_id: Int[Array, ""],
   151	    *,
   152	    local_expert_size: int,
   153	    receiver_alignment: int = 1,
   154	) -> tuple[ExpertA2aParams, ExpertA2aParams]:
   155	    """Build dispatch and return ``ragged_all_to_all`` parameters at (peer, expert) granularity.
   156	
   157	    One update per (destination shard, local expert). Sender reads each global-expert
   158	    group at its *unclipped* offset with its *clipped* size, so accepted rows need no
   159	    compaction: they are the prefix of each group. Receiver offsets pack arriving rows
   160	    expert-major (sender-major within each expert), so the received buffer needs no local
   161	    permute before the grouped MLP. The return direction is the exact mirror: it reads the
   162	    expert-major receiver buffer and writes valid prefixes back to the sender's unclipped
   163	    positions, leaving dropped rows at the output operand's values.
   164	
   165	    ``receiver_alignment`` rounds each receiver group's *extent* up to a multiple of that many
   166	    rows, which starts every group on an aligned row and leaves up to ``alignment - 1`` unwritten
   167	    rows between groups. It changes only where the receiver puts each group: senders read the
   168	    same rows and send the same sizes, the accepted set is untouched, and the return direction
   169	    reads the same valid prefixes back out. The receiver buffer must then hold
   170	    ``capacity + (alignment - 1) * groups`` rows, since the per-group slack is charged to the
   171	    buffer rather than to the capacity that decides drops.
   172	    """
   173	    num_shards = all_group_sizes.shape[0]
   174	
   175	    # [src, dest, e]: rows sender `src` contributes to `dest`'s local expert `e`.
   176	    clipped = clipped_group_sizes.reshape(num_shards, num_shards, local_expert_size)
   177	
   178	    # Sender side: unclipped group starts in this shard's expert-sorted buffer.
   179	    unclipped_starts = jnp.cumsum(all_group_sizes, axis=1) - all_group_sizes
   180	    my_send = clipped[shard_id]  # [dest, e]
   181	    dispatch_input_offsets = unclipped_starts[shard_id].reshape(num_shards, local_expert_size)
   182	
   183	    # Receiver side: expert-major segment starts on each destination, sender-major within.
   184	    dest_totals = jnp.sum(clipped, axis=0)  # [dest, e]
   185	    group_extents = _align_up_rows(dest_totals, receiver_alignment)  # [dest, e]
   186	    expert_starts = jnp.cumsum(group_extents, axis=1) - group_extents
   187	    senders_before_me = (jnp.cumsum(clipped, axis=0) - clipped)[shard_id]  # [dest, e]
   188	    dispatch_output_offsets = expert_starts + senders_before_me
   189	
   190	    # What each source sends this shard, source-major -- also the return direction's sends.
   191	    inbound = clipped[:, shard_id, :]  # [src, e]
   192	
   193	    dispatch = ExpertA2aParams(
   194	        dispatch_input_offsets.reshape(-1),
   195	        my_send.reshape(-1),
   196	        dispatch_output_offsets.reshape(-1),
   197	        inbound.reshape(-1),
   198	    )
   199	
   200	    # Return: read this shard's expert-major receiver buffer, write back to each original
   201	    # sender's unclipped sorted positions for the experts this shard owns.
   202	    my_expert_starts = expert_starts[shard_id]  # [e]
   203	    senders_before = jnp.cumsum(inbound, axis=0) - inbound  # [src, e]
   204	    return_input_offsets = my_expert_starts[None, :] + senders_before
   205	    my_global_experts = jnp.arange(local_expert_size, dtype=jnp.int32) + shard_id * local_expert_size
   206	    return_output_offsets = unclipped_starts[:, my_global_experts]  # [src, e]
   207	
   208	    ret = ExpertA2aParams(
   209	        return_input_offsets.reshape(-1),
   210	        inbound.reshape(-1),
   211	        return_output_offsets.reshape(-1),
   212	        my_send.reshape(-1),
   213	    )
   214	    return dispatch, ret

 ...  133 class ResidentDonation(StrEnum):
 ...  134     """Donation policy for the device-resident expert momentum leaves (diagnostic).
 ...  135 
 ...  136     DONATED donates the whole train state into the step, the original behavior. EXCLUDED passes
 ...  137     the resident momentum leaves as a separate, non-donated argument, so XLA can neither alias
 ...  138     them to an output nor reuse their buffers as scratch, and adds a per-step canary checksum of
 ...  139     each resident leaf (``debug/resident_ck_in`` / ``debug/resident_ck_out``). This discriminates
 ...  140     the k=1 NaN hypotheses: S1 (donation-enabled buffer reuse clobbers the leaf under the async
 ...  141     offload schedule) from S2 (a stray transport write lands in the leaf's address range
 ...  142     regardless of donation). EXCLUDED costs one extra device copy of each resident leaf per step
 ...  143     (the un-donated input and the fresh output coexist: +10.87 GiB transient per leaf at d6144
 ...  144     EP64, predicted peak ~134 GiB at k=1 -- near the 138.2 GiB threshold; watch for #8490
 ...  145     allocator churn).
 ...  146     """
 ...  147

 ...  170 def checkpoint_stores_master(candidate: str) -> bool:
 ...  171     """Whether checkpoint ``candidate``'s manifest lists fp32 master parameters.
 ...  172 
 ...  173     A missing manifest raises ``FileNotFoundError``, which restore treats like any other
 ...  174     unreadable candidate.
 ...  175     """
 ...  176     manifest = read_manifest(candidate)
 ...  177     if manifest is None:
 ...  178         raise FileNotFoundError(f"{candidate} has no manifest.json, so its layout cannot be read")
 ...  179     markers = (MASTER_PARAMS_KEY, f"{LEGACY_STATE_KEY}/{MASTER_PARAMS_KEY}")
 ...  180     return any(path == marker or path.startswith(marker + "/") for path in manifest.array_paths for marker in markers)
 ...  181 
 ...  182 
 ...  183 def template_for_candidate_layout(
 ...  184     state: "GrugTrainState", candidate: str, run_mode: MasterParamMode
 ...  185 ) -> "GrugTrainState":
 ...  186     """Pick the template restore reads checkpoint ``candidate`` with.
 ...  187 
 ...  188     Restore reads only the leaves the template names and takes each dtype from storage, checking
 ...  189     neither against the checkpoint, so reading a master-bearing checkpoint with the run's own
 ...  190     master-less template would silently return the bf16 compute copy. When the layouts match the
 ...  191     template is ``state`` itself. A master-bearing checkpoint read by a master-less run migrates
 ...  192     in process: the run's device fp32 ``params`` template is presented under ``master_params``, so
 ...  193     the checkpoint's authoritative fp32 master loads directly into it and the bf16 copy goes
 ...  194     unread; ``take_master_as_params`` then moves it back, and the next save writes the new layout.
 ...  195     """
 ...  196     has_master = checkpoint_stores_master(candidate)
 ...  197     if has_master == (run_mode != MasterParamMode.DEVICE):
 ...  198         return state
 ...  199     if not has_master:
 ...  200         raise ValueError(
 ...  201             f"checkpoint {candidate} stores no master parameters, but this run trains with {run_mode}. "
 ...  202             "Synthesizing a master from stored weights is not a conversion this supports."
 ...  203         )
 ...  204     logger.info("Checkpoint %s stores a pinned-host fp32 master; restoring it as the parameters.", candidate)
 ...  205     return dataclasses.replace(state, params=None, master_params=state.params)
 ...  206 
 ...  207 
 ...  208 def take_master_as_params(state: "GrugTrainState") -> "GrugTrainState":
 ...  209     """Move a master restored through ``template_for_candidate_layout`` into ``params``."""
 ...  210     if state.master_params is None:
 ...  211         return state
 ...  212     return dataclasses.replace(state, params=state.master_params, master_params=None)

 605  715     return jax.tree.map(_move, tree)

 ...  718 def _opt_state_offload_mask(opt_state, resident_expert_leaves: int):
 ...  719     """Boolean tree over ``opt_state``: True where an offloaded leaf moves to pinned host.
 ...  720 
 ...  721     The first ``resident_expert_leaves`` 4D leaves stay on device. Rank 4 identifies the
 ...  722     stacked expert momentum shards exactly: the expert matrices are the model's only 4D
 ...  723     parameters (scan stacking prepends a layer axis to the per-layer ``(experts, in, out)``
 ...  724     weights), so their optimizer moments are the only 4D optimizer leaves; every other
 ...  725     moment is 3D or smaller. ``jax.tree.flatten`` orders leaves by dataclass/NamedTuple
 ...  726     field declaration order and sorted dict keys, both fixed by the code alone, so
 ...  727     "first k" names the same shards on every process, step, and restart. For the hero
 ...  728     MuonH state that order is the ``MoEExpertMlp`` field order: ``w_gate``, ``w_up``,
 ...  729     ``w_down``.
 ...  730     """
 ...  731     paths_and_leaves, treedef = jax.tree_util.tree_flatten_with_path(opt_state)
 ...  732     leaves = [leaf for _, leaf in paths_and_leaves]
 ...  733     expert_indices = [index for index, leaf in enumerate(leaves) if getattr(leaf, "ndim", None) == 4]
 ...  734     if not 0 <= resident_expert_leaves <= len(expert_indices):
 ...  735         raise ValueError(
 ...  736             f"opt_state_resident_expert_leaves={resident_expert_leaves} must lie in "
 ...  737             f"[0, {len(expert_indices)}]: the optimizer state has {len(expert_indices)} 4D expert leaves."
 ...  738         )
 ...  739     if resident_expert_leaves:
 ...  740         # Fail closed on structure drift: residency is meaningful only while the 4D leaves are
 ...  741         # exactly the three muonh expert momentum shards in field order. A new 4D accumulator or
 ...  742         # model field would silently redirect which shard stays resident otherwise.
 ...  743         expert_path_names = ["/".join(str(k) for k in paths_and_leaves[i][0]) for i in expert_indices]
 ...  744         expected = ("w_gate", "w_up", "w_down")
 ...  745         tails = tuple(name.rsplit("/", 1)[-1].strip("'.[]") for name in expert_path_names)
 ...  746         if len(tails) != len(expected) or tuple(tails) != expected:
 ...  747             raise ValueError(
 ...  748                 "opt_state 4D-leaf structure drifted: expected exactly the muonh expert momentum "
 ...  749                 f"shards {expected} in field order, found {expert_path_names}. Re-derive the "
 ...  750                 "residency selection before trusting resident_expert_leaves."
 ...  751             )
 ...  752     resident = set(expert_indices[:resident_expert_leaves])
 ...  753     return jax.tree.unflatten(treedef, [index not in resident for index in range(len(leaves))])

 ...  758     return jax.tree.map(
 ...  759         lambda leaf, offload: _tree_to_memory_kind(leaf, memory_kind) if offload else leaf,
 ...  760         opt_state,
 ...  761         offload_mask,

 ...  765 def _split_resident_opt_state(opt_state, resident_expert_leaves: int):
 ...  766     """Partition ``opt_state`` into (offloaded-only, resident-only) trees with None placeholders."""
 ...  767     offload_mask = _opt_state_offload_mask(opt_state, resident_expert_leaves)
 ...  768     return eqx.partition(opt_state, offload_mask)

 ...  771 _UNSIGNED_BY_ITEMSIZE = {2: jnp.uint16, 4: jnp.uint32}
 ...  772 
 ...  773 
 ...  774 def _bitcast_u32_checksum(leaf: jax.Array) -> jax.Array:
 ...  775     """Wraparound uint32 sum of the leaf's raw bits.
 ...  776 
 ...  777     Exact integer addition mod 2**32 is associative and commutative, so the result is
 ...  778     deterministic across shardings and reduction orders. Detection is probabilistic, not
 ...  779     certain: a modulo sum admits additive cancellations and equal-sum rewrites, which is
 ...  780     acceptable for the large or random clobbers this canary exists to catch.
 ...  781     """
 ...  782     bits = jax.lax.bitcast_convert_type(leaf, _UNSIGNED_BY_ITEMSIZE[leaf.dtype.itemsize])
 ...  783     return jnp.sum(bits.astype(jnp.uint32), dtype=jnp.uint32)
 ...  784

 ...  786 def _resident_canary_metrics(prefix: str, opt_state, offload_mask) -> dict[str, jax.Array]:
 ...  787     """Checksum each device-resident optimizer leaf (False in ``offload_mask``) under ``prefix``.
 ...  788 
 ...  789     In-graph cost is one memory-bound reduce per resident leaf (~10.9 GiB per device shard at
 ...  790     d6144 EP64, roughly 2-3 ms per leaf per direction).
 ...  791     """
 ...  792     paths_and_leaves, _ = jax.tree_util.tree_flatten_with_path(opt_state)
 ...  793     mask_leaves = jax.tree.leaves(offload_mask)
 ...  794     metrics: dict[str, jax.Array] = {}
 ...  795     for (path, leaf), offloaded in zip(paths_and_leaves, mask_leaves, strict=True):
 ...  796         if offloaded:
 ...  797             continue
 ...  798         tail = str(path[-1]).strip("'.[]")
 ...  799         metrics[f"{prefix}/{tail}"] = _bitcast_u32_checksum(leaf)
 ...  800     return metrics

 ... 1046 class _ResidentExcludedTrainStep:
 ... 1047     """Train step that passes the resident momentum leaves as a separate, non-donated argument.
 ... 1048 
 ... 1049     Donation is per-argument, so splitting the resident leaves out of the donated state is what
 ... 1050     removes them from XLA's input/output alias set; ``jit_train_step`` is exposed so tests and
 ... 1051     diagnostics can inspect the lowering's aliasing directly.
 ... 1052     """
 ... 1053 
 ... 1054     def __init__(self, jit_train_step, resident_expert_leaves: int):
 ... 1055         self.jit_train_step = jit_train_step
 ... 1056         self._resident_expert_leaves = resident_expert_leaves
 ... 1057 
 ... 1058     def __call__(self, state: GrugTrainState, batch):
 ... 1059         offloaded_opt, resident_opt = _split_resident_opt_state(state.opt_state, self._resident_expert_leaves)
 ... 1060         donated = dataclasses.replace(state, opt_state=offloaded_opt)
 ... 1061         return self.jit_train_step(donated, resident_opt, batch)

210 223 _gather_dispatch_rows.defvjp(_gather_dispatch_rows_fwd, _gather_dispatch_rows_bwd)

... 226 def _loop_local_zeros(
... 227     rows: int, hidden_dim: int, dtype, tie: Int[Array, "..."], site: int = 0
... 228 ) -> Float[Array, "rows H"]:
... 229     """Zero buffer for an in-place ``ragged_all_to_all`` output slot, built so XLA never copies it.
... 230 
... 231     ``ragged_all_to_all`` writes its result in place into the output-init operand. A literal
... 232     ``jnp.zeros`` init is a trace-time constant: it gets hoisted out of the layer scan (and
... 233     identical inits CSE together), so CopyInsertion must mint a fresh multi-GB device copy of
... 234     the pristine zeros into the a2a's output slot on every scan iteration. Deriving the zeros
... 235     from ``tie`` -- a per-site, per-iteration traced value -- keeps each init inside the loop
... 236     body and distinct from every other init, so it lowers to one write-only fill kernel whose
... 237     buffer the a2a updates directly.
... 238 
... 239     ``tie`` must be a non-negative integer array (group or transfer sizes): with ``site >= 0``,
... 240     ``min(tie[0], -site) + site`` is exactly zero at runtime but not foldable at compile time.
... 241 
... 242     ``site`` must be distinct per call site. Two sites can hold the SAME tie tensor without it
... 243     being obvious (dispatch send_sizes and return recv_sizes are one tensor in ep_common), and
... 244     same-shape same-tie fills CSE into one value with two destructive in-place a2a consumers --
... 245     which makes CopyInsertion mint back the multi-GB copy this helper exists to prevent.
... 246     """
... 247     zero = (jnp.minimum(tie.reshape(-1)[0], -site) + site).astype(dtype)
... 248     return jax.lax.broadcast(zero, (rows, hidden_dim))
... 249 
... 250 
... 251 @functools.partial(jax.custom_vjp, nondiff_argnums=(0, 1))
... 252 def _dispatch_ragged_a2a(
... 253     capacity: int,
... 254     source_rows: int,
... 255     chunk_source: Float[Array, "TK H"],
... 256     input_offsets: Int[Array, "U"],
... 257     send_sizes: Int[Array, "U"],
... 258     output_offsets: Int[Array, "U"],
... 259     recv_sizes: Int[Array, "U"],
... 260 ) -> Float[Array, "C H"]:
... 261     """Dispatch-direction ``ragged_all_to_all`` into a freshly zeroed receiver buffer.
... 262 
... 263     Owning the output-init here (instead of taking a caller-built ``jnp.zeros``) lets both the
... 264     primal and the transposed direction build their inits with `_loop_local_zeros`. jax's
... 265     built-in transpose rule inits the swapped a2a with plain zeros, which XLA hoists out of
... 266     the layer loop and re-copies every iteration; the custom vjp below is that same rule with
... 267     the init construction replaced. Zeros stay load-bearing: receiver rows no peer writes must
... 268     read 0 downstream, and dropped source rows must read a 0 cotangent in the backward.
... 269     """
... 270     del source_rows
... 271     output_init = _loop_local_zeros(capacity, chunk_source.shape[1], chunk_source.dtype, send_sizes, site=1)
... 272     return jax.lax.ragged_all_to_all(
... 273         chunk_source, output_init, input_offsets, send_sizes, output_offsets, recv_sizes, axis_name="expert"
... 274     )

... 283     output_offsets: Int[Array, "U"],
... 284     recv_sizes: Int[Array, "U"],
... 285 ) -> tuple[Float[Array, "C H"], tuple[jax.Array, jax.Array, jax.Array, jax.Array]]:
... 286     result = _dispatch_ragged_a2a(
... 287         capacity, source_rows, chunk_source, input_offsets, send_sizes, output_offsets, recv_sizes
... 288     )
... 289     return result, (input_offsets, send_sizes, output_offsets, recv_sizes)

... 291 
... 292 def _dispatch_ragged_a2a_bwd(
... 293     capacity: int,
... 294     source_rows: int,
... 295     residuals: tuple[jax.Array, jax.Array, jax.Array, jax.Array],
... 296     cotangent: Float[Array, "C H"],
... 297 ) -> tuple[Float[Array, "TK H"], None, None, None, None]:
... 298     del capacity
... 299     input_offsets, send_sizes, output_offsets, recv_sizes = residuals
... 300     # The transpose of a ragged all-to-all is the reverse ragged all-to-all: swap the send and
... 301     # recv roles and exchange the offset vectors across shards, exactly as jax's transpose rule
... 302     # does. Source rows that were clipped receive no cotangent and keep the init's zeros.
... 303     output_offsets_x = jax.lax.all_to_all(output_offsets, "expert", 0, 0, tiled=True)
... 304     input_offsets_x = jax.lax.all_to_all(input_offsets, "expert", 0, 0, tiled=True)
... 305     # Tie to this side's send_sizes, not recv_sizes: the return path's passthrough fill ties to
... 306     # its own send_sizes, which is the SAME tensor as this dispatch's recv_sizes, and two fills
... 307     # with identical shape and tie CSE back into one value with a destructive consumer --
... 308     # re-minting exactly the copy this construction removes.
... 309     init = _loop_local_zeros(source_rows, cotangent.shape[1], cotangent.dtype, send_sizes, site=2)
... 310     source_ct = jax.lax.ragged_all_to_all(
... 311         cotangent, init, output_offsets_x, recv_sizes, input_offsets_x, send_sizes, axis_name="expert"
... 312     )
... 313     return source_ct, None, None, None, None

... 330 
... 331     Same construction as `_dispatch_ragged_a2a`: the primal is unchanged, and the custom vjp
... 332     replicates jax's transpose rule operation for operation, replacing only the transposed
... 333     a2a's zero init so it is built per-iteration instead of hoisted and copied.
... 334     """
... 335     del capacity
... 336     return jax.lax.ragged_all_to_all(
... 337         out_dispatch, returned, input_offsets, send_sizes, output_offsets, recv_sizes, axis_name="expert"
... 338     )

... 356 def _return_ragged_a2a_bwd(
... 357     capacity: int,
... 358     residuals: tuple[jax.Array, jax.Array, jax.Array, jax.Array],
... 359     cotangent: Float[Array, "TK H"],
... 360 ) -> tuple[Float[Array, "C H"], Float[Array, "TK H"], None, None, None, None]:
... 361     input_offsets, send_sizes, output_offsets, recv_sizes = residuals
... 362     output_offsets_x = jax.lax.all_to_all(output_offsets, "expert", 0, 0, tiled=True)
... 363     input_offsets_x = jax.lax.all_to_all(input_offsets, "expert", 0, 0, tiled=True)
... 364     init = _loop_local_zeros(capacity, cotangent.shape[1], cotangent.dtype, recv_sizes, site=3)
... 365     out_dispatch_ct = jax.lax.ragged_all_to_all(
... 366         cotangent, init, output_offsets_x, recv_sizes, input_offsets_x, send_sizes, axis_name="expert"
... 367     )
... 368     # Rows this a2a overwrote took their value from ``out_dispatch``, so the pass-through
... 369     # cotangent to ``returned`` is zeroed on exactly the written intervals. This mirrors jax's
... 370     # transpose rule op for op (interval marks, cumsum, integer select_n) so the behavior is
... 371     # bit-identical, including on degenerate empty-group offset patterns.
... 372     interval_marks = (
... 373         jnp.zeros(cotangent.shape[0], jnp.int32).at[output_offsets_x].set(1).at[output_offsets_x + recv_sizes].add(-1)
... 374     )
... 375     written = jnp.broadcast_to(jnp.cumsum(interval_marks)[:, None], cotangent.shape)
... 376     passthrough_zero = _loop_local_zeros(cotangent.shape[0], cotangent.shape[1], cotangent.dtype, send_sizes, site=4)
... 377     returned_ct = jax.lax.select_n(written, cotangent, passthrough_zero)
... 378     return out_dispatch_ct, returned_ct, None, None, None, None

... 384 def _resolve_expert_chunks(expert_chunks: int | None, local_experts: int) -> int:
... 385     """Sequential chunk count for a bank of ``local_experts``.
... 386 
... 387     ``None`` takes `RAGGED_DEFAULT_EXPERT_CHUNKS` and falls back to one chunk on a bank the
... 388     default does not divide, which is how a mesh holding a single local expert runs. An explicit
... 389     count is a measurement knob, so an indivisible one raises instead of quietly running -- and
... 390     reporting -- a different chunk count than the one that was asked for.
... 391     """
... 392     if expert_chunks is None:
... 393         return RAGGED_DEFAULT_EXPERT_CHUNKS if local_experts % RAGGED_DEFAULT_EXPERT_CHUNKS == 0 else 1
... 394     if expert_chunks < 1:
... 395         raise ValueError(f"expert_chunks must be positive, got {expert_chunks}")
... 396     if local_experts % expert_chunks != 0:
... 397         raise ValueError(f"expert_chunks={expert_chunks} must divide the local expert count={local_experts}")
... 398     return expert_chunks

55 .. def _interleave_gate_up(moe_w13: jax.Array, moe_dim: int) -> jax.Array:
56 ..     """grug w13 [E,H,2I] gate=[:I], up=[I:] -> interleaved [g0,u0,g1,u1,...] (QuACK layout)."""
57 ..     gate = moe_w13[..., :moe_dim]
58 ..     up = moe_w13[..., moe_dim:]
59 ..     return jnp.stack([gate, up], axis=-1).reshape(moe_w13.shape)
60 .. 
61 .. 
62 .. def _swiglu_gate_up_backward(gu: jax.Array, dh: jax.Array) -> jax.Array:
63 ..     """Cotangent of the interleaved gate/up pre-activations, given the SwiGLU output's."""
64 ..     gate, up = gu[:, 0::2], gu[:, 1::2]
65 ..     sg = jax.nn.sigmoid(gate)
66 ..     silu = gate * sg
67 ..     dgate = dh * up * (sg + silu * (1.0 - sg))
68 ..     dup = dh * silu
69 ..     return jnp.stack([dgate, dup], axis=-1).reshape(gu.shape)

{"baseRefName":"main","body":"Reworks the ragged all-to-all expert-parallel MoE backend into a replacement for the pooled-wave hero transport. In an A/B at the hero shape — both arms restored from the live hero's step-6000 checkpoint on real data, one NVL72 rack, transport the only variable — ragged delivers:\n\n- **matching-to-slightly-ahead throughput**: **22.87 vs 22.71 MFU**, with the two arms run back to back on the same rack so placement differences cannot account for the gap (standard deviation across the scored steps: 0.11 for ragged, 0.59 for pooled-wave; three earlier runs of the ragged configuration ranged 22.34–22.58)\n- **~150× lower drop rate**: **0.018%** vs 2.67% of expert assignments under the trained router, with the loss at the scored step correspondingly lower (1.4727 vs 1.4777)\n- **~12 GiB lower runtime device peak**: **137.9 vs 149.9 GiB** at identical steady-state footprint\n\nThis PR does not change the default backend: the `moe_hero_ep` entry points keep `fixed_pooled_wave_all_to_all`, and the ragged backend is opt-in via `moe_implementation=\"ragged_all_to_all\"`.\n\nKey changes:\n\n- **Expert-granular transport data path** — one `ragged_all_to_all` update per (peer, local expert): senders read each expert group's accepted prefix in place and rows arrive grouped by expert, replacing ~1.1 s/step of repeat/sort/compact permutes. With chunking, **+1.5 MFU** over the prior ragged path.\n- **Sequential expert chunks** — local experts run in two chunks with per-chunk capacity, halving the transport buffers XLA cannot rematerialize. Not a tuning choice: the unchunked graph needs 192–194 GiB against 184 GiB HBM and OOMs at the first hero step.\n- **QuACK SM100 grouped GEMMs + cuDNN grouped weight gradients** for the expert MLP — the core of the earlier **16.1% → 21.9%** stack. Those two figures were measured before the current protocol and are not directly comparable to the numbers above. SM100 + SiLU only; everything else keeps XLA's `ragged_dot`.\n- **Device-initiated transport** — the ragged backend engages XLA's device-initiated (NCCL LSA) ragged-all-to-all kernel through `XLA_FLAGS` defaults it sets itself. The kernel partitions copy work across CTAs by bytes, so splitting a peer transfer into several updates buys no load balance and only adds granularity cost (21.12 MFU when we measured it at 64 splits, against 22.34–22.58 unsplit). The backend therefore exposes no splitting option, and the two flags are not overridable: the host-launched kernel would need both flags cleared together plus the update splitting this backend does not produce, so a partial override would silently run a configuration nothing here measures.\n- **Fused combine gather + weighted sum** and a backend-specific scheduling posture (latency-hiding scheduler off, collective overlap 1) — part of the stack above. The scheduler is off for memory, not scheduling: its longer live ranges fail NCCL's first-step allocations at the current HBM budget, and a follow-up that offloads layer activations to pinned host re-enables it at a measured gain (#8317).\n- **`--master-params` option** — fp32 weights on device instead of a pinned-host master: **~+0.4 MFU**.\n- **Validation harness** — the 4-GPU `ragged_ep_check` gates forward and gradients against an exact fp32 dense reference, both at a capacity high enough that nothing is clipped and in the drop regime the hero actually trains in. For the latter it computes which assignments survive in NumPy — accepted rows are the prefix of each expert group under a greedy first-sender-wins gate, so the surviving set is a pure function of the routing and the capacity — and requires the transport to equal dense over exactly the rows it kept. It also records which kernels the run selected, since that depends on the device and the installed packages. Nothing runs it on a schedule, and it sits under `experiments/` rather than `tests/cluster/`, because the repository has no marker, fixture, or workflow for a test that needs particular accelerators (#8704). That same gap silences the two unit tests that exercise this backend end to end: both skip under CI's single CPU device, and `addopts` carries no `-rs`, so the skips do not appear in the output. Separately, a d768 ablation pair (10.8k steps, identical settings) has ragged ahead of pooled-wave on train loss (**1.939 vs 1.956**), eval bpb (**0.975 vs 1.033**), and steady-state drop rate (**~0.03% vs ~2.7%** at that scale).\n\nContext: pooled-wave is the hero default but drops a low-single-digit percentage of expert assignments at steady state. The goal here is at-least-parity throughput with materially fewer drops, without touching the model or precision. That trade matters most for long-context training, where a batch holds fewer, longer examples: per-shard token pools average over fewer documents, routing skew grows, and capacity clipping bites harder. Memory is a second operational motivation. The hero's intermittent OOMs traced to the step peak overshooting the cuda_async release threshold (#8490), and main now holds the production pooled-wave hero under that threshold by shrinking the train-step arena (#8507, slop factor 85) with the master kept on pinned host. Ragged reaches the same safety with ~12 GiB to spare: in that same paired run, where both arms carry the heavier fp32-on-device master, pooled-wave still peaks 11.7 GiB over the threshold (149.9 vs 138.2 GiB) while ragged sits just under it (137.9 GiB) — headroom that loosens the arena and master-placement constraints the pooled posture needs.\n\nCaveat — **quoted throughput depends on an XLA patch, shipped separately.** The device kernel itself runs on stock XLA (jax ≥ 0.11.1 defines the flags; older jaxlibs abort at import on unknown `XLA_FLAGS` entries), but its stock CTA assignment starves under trained-router skew and measures ~19.4% MFU at this shape. The quoted numbers use a one-commit balanced-CTA-assignment patch, [mcwitt/xla@d6d3132a90](https://github.com/mcwitt/xla/commit/d6d3132a90dada14d570b66da38eccb7f6d774a3) (2.35× on the standalone transport benchmark; being upstreamed). This PR does not ship a wheel; the pinned build lands in a follow-up. The 4-GPU validation has been run green on GB200 against the host-launched kernel, which exercises the expert-MLP kernels and the offset arithmetic; re-running it against the device kernel needs that build.\n\nPart of #8317. Per-arm ledgers and trace anatomy live on `research/mcwitt/8317-ragged-tune` under `autoresearch/loop-260821-leg2/` (one-shot tuning) and on `research/mcwitt/8317-dk-native` under `autoresearch/loop-260824-dkperf/` (device-kernel root-cause and the balanced-CTA result).\n\n\n\n","comments":[],"commits":[{"authoredDate":"2026-08-20T22:55:23Z","authors":[{"email":"matt.wittmann@openathena.ai","id":"MDQ6VXNlcjMxOTQxMQ==","login":"mcwitt","name":"Matt Wittmann"}],"committedDate":"2026-08-25T19:10:30Z","messageBody":"The hero launcher asserted `fixed_pooled_wave_all_to_all` and hardcoded one\nprocess per node, so no other expert-parallel backend could be measured at the\nhero shape without editing the file. {"body":"`cudnn_grouped_wgrad` (`lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe/cudnn_wgrad_cute.py`, introduced by PR #8081 and carried by its derived measurement branches — not yet on main) silently computes wrong weight gradients whenever a group's row offset is not 64-aligned. `pad_grouped_rows` pads groups to 8-row boundaries, but the cuDNN CuTeDSL grouped Wgrad kernel needs 64: at 8- or 32-aligned offsets the max error against a NumPy reference is 0.17-0.55 relative to the gradient peak, versus the bf16 accumulation floor of ~0.003 at 64/128/256 alignment. Measured on GB200 at production dims (k=6144 n=3072 and k=1536 n=6144, G=3, realistic routing counts); the error grows with group count (0.17 at G=2 to 0.55 at G=12 at k=512).\n\nEvery `*_cudnn_cute` MoE backend on the PR #8081 lineage routes dw13/dw2 through this kernel, so training runs on those branches computed corrupted expert weight gradients for any routing outcome whose group sizes were not 64-multiples — effectively always. Loss curves in short benchmark runs still fall, which is why it went unnoticed; existing grad conformance checks passed because their `atol` absorbed the error at small-magnitude weights.\n\nReproduce:\n1. On a GB200 pod with the gpu extra, on the PR #8081 branch: build `x [2560, 512]`, `d [2560, 1536]` bf16, `group_sizes = [900, 800, 860]`.\n2. Compare `cudnn_grouped_wgrad(x, d, gs)` against per-group `x[off:off+s].T @ d[off:off+s]` in NumPy.\n\nExpected: max error at the bf16 floor (~0.003 relative to peak), as it is when every group size is a 64-multiple.\n\nFix validated on branch `marin-ep-8081` (f2c9f702f3): raise `_GROUP_ALIGNMENT` to 64 (the smallest exact alignment; 32 still fails). Cost is at most 63 zero rows per group. Marin bypassed the public facade and called the internal MoEGroupedGemmWgradBF16Kernel with 8-row padding.\n\nA direct PyTorch/cuDNN Frontend reduction on GB200 produced 0.269 relative error for 8-aligned starts, 0.217 for 32-aligned starts, and 0 for 64-aligned starts. That confirms the internal kernel silently corrupts these inputs, but the 8-, 32-, and 64-aligned cases are all outside the public cuDNN contract unless they are also 256-aligned.\n\nThe correct integration fix is to pad every group to a multiple of 256, or use another kernel whose supported contract accepts smaller groups. {"body":"The expert-parallel ring MoE backend (`lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe/ep_ring.py`, `_moe_mlp_ep_ring_local`) computes wrong outputs. At capacity 2.0, ring had 0 drops but forward relative max error was 0.79, 0.90, 0.96, and 1.93 across seeds 0–3; seed 1 produced non-finite gradients. {"body":"`cudnn_grouped_wgrad` (`lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe/cudnn_wgrad_cute.py`, introduced by PR #8081 and carried by its derived measurement branches — not yet on main) silently computes wrong weight gradients whenever a group's row offset is not 64-aligned. `pad_grouped_rows` pads groups to 8-row boundaries, but the cuDNN CuTeDSL grouped Wgrad kernel needs 64: at 8- or 32-aligned offsets the max error against a NumPy reference is 0.17-0.55 relative to the gradient peak, versus the bf16 accumulation floor of ~0.003 at 64/128/256 alignment. Measured on GB200 at production dims (k=6144 n=3072 and k=1536 n=6144, G=3, realistic routing counts); the error grows with group count (0.17 at G=2 to 0.55 at G=12 at k=512).\n\nEvery `*_cudnn_cute` MoE backend on the PR #8081 lineage routes dw13/dw2 through this kernel, so training runs on those branches computed corrupted expert weight gradients for any routing outcome whose group sizes were not 64-multiples — effectively always. Loss curves in short benchmark runs still fall, which is why it went unnoticed; existing grad conformance checks passed because their `atol` absorbed the error at small-magnitude weights.\n\nReproduce:\n1. Marin bypassed the public facade and called the internal MoEGroupedGemmWgradBF16Kernel with 8-row padding.\n\nA direct PyTorch/cuDNN Frontend reduction on GB200 produced 0.269 relative error for 8-aligned starts, 0.217 for 32-aligned starts, and 0 for 64-aligned starts. Raising the padding from 8 to 64 avoids the observed corruption but still violates the cuDNN Frontend contract.","createdAt":"2026-08-17T18:38:58Z","url":"https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8339#issuecomment-5318708904"}],"number":8339,"state":"CLOSED","title":"[levanter] cuDNN grouped Wgrad silently wrong unless group offsets are 64-aligned","url":"https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8339"}

    15	# Row count each expert group is padded up to, so every group starts where the kernel's
    16	# tile loads expect it to.
    17	_GROUP_ALIGNMENT = 8
    18	# Vector width the feature (non-grouped) dimensions must divide, which is what the tensor
    19	# specs below declare to the kernel.
    20	_FEATURE_ALIGNMENT = 8
    21	_MMA_TILER_MN = (256, 256)
    22	_CLUSTER_SHAPE_MN = (2, 1)
    23

    25	class _CudnnModules(NamedTuple):
    26	    """CuTeDSL and cuDNN Frontend entry points, imported only where the GPU extra exists."""
    27	
    28	    cutlass: Any
    29	    cute: Any
    30	    cutlass_jax: Any
    31	    kernel_type: Any
    32	    weight_mode: Any
    33	    input_order: Any

    36	@functools.cache
    37	def _cudnn_modules() -> _CudnnModules:
    38	    kernel_module = importlib.import_module("cudnn.gemm.cutedsl.grouped.wgrad.moe_grouped_gemm_wgrad")
    39	    utility_module = importlib.import_module("cudnn.gemm.cutedsl.grouped.moe_utils")
    40	    return _CudnnModules(
    41	        cutlass=importlib.import_module("cutlass"),
    42	        cute=importlib.import_module("cutlass.cute"),
    43	        cutlass_jax=importlib.import_module("cutlass.jax"),
    44	        kernel_type=kernel_module.MoEGroupedGemmWgradBF16Kernel,
    45	        weight_mode=utility_module.MoEWeightMode,
    46	        input_order=utility_module.WGradInputOrder,
    47	    )

    50	@cute_launcher_factory
    51	def _build_launcher(
    52	    modules,
    53	    *,
    54	    expert_count: int,
    55	    max_active_clusters: int,
    56	):
    57	    @modules.cute.jit
    58	    def launcher(stream, mat_a, mat_b, offsets, output, workspace):
    59	        kernel = modules.kernel_type(
    60	            acc_dtype=modules.cutlass.Float32,
    61	            use_2cta_instrs=True,
    62	            mma_tiler_mn=_MMA_TILER_MN,
    63	            cluster_shape_mn=_CLUSTER_SHAPE_MN,
    64	            accumulate_on_output=False,
    65	            expert_cnt=expert_count,
    66	            weight_mode=modules.weight_mode.DENSE,
    67	            input_order=modules.input_order.Tensor2D,
    68	        )
    69	        kernel(mat_a, mat_b, output, offsets, workspace, max_active_clusters, stream, None)
    70	
    71	    return launcher

    74	def pad_grouped_rows(values: jax.Array, group_sizes: jax.Array) -> tuple[jax.Array, jax.Array]:
    75	    """Insert zero rows so each contiguous expert group ends on an eight-row boundary."""
    76	    if values.ndim != 2:
    77	        raise ValueError(f"values must be rank 2, got shape={values.shape}")
    78	    if values.shape[0] == 0:
    79	        raise ValueError("values must contain at least one physical row")
    80	    if group_sizes.ndim != 1 or group_sizes.shape[0] == 0:
    81	        raise ValueError(f"group_sizes must be a nonempty vector, got shape={group_sizes.shape}")
    82	
    83	    group_sizes = group_sizes.astype(jnp.int32)
    84	    padded_group_sizes = ((group_sizes + _GROUP_ALIGNMENT - 1) // _GROUP_ALIGNMENT) * _GROUP_ALIGNMENT
    85	    active_offsets = jnp.cumsum(group_sizes, dtype=jnp.int32)
    86	    padded_offsets = jnp.cumsum(padded_group_sizes, dtype=jnp.int32)
    87	    active_starts = jnp.concatenate([jnp.zeros((1,), jnp.int32), active_offsets[:-1]])
    88	    padded_starts = jnp.concatenate([jnp.zeros((1,), jnp.int32), padded_offsets[:-1]])
    89	
    90	    # At most seven rows are inserted per group. Keep a static worst-case tail so the output shape
    91	    # does not depend on the runtime routing counts.
    92	    padded_capacity = values.shape[0] + (_GROUP_ALIGNMENT - 1) * group_sizes.shape[0]
    93	    padded_rows = jnp.arange(padded_capacity, dtype=jnp.int32)
    94	    expert_ids = jnp.sum(padded_rows[:, None] >= padded_offsets[None, :], axis=1, dtype=jnp.int32)
    95	    safe_expert_ids = jnp.minimum(expert_ids, group_sizes.shape[0] - 1)
    96	    rows_within_group = padded_rows - padded_starts[safe_expert_ids]
    97	    source_rows = active_starts[safe_expert_ids] + rows_within_group
    98	    valid = (expert_ids < group_sizes.shape[0]) & (rows_within_group < group_sizes[safe_expert_ids])
    99	    source_rows = jnp.clip(source_rows, 0, values.shape[0] - 1)
   100	    padded = jnp.where(valid[:, None], values[source_rows], jnp.zeros((), dtype=values.dtype))
   101	    return padded, padded_offsets
   102	
   103	
   104	def cudnn_grouped_wgrad(lhs: jax.Array, rhs: jax.Array, group_sizes: jax.Array) -> jax.Array:
   105	    """Compute per-expert ``lhs.T @ rhs`` for contiguous ragged row groups."""
   106	    if lhs.ndim != 2 or rhs.ndim != 2:
   107	        raise ValueError(f"lhs and rhs must be rank 2, got lhs={lhs.shape}, rhs={rhs.shape}")
   108	    if lhs.shape[0] != rhs.shape[0]:
   109	        raise ValueError(f"lhs and rhs row counts must match, got lhs={lhs.shape}, rhs={rhs.shape}")
   110	    if lhs.dtype != jnp.bfloat16 or rhs.dtype != jnp.bfloat16:
   111	        raise ValueError(f"cuDNN grouped Wgrad requires BF16 inputs, got lhs={lhs.dtype}, rhs={rhs.dtype}")
   112	    if lhs.shape[1] % _FEATURE_ALIGNMENT != 0 or rhs.shape[1] % _FEATURE_ALIGNMENT != 0:
   113	        raise ValueError(
   114	            f"cuDNN grouped Wgrad feature dimensions must divide {_FEATURE_ALIGNMENT}, "
   115	            f"got lhs={lhs.shape}, rhs={rhs.shape}"
   116	        )
   117	
   118	    lhs_padded, padded_offsets = pad_grouped_rows(lhs, group_sizes)
   119	    rhs_padded, _ = pad_grouped_rows(rhs, group_sizes)
   120	    modules = _cudnn_modules()
   121	    max_active_clusters = modules.cutlass.utils.HardwareInfo().get_max_active_clusters(
   122	        _CLUSTER_SHAPE_MN[0] * _CLUSTER_SHAPE_MN[1]
   123	    )
   124	    launcher = _build_launcher(
   125	        modules,
   126	        expert_count=group_sizes.shape[0],
   127	        max_active_clusters=max_active_clusters,
   128	    )
   129	    tensor_spec = modules.cutlass_jax.TensorSpec
   130	    call = cutlass_call(
   131	        launcher,
   132	        output_shape_dtype=(
   133	            jax.ShapeDtypeStruct((group_sizes.shape[0], lhs.shape[1], rhs.shape[1]), lhs.dtype),
   134	            jax.ShapeDtypeStruct((1,), jnp.uint8),
   135	        ),
   136	        input_spec=(
   137	            tensor_spec(mode=(1, 0), divisibility=(1, _FEATURE_ALIGNMENT), static=False),
   138	            tensor_spec(divisibility=(1, _FEATURE_ALIGNMENT), static=False),
   139	            tensor_spec(static=False),
   140	        ),
   141	        output_spec=(
   142	            tensor_spec(divisibility=(1, 1, _FEATURE_ALIGNMENT), static=False),
   143	            tensor_spec(static=False),
   144	        ),
   145	        use_static_tensors=False,
   146	    )
   147	    output, _workspace = call(lhs_padded, rhs_padded, padded_offsets)
   148	    return output
    70	        moe_w13_local: Float[Array, "Echunk H I2"],
    71	        moe_w2_local: Float[Array, "Echunk I H"],
    72	        physical_group_sizes: Int[Array, "Echunk"],
    73	        active_group_sizes: Int[Array, "Echunk"],
    74	        activation_fn: Callable[[jax.Array], jax.Array],
    75	    ) -> Float[Array, "C H"]: ...
    76	
    77	
    78	def _ragged_dot_expert_mlp(
    79	    x_dispatch: Float[Array, "C H"],
    80	    moe_w13_local: Float[Array, "Echunk H I2"],
    81	    moe_w2_local: Float[Array, "Echunk I H"],
    82	    physical_group_sizes: Int[Array, "Echunk"],
    83	    active_group_sizes: Int[Array, "Echunk"],
    84	    activation_fn: Callable[[jax.Array], jax.Array],
    85	) -> Float[Array, "C H"]:
    86	    """Portable expert MLP over XLA's `ragged_dot`, which covers the whole receiver buffer."""
    87	    del active_group_sizes
    88	    w13_out = ragged_dot(x_dispatch, moe_w13_local, physical_group_sizes)
    89	    moe_dim = moe_w2_local.shape[1]
    90	    gate, up = jnp.split(w13_out, [moe_dim], axis=-1)
    91	    return ragged_dot(activation_fn(gate) * up, moe_w2_local, physical_group_sizes)
    92	
    93	
    94	def _cute_expert_mlp(
    95	    x_dispatch: Float[Array, "C H"],
    96	    moe_w13_local: Float[Array, "Echunk H I2"],
    97	    moe_w2_local: Float[Array, "Echunk I H"],
    98	    physical_group_sizes: Int[Array, "Echunk"],
    99	    active_group_sizes: Int[Array, "Echunk"],
   100	    activation_fn: Callable[[jax.Array], jax.Array],
   101	) -> Float[Array, "C H"]:
   102	    """Expert MLP on QuACK's SM100 grouped GEMMs plus cuDNN grouped weight gradients.
   103	
   104	    The grouped kernels are driven by segment boundaries, so they take the active sizes and
   105	    mask the receiver buffer's trailing padding rather than charging it to the last expert.
   106	    """
   107	    del activation_fn, physical_group_sizes
   108	
   109	    # QuACK, cuDNN Frontend, and CUTLASS DSL are installed only with the CUDA 13 GPU extra.
   110	    from levanter.grug._moe.sonic_cute import _expert_mlp_cudnn, _interleave_gate_up  # noqa: PLC0415
   111	
   112	    moe_dim = moe_w2_local.shape[1]
   113	    w13_interleaved = _interleave_gate_up(moe_w13_local, moe_dim)
   114	    cumulative_group_sizes = jnp.concatenate(
   115	        [jnp.zeros((1,), jnp.int32), jnp.cumsum(active_group_sizes).astype(jnp.int32)]
   116	    )
   117	    return _expert_mlp_cudnn(x_dispatch, w13_interleaved, moe_w2_local, active_group_sizes, cumulative_group_sizes)
   118	
   119	
   120	@functools.cache
   121	def _quack_grouped_gemm_available() -> bool:
   122	    if jax.default_backend() != "gpu":
   123	        return False
   124	    if float(jax.devices("gpu")[0].compute_capability) < _SM100_COMPUTE_CAPABILITY:
   125	        return False
   126	    try:
   127	        import levanter.grug._moe.sonic_cute  # noqa: F401,PLC0415
   128	        from levanter.grug._moe.cudnn_wgrad_cute import _cudnn_modules  # noqa: PLC0415
   129	
   130	        _ = _cudnn_modules()  # check if compatible cudnn is available
   131	    except (ImportError, AttributeError) as exc:
   132	        logger.warning(
   133	            "SM100 GPU present but the QuACK/cuDNN grouped-GEMM kernels did not import (%s). "
   134	            "The ragged expert MLP falls back to ragged_dot, which computes the same function "
   135	            "more slowly. Install levanter's `gpu` extra to use them.",
   136	            exc,
   137	        )
   138	        return False
   139	    return True
   140	
   141	
   142	def _select_expert_mlp(activation_fn: Callable[[jax.Array], jax.Array]) -> _ExpertMlp:
   143	    """Pick the fastest expert-MLP kernel this process can actually run.
   144	
   145	    QuACK's kernel fuses SwiGLU, so it only applies to SiLU. Everything else -- another
   146	    activation, a non-SM100 GPU, a TPU or CPU, or a build without the GPU extra -- runs the
   147	    portable `ragged_dot` path, which computes the same function.
   148	    """
   149	    if activation_fn is jax.nn.silu and _quack_grouped_gemm_available():
   150	        return _cute_expert_mlp
   151	    return _ragged_dot_expert_mlp
   152	
   153	
   154	def _unpermute_from_global_expert(
   155	    intermediate: Float[Array, "TK H"],
   156	    sorted_indices: Int[Array, "TK"],
   157	    combine_weights_local: Float[Array, "Tlocal K"],
   158	    *,
   159	    tokens_per_shard: int,
   160	    topk: int,
   161	) -> Float[Array, "Tlocal H"]:
   162	    """Weight each token's expert outputs by its routing weights and sum them."""
   163	    positions = jnp.argsort(sorted_indices)
   164	    if sonic_gather_sum_available():
   165	        # One kernel for the gather and the sum, materializing neither the unpermuted
   166	        # ``[TK, H]`` buffer nor the ``[T, K, H]`` view -- at top-8 that view is eight times
   167	        # the output. It accumulates in fp32 like the einsum below and keeps the routing
   168	        # weight in fp32 through the multiply, where the einsum has to cast it down to avoid
   169	        # promoting the larger operand, so the two agree to a single rounding.
   170	        return sonic_gather_sum(intermediate, positions.reshape(tokens_per_shard, topk), combine_weights_local)
   171	    unsorted = _sort_activations(intermediate, positions)
   172	    reshaped = unsorted.reshape(tokens_per_shard, topk, -1)
   173	    return jnp.einsum(
   174	        "tkd,tk->td", reshaped, combine_weights_local.astype(reshaped.dtype), preferred_element_type=jnp.float32
   175	    )
   176	
   177	
   178	@functools.partial(jax.custom_vjp, nondiff_argnums=(2,))
   179	def _gather_dispatch_rows(
   180	    x_local: Float[Array, "Tlocal H"], sorted_indices: Int[Array, "TK"], topk: int
   181	) -> Float[Array, "TK H"]:
   182	    """Build the expert-sorted dispatch buffer with one gather.
   183	
   184	    Equivalent to ``jnp.repeat(x_local, topk, axis=0)[sorted_indices]`` without
   185	    materializing the repeated buffer or running a data-sized permute. The backward pass
   186	    is the transpose: each token sums the cotangent rows of its ``topk`` sorted slots.
   187	    """
   188	    return x_local[sorted_indices // topk]

     4	"""Public Grug MoE interface and implementation dispatcher.
     5	
     6	Implementation overview:
     7	- Routing keeps the argsort-grouped dispatch path that emerged as the stable
     8	  default from https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/2704 and commit
     9	  89318a910 (and its parent).
    10	- Expert parallelism keeps the ring-style strategy from
    11	  https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/2710: token-sharded
    12	  `all_gather` for dispatch, then `psum_scatter` for collection.
    13	- Backend bodies live in the private `levanter.grug._moe` package; this module
    14	  keeps the stable public API used by Grug model code and benchmarks.
    15	"""
