    69	class MoEExpertMlp(eqx.Module):
    70	    """Expert MLP weights for routed MoE calls."""
    71	
    72	    w_gate: jax.Array
    73	    w_up: jax.Array
    74	    w_down: jax.Array
    75	    implementation: MoeImplementation = eqx.field(static=True)
    76	    activation: MoeActivation = eqx.field(static=True)
    77	    capacity_factor: float = eqx.field(static=True)
    78	    pooled_transport_capacity_factor: float | None = eqx.field(static=True, default=None)
    79	    expert_chunks: int = eqx.field(static=True, default=1)
    80	    ragged_expert_chunks: int | None = eqx.field(static=True, default=None)
    81	    ragged_receiver_alignment: int | None = eqx.field(static=True, default=None)
    82	    num_expert_waves: int = eqx.field(static=True, default=1)
    83	
    84	    @staticmethod
    85	    def init(
    86	        *,
    87	        num_experts: int,
    88	        hidden_dim: int,
    89	        intermediate_dim: int,
    90	        initializer_std: float,
    91	        key: jax.Array,
    92	        gate_up_initializer_std: float | None = None,
    93	        implementation: MoeImplementation | str | None = None,
    94	        activation: MoeActivation = ActivationFunctionEnum.silu,
    95	        capacity_factor: float = _DEFAULT_EP_CAPACITY_FACTOR,
    96	        pooled_transport_capacity_factor: float | None = None,
    97	        expert_chunks: int = 1,
    98	        ragged_expert_chunks: int | None = None,
    99	        ragged_receiver_alignment: int | None = None,
   100	        num_expert_waves: int = 1,
   101	        pspecs: MoEExpertMlpPspecs = MoEExpertMlpPspecs(),
   102	    ) -> "MoEExpertMlp":
   103	        resolved_implementation = resolve_moe_implementation(implementation)
   104	        k_gate, k_up, k_down = jax.random.split(key, 3)
   105	        # `w_gate`/`w_up` contract over `hidden_dim`, so their fan-in moves when the experts run
   106	        # in a latent space; `w_down` contracts over `intermediate_dim` and is unaffected.
   107	        gate_up_std = initializer_std if gate_up_initializer_std is None else gate_up_initializer_std
   108	        w_gate = _init_weight(k_gate, (num_experts, hidden_dim, intermediate_dim), gate_up_std)
   109	        w_up = _init_weight(k_up, (num_experts, hidden_dim, intermediate_dim), gate_up_std)
   110	        w_down = _reshard_for_init(
   111	            _init_weight(k_down, (num_experts, intermediate_dim, hidden_dim), initializer_std),
   112	            pspecs.w_down,
   113	        )
   114	        return MoEExpertMlp(
   115	            w_gate=_reshard_for_init(w_gate, pspecs.w_gate_up),
   116	            w_up=_reshard_for_init(w_up, pspecs.w_gate_up),
   117	            w_down=w_down,
   118	            implementation=resolved_implementation,
   119	            activation=activation,
   120	            capacity_factor=capacity_factor,
   121	            pooled_transport_capacity_factor=pooled_transport_capacity_factor,
   122	            expert_chunks=expert_chunks,
   123	            ragged_expert_chunks=ragged_expert_chunks,
   124	            ragged_receiver_alignment=ragged_receiver_alignment,
   125	            num_expert_waves=num_expert_waves,
   126	        )
   127	
   128	    @named_call
   129	    def __call__(
   130	        self,
   131	        x: Float[Array, "T D"],
   132	        selected_experts: Int[Array, "T K"],
   133	        combine_weights: Float[Array, "T K"],
   134	        *,
   135	        mesh: jax.sharding.AbstractMesh | None = None,
   136	        report_capacity_overflow: bool = False,
   137	    ) -> Float[Array, "T D"] | tuple[Float[Array, "T D"], CapacityOverflow]:
   138	        w_gate_up = jnp.concatenate([self.w_gate, self.w_up], axis=-1)
   139	        return moe_mlp(
   140	            x,
   141	            selected_experts,
   142	            combine_weights,
   143	            w_gate_up,
   144	            self.w_down,
   145	            activation=self.activation,
   146	            implementation=self.implementation,
   147	            mesh=mesh,
   148	            capacity_factor=self.capacity_factor,
   149	            pooled_transport_capacity_factor=self.pooled_transport_capacity_factor,
   150	            report_capacity_overflow=report_capacity_overflow,
   151	            expert_chunks=self.expert_chunks,
   152	            ragged_expert_chunks=self.ragged_expert_chunks,
   153	            ragged_receiver_alignment=self.ragged_receiver_alignment,
   154	            num_expert_waves=self.num_expert_waves,
   155	        )
   156	
   157	
   158	@named_call
   159	def moe_mlp(
   160	    x: Float[Array, "T D"],
   161	    selected_experts: Int[Array, "T K"],
   162	    combine_weights: Float[Array, "T K"],
   163	    w_up_gate: Float[Array, "E D I2"],
   164	    w_down: Float[Array, "E I D"],
   165	    *,
   166	    activation: MoeActivation = ActivationFunctionEnum.silu,
   167	    implementation: MoeImplementation | str | None = None,
   168	    mesh: jax.sharding.Mesh | jax.sharding.AbstractMesh | None = None,
   169	    capacity_factor: float = _DEFAULT_EP_CAPACITY_FACTOR,
   170	    pooled_transport_capacity_factor: float | None = None,
   171	    report_capacity_overflow: bool = False,
   172	    expert_chunks: int = 1,
   173	    ragged_expert_chunks: int | None = None,
   174	    ragged_receiver_alignment: int | None = None,
   175	    num_expert_waves: int = 1,
   176	) -> Float[Array, "T D"] | tuple[Float[Array, "T D"], CapacityOverflow]:
   177	    """Functional routed MoE MLP core used by Grug modules and benchmarks.
   178	
   179	    This helper handles dispatch/permute/unpermute (+EP collectives) from
   180	    precomputed token-to-expert assignments. Routing logits/top-k selection
   181	    stays in the caller (e.g. model MLP block).
   182	
   183	    Set `report_capacity_overflow=True` to also return sender and receiver
   184	    counts for expert assignments dropped by EP capacity clipping.
   185	
   186	    `expert_chunks` applies only to the local `sonic_cute` FSDP path. Values
   187	    greater than one split the expert bank into equal, statically sized chunks.
   188	
   189	    `ragged_expert_chunks` is the matching knob for the `ragged_all_to_all` EP
   190	    transport: how many sequential chunks the local expert bank is processed in,
   191	    each with its own share of the receiver capacity. `None` takes
   192	    `RAGGED_DEFAULT_EXPERT_CHUNKS`; an explicit count must divide the local bank.
   193	
   194	    `ragged_receiver_alignment` lays that transport's receiver buffer out with
   195	    every expert group starting on a multiple of that many rows, which lets the
   196	    cuDNN grouped weight-gradient kernel read the buffer without its operand
   197	    pre-pass. `None` packs the groups back to back, as before. It changes the
   198	    layout only: the same rows are accepted and dropped either way.
   199	
   200	    `pooled_transport_capacity_factor` sets the sender capacity for each
   201	    destination pool. `num_expert_waves` sets the static wave count for the
   202	    fixed pooled-wave implementation.
   203	    """
   204	    resolved_implementation = resolve_moe_implementation(implementation)
   205	
   206	    if mesh is None:
   207	        mesh = _current_mesh()
   208	
   209	    if isinstance(activation, ActivationFunctionEnum):
   210	        activation_fn: Callable[[jax.Array], jax.Array] = activation.to_jax_fn()
   211	    else:
   212	        activation_fn = activation
   213	
   214	    if x.ndim != 2:
   215	        raise ValueError(f"x must be rank-2 [T, D], got shape={x.shape}")
   216	    if selected_experts.ndim != 2:
   217	        raise ValueError(f"selected_experts must be rank-2 [T, K], got shape={selected_experts.shape}")
   218	    if selected_experts.shape != combine_weights.shape:
   219	        raise ValueError(
   220	            "selected_experts and combine_weights must have identical [T, K] shapes; "
   221	            f"got {selected_experts.shape} vs {combine_weights.shape}"
   222	        )
   223	    if selected_experts.shape[0] != x.shape[0]:
   224	        raise ValueError(
   225	            f"selected_experts/combine_weights token dim ({selected_experts.shape[0]}) must match x token "
   226	            f"dim ({x.shape[0]})"
   227	        )
   228	
   229	    num_experts = int(w_up_gate.shape[0])
   230	    if w_down.shape[0] != num_experts:
   231	        raise ValueError(
   232	            f"w_down expert dimension ({w_down.shape[0]}) must match w_up_gate expert dimension ({num_experts})"
   233	        )
   234	
   235	    has_expert_axis = _mesh_has_axis(mesh, "expert")
   236	    expert_axis_size = _mesh_axis_size(mesh, "expert")
   237	
   238	    if mesh is None or mesh.empty:
   239	        out, dropped = _moe_mlp_local(
   240	            x,
   241	            selected_experts,
   242	            combine_weights,
   243	            w_up_gate,
   244	            w_down,
   245	            activation_fn=activation_fn,
   246	            num_experts=num_experts,
   247	            implementation=resolved_implementation,
   248	            expert_chunks=expert_chunks,
   249	        )
   250	        if report_capacity_overflow:
   251	            return out, CapacityOverflow(sender=dropped, receiver=jnp.zeros_like(dropped))
   252	        return out
   253	
   254	    batch_spec = _batch_spec_from_x(x, mesh)
   255	
   256	    if has_expert_axis and expert_axis_size > 1:
   257	        if expert_chunks != 1:
   258	            raise ValueError("expert_chunks must be 1 when expert parallelism is active")
   259	        if resolved_implementation not in _EP_MOE_IMPLEMENTATIONS:
   260	            raise ValueError(
   261	                "Local MoE implementations do not yet support expert-parallel collectives; adding EP support "
   262	                "requires a dispatch/combine schedule inside each expert shard plus cross-shard routing. "
   263	                f"got implementation={resolved_implementation!r} with expert axis size={expert_axis_size}"
   264	            )
   265	        if num_experts % expert_axis_size != 0:
   266	            raise ValueError(f"num_experts={num_experts} must be divisible by expert axis size={expert_axis_size}")
   267	
   268	        if resolved_implementation == "ring":
   269	            shard_local_fn = _moe_mlp_ep_ring_local
   270	        elif resolved_implementation == "ragged_all_to_all":
   271	            shard_local_fn = partial(
   272	                _moe_mlp_ep_ragged_a2a_local,
   273	                expert_chunks=ragged_expert_chunks,
   274	                receiver_alignment=ragged_receiver_alignment,
   275	            )
   276	        elif resolved_implementation == "fixed_all_to_all":
   277	            shard_local_fn = _moe_mlp_ep_fixed_a2a_local
   278	        elif resolved_implementation == "fixed_pooled_wave_all_to_all":
   279	            if pooled_transport_capacity_factor is None:
   280	                raise ValueError("fixed_pooled_wave_all_to_all requires pooled_transport_capacity_factor")
   281	            shard_local_fn = partial(
   282	                _moe_mlp_ep_fixed_pooled_wave_a2a_local,
   283	                transport_capacity_factor=pooled_transport_capacity_factor,
   284	                num_expert_waves=num_expert_waves,
   285	            )
   286	        elif resolved_implementation == "deepep":
   287	            shard_local_fn = _moe_mlp_ep_deepep_local
   288	        else:
   289	            raise AssertionError(f"Unhandled MoE implementation {resolved_implementation!r}")
   290	
   291	        w_up_gate_spec = P("expert", None, None)
   292	        w_down_spec = P("expert", None, None)
   293	
   294	        x = _reshard_for_shard_map(x, mesh, batch_spec)
   295	        selected_experts = _reshard_for_shard_map(selected_experts, mesh, batch_spec)
   296	        combine_weights = _reshard_for_shard_map(combine_weights, mesh, batch_spec)
   297	        w_up_gate = _reshard_for_shard_map(w_up_gate, mesh, w_up_gate_spec)
   298	        w_down = _reshard_for_shard_map(w_down, mesh, w_down_spec)
   299	
   300	        shard_fn = shard_map(
   301	            partial(
   302	                shard_local_fn,
   303	                activation_fn=activation_fn,
   304	                num_experts=num_experts,
   305	                capacity_factor=capacity_factor,
   306	            ),
   307	            mesh=mesh,
   308	            in_specs=(
   309	                batch_spec,
   310	                batch_spec,
   311	                batch_spec,
   312	                w_up_gate_spec,
   313	                w_down_spec,
   314	            ),
   315	            out_specs=(batch_spec, CapacityOverflow(sender=P(), receiver=P())),
   316	            check_vma=False,
   317	        )
   318	        out, overflow = shard_fn(x, selected_experts, combine_weights, w_up_gate, w_down)
   319	        if report_capacity_overflow:
   320	            return out, overflow
   321	        return out
   322	
   323	    # Fallback path for no expert axis (or expert axis size 1) keeps routing
   324	    # semantics without EP collectives. JAX 0.9 requires shard_map in_specs to
   325	    # match the actual input sharding, so reshard ordinary inputs to the mesh
   326	    # specs that preserve data-axis parallelism.
   327	    x_spec = _value_spec_or_default(x, batch_spec, replace_replicated=True)
   328	    selected_experts_spec = _value_spec_or_default(selected_experts, batch_spec, replace_replicated=True)
   329	    combine_weights_spec = _value_spec_or_default(combine_weights, batch_spec, replace_replicated=True)
   330	    if expert_chunks > 1 and resolved_implementation == "sonic_cute":
   331	        # The chunked sonic_cute path all-gathers the hidden dim per expert-chunk over ``data``, so it
   332	        # needs a real data axis; without one the local kernel hits an unbound-axis error.
   333	        if not _mesh_has_axis(mesh, "data") or _mesh_axis_size(mesh, "data") <= 1:
   334	            raise ValueError(
   335	                "chunked sonic_cute (expert_chunks > 1) requires a data axis to all-gather the expert "
   336	                "weights; use expert_chunks=1 on a single device or an unsharded mesh."
   337	            )
   338	        # The local weights must arrive H-sharded ([E, H/data, 2I] / [E, I, H/data]). Force that FSDP
   339	        # layout rather than inheriting whatever (possibly replicated) sharding the layer scan left,
   340	        # which would make the tiled all-gather reconstruct H * data_shards.
   341	        w_up_gate_spec = _drop_absent_mesh_axes(mesh, P("expert", "data", "model"))
   342	        w_down_spec = _drop_absent_mesh_axes(mesh, P("expert", "model", "data"))
   343	    else:
   344	        w_up_gate_spec = _value_spec_or_default(w_up_gate, P(*(None for _ in range(w_up_gate.ndim))))
   345	        w_down_spec = _value_spec_or_default(w_down, P(*(None for _ in range(w_down.ndim))))
   346	
   347	    x = _reshard_for_shard_map(x, mesh, x_spec)
   348	    selected_experts = _reshard_for_shard_map(selected_experts, mesh, selected_experts_spec)
   349	    combine_weights = _reshard_for_shard_map(combine_weights, mesh, combine_weights_spec)
   350	    w_up_gate = _reshard_for_shard_map(w_up_gate, mesh, w_up_gate_spec)
   351	    w_down = _reshard_for_shard_map(w_down, mesh, w_down_spec)
   352	
   353	    def local_moe(x, selected_experts, combine_weights, w_up_gate, w_down):
   354	        out, dropped = _moe_mlp_local(
   355	            x,
   356	            selected_experts,
   357	            combine_weights,
   358	            w_up_gate,
   359	            w_down,
   360	            activation_fn=activation_fn,

   256	    """Sequential local-expert chunks in the ragged all-to-all transport, each taking its own
   257	    share of the receiver capacity. None takes the backend default
   258	    (`RAGGED_DEFAULT_EXPERT_CHUNKS`, falling back to one chunk on a local bank it does not
   259	    divide); an explicit count must divide the local bank. Other transports ignore it."""
   260	    ragged_receiver_alignment: int | None = None
   261	    """Row alignment each expert group starts on in the ragged all-to-all receiver buffer. None
   262	    packs the groups back to back and leaves the cuDNN grouped weight-gradient wrapper to copy
   263	    both operands into an aligned buffer itself; a value (a multiple of
   264	    `RAGGED_CUDNN_RECEIVER_ALIGNMENT`) builds that layout in the transport and deletes the copies.
   265	    It moves rows within the buffer, not capacity, so the accepted set is unchanged. Other
   266	    transports ignore it."""
   267	    pooled_transport_capacity_factor: float | None = None

   271	    """Per-block gradient checkpointing. "recompute_all" reruns the whole block in
   272	    backward (lowest memory); "save_moe" keeps the tagged MoE dispatch tensors so
   273	    backward skips re-running expert dispatch and its EP collectives; "offload_carry"
   274	    recomputes everything but stages the layer-input residual on pinned host, which
   275	    releases its HBM between forward and backward."""
   276	    remat_save_names: tuple[str, ...] = ()
   277	    """Named intermediates the remat policy keeps on device for the backward, deleting
   278	    their recompute. Names must come from REMAT_SAVEABLE_NAMES; the empty default keeps
   279	    every remat mode's existing policy unchanged. This extends only which named tensors
   280	    are saved -- the offload_carry offload list and the XLA memory-budget flags are
   281	    untouched. Saved values are bit-identical to their recompute; only residency changes."""

   285	    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
   286	        _ = self.inferred_head_dim
   287	        if self.num_heads % self.stored_kv_heads != 0:
   288	            raise ValueError("num_heads must be divisible by the stored KV-head count")
   289	        if (self.local_kv_heads is None) != (self.global_kv_heads is None):
   290	            raise ValueError("local_kv_heads and global_kv_heads must be set together")
   291	        if self.local_kv_heads is not None and self.global_kv_heads is not None:
   292	            if self.local_kv_heads <= 0 or self.global_kv_heads <= 0:
   293	                raise ValueError("local_kv_heads and global_kv_heads must be positive")
   294	            if self.num_heads % self.local_kv_heads != 0 or self.num_heads % self.global_kv_heads != 0:
   295	                raise ValueError("num_heads must be divisible by both local and global KV-head counts")
   296	            if self.num_kv_heads != max(self.local_kv_heads, self.global_kv_heads):
   297	                raise ValueError("num_kv_heads must equal the stored maximum of local/global KV heads")
   298	        if self.global_every <= 0:
   299	            raise ValueError("global_every must be positive")
   300	        if self.vocab_size <= 0:
   301	            raise ValueError("vocab_size must be positive")
   302	        if self.max_seq_len <= 0:
   303	            raise ValueError("max_seq_len must be positive")
   304	        if self.num_experts <= 0:
   305	            raise ValueError("num_experts must be positive")
   306	        if self.num_experts_per_token <= 0:
   307	            raise ValueError("num_experts_per_token must be positive")
   308	        if self.num_experts_per_token >= self.num_experts:
   309	            # QB routing takes top-(k+1) and keeps the last entry as the threshold alpha, so a
   310	            # full-bank top-k asks `jax.lax.top_k` for more entries than the router has experts.
   311	            raise ValueError("num_experts_per_token must be < num_experts, because QB routing selects top-(k+1)")
   312	        if self.latent_dim is not None and not 0 < self.latent_dim <= self.hidden_dim:
   313	            raise ValueError(
   314	                f"latent_dim must be in (0, hidden_dim={self.hidden_dim}], got {self.latent_dim}; "
   315	                "it only reduces communication when it is smaller than the hidden dimension"
   316	            )
   317	        if self.shared_expert_intermediate_dim < 0:
   318	            raise ValueError("shared_expert_intermediate_dim must be non-negative")
   319	        if self.capacity_factor <= 0:
   320	            raise ValueError("capacity_factor must be positive")
   321	        if self.expert_chunks <= 0:
   322	            raise ValueError("expert_chunks must be positive")
   323	        if self.ragged_expert_chunks is not None and self.ragged_expert_chunks <= 0:
   324	            raise ValueError("ragged_expert_chunks must be positive")
   325	        if self.ragged_receiver_alignment is not None and (
   326	            self.ragged_receiver_alignment <= 0 or self.ragged_receiver_alignment % RAGGED_CUDNN_RECEIVER_ALIGNMENT != 0
   327	        ):
   328	            raise ValueError(
   329	                f"ragged_receiver_alignment must be a positive multiple of {RAGGED_CUDNN_RECEIVER_ALIGNMENT}, "
   330	                f"got {self.ragged_receiver_alignment}"
   331	            )
   332	        if self.pooled_transport_capacity_factor is not None and self.pooled_transport_capacity_factor <= 0:
   333	            raise ValueError("pooled_transport_capacity_factor must be positive")
   334	        if self.moe_implementation == "fixed_pooled_wave_all_to_all":
   335	            if self.pooled_transport_capacity_factor is None:
   336	                raise ValueError("fixed_pooled_wave_all_to_all requires pooled_transport_capacity_factor")
   337	        if self.num_expert_waves <= 0:
   338	            raise ValueError("num_expert_waves must be positive")
   339	        if self.num_shared_experts <= 0:
   340	            raise ValueError("num_shared_experts must be positive")
   341	        unknown_save_names = set(self.remat_save_names) - REMAT_SAVEABLE_NAMES
   342	        if unknown_save_names:
   343	            raise ValueError(
   344	                f"remat_save_names contains names with no call site: {sorted(unknown_save_names)}; "
   345	                f"choose from {sorted(REMAT_SAVEABLE_NAMES)}"
   346	            )

  1001	        lo = jax.lax.pmin(jax.lax.stop_gradient(jnp.min(s_local)), axis_name=_BATCH_AXES)
  1002	        hi = jax.lax.pmax(jax.lax.stop_gradient(jnp.max(s_local)), axis_name=_BATCH_AXES)
  1003	        hi_grid = jnp.maximum(hi, lo + 1e-6)  # guard a degenerate all-equal range
  1004	        beta = _bincount_upper_quantile(
  1005	            s_local, num_experts=num_experts, n_bins=n_bins, lo=lo, hi=hi_grid, target_rank=target_rank
  1006	        )
  1007	        return beta, lo, hi  # surface the live margin range for logging

  1012	class MoEMLP(eqx.Module):
  1013	    """QB-routed MoE with sigmoid combine weights."""
  1014	
  1015	    router: jax.Array
  1016	    router_bias: jax.Array
  1017	    expert_mlp: MoEExpertMlp
  1018	    w_latent_down: jax.Array | None
  1019	    latent_norm: RMSNorm | None
  1020	    w_latent_up: jax.Array | None
  1021	    cfg: GrugModelConfig = eqx.field(static=True)
  1022	
  1023	    @staticmethod
  1024	    def init(cfg: GrugModelConfig, *, key: PRNGKeyArray) -> "MoEMLP":
  1025	        k_router, k_expert, k_down, k_up = random.split(key, 4)
  1026	        mesh = get_abstract_mesh()
  1027	
  1028	        expert_axis_size = _mesh_axis_size(mesh, "expert")
  1029	        if cfg.num_experts % expert_axis_size != 0:
  1030	            raise ValueError(f"num_experts={cfg.num_experts} must be divisible by expert axis size={expert_axis_size}")
  1031	
  1032	        d, e = cfg.hidden_dim, cfg.num_experts
  1033	        # Routed experts live in the latent space; the router reads the full-width token, so its
  1034	        # own projection keeps `hidden_dim`.
  1035	        expert_width = cfg.latent_dim if cfg.latent_dim is not None else d
  1036	        latent = cfg.latent_dim
  1037	        return MoEMLP(
  1038	            router=reshard(_init_weight(k_router, (d, e), cfg.initializer_std), P(None, None)),
  1039	            router_bias=jnp.zeros((e,)),
  1040	            w_latent_down=(
  1041	                None
  1042	                if latent is None
  1043	                else reshard(_init_weight(k_down, (d, latent), cfg.initializer_std), P(_FSDP_AXES, "model"))
  1044	            ),
  1045	            latent_norm=None if latent is None else RMSNorm.init(latent, cfg.layer_norm_eps),
  1046	            w_latent_up=(
  1047	                None
  1048	                if latent is None
  1049	                else reshard(_init_weight(k_up, (latent, d), cfg.initializer_std), P("model", _FSDP_AXES))
  1050	            ),
  1051	            expert_mlp=MoEExpertMlp.init(
  1052	                num_experts=cfg.num_experts,
  1053	                hidden_dim=expert_width,
  1054	                intermediate_dim=cfg.intermediate_dim,
  1055	                initializer_std=cfg.initializer_std,
  1056	                key=k_expert,
  1057	                implementation=cfg.moe_implementation,
  1058	                activation=ActivationFunctionEnum.silu,
  1059	                capacity_factor=cfg.capacity_factor,
  1060	                pooled_transport_capacity_factor=cfg.pooled_transport_capacity_factor,
  1061	                expert_chunks=cfg.expert_chunks,
  1062	                ragged_expert_chunks=cfg.ragged_expert_chunks,
  1063	                ragged_receiver_alignment=cfg.ragged_receiver_alignment,
  1064	                num_expert_waves=cfg.num_expert_waves,
  1065	            ),
  1066	            cfg=cfg,
  1067	        )
  1068	
  1069	    @named_call
  1070	    def __call__(
  1071	        self,
  1072	        x: Float[Array, "B S D"],
  1073	    ) -> tuple[Float[Array, "B S D"], dict[str, jax.Array]]:
  1074	        b, s, _ = x.shape
  1075	        x_flat = rearrange(x, "b s d -> (b s) d")
  1076	        # Keep the router path in fp32 before top-k, softmax, and QB statistics.
  1077	        router_logits = jnp.einsum("td,de->te", x_flat, reshard(self.router, P(None, None))).astype(jnp.float32)
  1078	        biased_logits = router_logits + jax.lax.stop_gradient(self.router_bias)
  1079	        router_probs = jax.nn.softmax(router_logits, axis=-1)
  1080	        # Select top-(K+1) on biased logits; the (K+1)-th is the QB threshold alpha.

   850	    # Per-layer int32 counts summed over layers in int64 on the host: the global totals exceed int32 at
   851	    # large batch (jax_enable_x64 is off, so an in-device sum would overflow), and float32 would round them.
   852	    def _sum_int64(per_layer: jax.Array) -> int:
   853	        return int(np.asarray(per_layer).astype(np.int64).sum())
   854	
   855	    dropped_assignments_host = _sum_int64(dropped_assignments)
   856	    sender_dropped_assignments_host = _sum_int64(sender_dropped_assignments)
   857	    receiver_dropped_assignments_host = _sum_int64(receiver_dropped_assignments)
   858	    if dropped_assignments_host != sender_dropped_assignments_host + receiver_dropped_assignments_host:
   859	        raise ValueError("total dropped assignments must equal sender plus receiver dropped assignments")
   860	    total_assignments = batch_size * sequence_length * top_k * num_layers
   861	    receiver_assignments = total_assignments - sender_dropped_assignments_host
   862	    return {
   863	        "moe/dropped_assignments": dropped_assignments_host,
   864	        "moe/drop_fraction": dropped_assignments_host / total_assignments,
   865	        "moe/sender_dropped_assignments": sender_dropped_assignments_host,
   866	        "moe/sender_drop_fraction": sender_dropped_assignments_host / total_assignments,
   867	        "moe/receiver_dropped_assignments": receiver_dropped_assignments_host,
   868	        "moe/receiver_drop_fraction": receiver_dropped_assignments_host / total_assignments,
   869	        "moe/receiver_drop_fraction_of_received": receiver_dropped_assignments_host / max(receiver_assignments, 1),
   870	    }

   873	def _loss_and_grads(params, batch, mp: jmp.Policy, z_loss: float | None):
   874	    def loss_fn(model):
   875	        compute_params = mp.cast_to_compute(model)
   876	        return compute_params.next_token_loss(
   877	            batch.tokens,
   878	            batch.loss_weight,
   879	            mask=batch.attn_mask,
   880	            reduction="mean",
   881	            logsumexp_weight=z_loss,
   882	            return_router_metrics=True,
   883	        )
   884	
   885	    return jax.value_and_grad(loss_fn, has_aux=True)(params)
   886

   117	    @staticmethod
   118	    def _copy_values_to_host(tensor: torch.Tensor) -> Tuple[int, ...]:
   119	        return tuple(int(value) for value in tensor.detach().cpu().tolist())
   120	
   121	    @staticmethod
   122	    def _is_validation_cached(cache: dict[int, tuple], tensor: torch.Tensor, extra) -> bool:
   123	        cached = cache.get(id(tensor))
   124	        return bool(cached and cached[0]() is tensor and cached[1] == int(tensor._version) and cached[2] == extra)
   125	
   126	    @staticmethod
   127	    def _remember_validation(cache: dict[int, tuple], tensor: torch.Tensor, extra) -> None:
   128	        key = id(tensor)
   129	
   130	        def discard(_reference, *, cache=cache, key=key):
   131	            cache.pop(key, None)
   132	
   133	        cache[key] = (weakref.ref(tensor, discard), int(tensor._version), extra)
   134	
   135	    @staticmethod
   136	    def _validate_offset_sequence(values: Tuple[int, ...], *, expert_cnt: int, tokens_sum: int) -> Tuple[int, ...]:
   137	        if len(values) != expert_cnt:
   138	            raise ValueError(f"sample_offsets length mismatch: expected {expert_cnt}, got {len(values)}")
   139	        groups = []
   140	        previous = 0
   141	        for index, value in enumerate(values):
   142	            if value < previous:
   143	                raise ValueError("sample_offsets must be a non-decreasing cumulative sum; " f"index {index} is {value} after {previous}")
   144	            group_k = value - previous
   145	            if group_k % MoEGroupedGemmWgradBF16Kernel.FIX_PAD_SIZE != 0:
   146	                raise ValueError(f"sample_offsets group {index} must be 256-aligned, got {group_k}")
   147	            groups.append(group_k)
   148	            previous = value
   149	        if not values or values[-1] != tokens_sum:
   150	            raise ValueError(f"sample_offsets last value must equal total tokens {tokens_sum}, " f"got {values[-1] if values else None}")
   151	        return tuple(groups)
   152	
   153	    def _validate_offsets_once(self, offsets: torch.Tensor, *, tokens_sum: int) -> None:
   154	        extra = (self.expert_cnt, tokens_sum)
   155	        if self._is_validation_cached(self._validated_offsets, offsets, extra):
   156	            return
   157	        values = self._copy_values_to_host(offsets)
   158	        self._validate_offset_sequence(values, expert_cnt=self.expert_cnt, tokens_sum=tokens_sum)
   159	        self._remember_validation(self._validated_offsets, offsets, extra)
   160	
   161	    def _validate_pointer_values_once(self, pointers: torch.Tensor) -> None:
   162	        if self._is_validation_cached(self._validated_pointer_values, pointers, self.expert_cnt):
   163	            return
   164	        values = self._copy_values_to_host(pointers)
   165	        if any(value == 0 or value % 16 != 0 for value in values):
   166	            raise ValueError("wgrad_ptrs entries must be non-null and 16-byte aligned")
   167	        self._remember_validation(self._validated_pointer_values, pointers, self.expert_cnt)
   168	
   169	    @staticmethod
   170	    def _validate_pointer_array_alignment(tensor: torch.Tensor) -> None:
   171	        if tensor.data_ptr() % 8 != 0:
   172	            raise ValueError("wgrad_ptrs data pointer must be 8-byte aligned")
   173	
   174	    @staticmethod
   175	    def _validate_data_alignment(tensor: torch.Tensor, name: str, alignment: int = 16) -> None:
   176	        if tensor.data_ptr() % alignment != 0:
   177	            raise ValueError(f"{name} data pointer must be {alignment}-byte aligned")
   178	
   179	    @staticmethod
   180	    def _record_pointer_stream(pointers: torch.Tensor, current_stream: cuda.CUstream) -> None:
   181	        handle = int(current_stream)
   182	        torch_current = torch.cuda.current_stream(pointers.device)
   183	        torch_default = torch.cuda.default_stream(pointers.device)
   184	        if handle == torch_current.cuda_stream:
   185	            launch_stream = torch_current
   186	        elif handle == torch_default.cuda_stream:
   187	            launch_stream = torch_default
   188	        else:
   189	            launch_stream = torch.cuda.ExternalStream(handle, device=pointers.device)
   190	        pointers.record_stream(launch_stream)

   201	    @staticmethod
   202	    def _infer_b_major(desc: TensorDesc) -> str:
   203	        tokens, n = desc.shape
   204	        if desc.stride == (1, tokens):
   205	            return "k"
   206	        if desc.stride == (n, 1):
   207	            return "n"
   208	        raise ValueError(f"B tensor must use a supported K-major or N-major layout, got stride {desc.stride}")
   209	
   210	    @staticmethod
   211	    def _expect_device(desc: TensorDesc, device: torch.device, name: str) -> None:
   212	        if desc.device != device:
   213	            raise ValueError(f"{name} must be on {device}, got {desc.device}")
   214	
   215	    def check_support(self) -> bool:
   216	        if self.a_desc.ndim != 2:
   217	            raise ValueError(f"sample_a must be rank-2, got {self.a_desc.shape}")
   218	        if self.b_desc.ndim != 2:
   219	            raise ValueError(f"sample_b must be rank-2, got {self.b_desc.shape}")
   220	        m, tokens_sum = self.a_desc.shape
   221	        tokens_b, n = self.b_desc.shape
   222	        if tokens_b != tokens_sum:
   223	            raise ValueError(f"sample_a and sample_b token dimensions must match, got {tokens_sum} and {tokens_b}")
   224	        self.a_major = self._infer_a_major(self.a_desc)
   225	        self.b_major = self._infer_b_major(self.b_desc)
   226	        self._check_dtype(self.a_desc, torch.bfloat16, "sample_a")
   227	        self._check_dtype(self.b_desc, torch.bfloat16, "sample_b")
   228	        self._check_dtype(self.offsets_desc, torch.int32, "sample_offsets")
   229	        self._check_dtype(self.wgrad_dtype, _OUTPUT_DTYPES, "wgrad_dtype")
   230	        if self.acc_dtype != torch.float32:
   231	            raise ValueError(f"acc_dtype must be torch.float32, got {self.acc_dtype}")
   232	        if any(control is not None for control in self._scale_controls):
   233	            raise ValueError("BF16 wgrad forbids scale and global-scale tensors")
   234	        if self.sf_vec_size != 16:
   235	            raise ValueError(f"BF16 wgrad requires sf_vec_size=16, got {self.sf_vec_size}")
   236	        if self.offsets_desc.shape != (self.expert_cnt,):
   237	            raise ValueError(f"sample_offsets must have shape {(self.expert_cnt,)}, got {self.offsets_desc.shape}")
   238	        if self.offsets_desc.stride != (1,):
   239	            raise ValueError("sample_offsets must be contiguous")
   240	
   241	        if self.weight_mode == MoEWeightMode.DENSE:
   242	            if self.wgrad_desc.ndim != 3:
   243	                raise ValueError(f"sample_wgrad must be rank-3, got {self.wgrad_desc.shape}")
   244	            if self.wgrad_desc.shape != (self.expert_cnt, m, n):
   245	                raise ValueError(f"sample_wgrad shape mismatch: expected {(self.expert_cnt, m, n)}, got {self.wgrad_desc.shape}")
   246	            if self.wgrad_desc.stride != (m * n, n, 1):
   247	                raise ValueError("sample_wgrad must be contiguous in expert/M/N order")
   248	            output_desc = self.wgrad_desc
   249	        else:
   250	            if self.wgrad_shape != (m, n):
   251	                raise ValueError(f"wgrad_shape mismatch: expected {(m, n)}, got {self.wgrad_shape}")
   252	            output_desc = self.single_expert_wgrad_desc
   253	            if output_desc.shape not in ((m, n), (m, n, 1)):
   254	                raise ValueError(f"sample_wgrad_expert shape mismatch: expected {(m, n)}, got {output_desc.shape}")
   255	            expected_stride = (n, 1) if output_desc.ndim == 2 else (n, 1, 1)
   256	            if output_desc.stride != expected_stride:
   257	                raise ValueError("sample_wgrad_expert must be contiguous in M/N order")
   258	            self._check_dtype(output_desc, self.wgrad_dtype, "sample_wgrad_expert")
   259	
   260	        device = self.a_desc.device
   261	        for desc, name in (
   262	            (self.b_desc, "sample_b"),
   263	            (self.offsets_desc, "sample_offsets"),
   264	            (output_desc, "sample_wgrad"),
   265	        ):
   266	            self._expect_device(desc, device, name)
   267	        for name, pointer in self._sample_data_ptrs.items():
   268	            alignment = 4 if name == "sample_offsets" else 16
   269	            if pointer % alignment:
   270	                raise ValueError(f"{name} data pointer must be {alignment}-byte aligned")
   271	
   272	        groups = self._validate_offset_sequence(
   273	            self._sample_offset_values,
   274	            expert_cnt=self.expert_cnt,
   275	            tokens_sum=tokens_sum,
   276	        )
   277	        sample_offsets = self._sample_offsets_ref()
   278	        if sample_offsets is not None and int(sample_offsets._version) == self._sample_offsets_version:
   279	            self._remember_validation(
   280	                self._validated_offsets,
   281	                sample_offsets,
   282	                (self.expert_cnt, tokens_sum),
   283	            )
   284	        elif sample_offsets is not None:
   285	            self._validate_offsets_once(sample_offsets, tokens_sum=tokens_sum)
   286	
   287	        if not self._kernel.can_implement(
   288	            _convert_to_cutlass_data_type(torch.bfloat16),
   289	            _convert_to_cutlass_data_type(self.wgrad_dtype),
   290	            _convert_to_cutlass_data_type(self.acc_dtype),
   291	            self.use_2cta_instrs,
   292	            self.mma_tiler_mn,
   293	            self.cluster_shape_mn,
   294	            m,
   295	            n,
   296	            list(groups),
   297	            self.expert_cnt,
   298	            self.a_major,
   299	            self.b_major,
   300	            self.weight_mode,
   301	            self.input_order,
   302	        ):
   303	            raise ValueError("Unsupported BF16 grouped GEMM wgrad configuration: check mma_tiler, cluster, and alignment")
   304	        if not torch.cuda.is_available():
   305	            raise RuntimeError("CUDA is not available")

     4	"""
     5	MoE BF16 Grouped GEMM Kernel — Weight Gradient (2Dx2D).
     6	
     7	Computes:  A(hidden, tokens_sum) x B(tokens_sum, intermediate)
     8	        -> C(experts, hidden, intermediate)
     9

    11	M (hidden) and N (intermediate) are fixed across all experts.

    59	    """BF16 grouped GEMM kernel for MoE weight gradient (2Dx2D).
    60	
    61	    :param acc_dtype: Accumulator data type (Float32).
    62	    :param use_2cta_instrs: Use 2-CTA MMA instructions.
    63	    :param mma_tiler_mn: MMA tile shape (M, N).
    64	    :param cluster_shape_mn: Cluster shape (M, N).
    65	    :param accumulate_on_output: Use TMA reduce for atomic accumulation.
    66	    :param expert_cnt: Number of experts.
    67	    :param weight_mode: ``MoEWeightMode.DENSE`` or ``MoEWeightMode.DISCRETE`` for output.
    68	    :param input_order: ``WGradInputOrder.Tensor2D`` (default, single global K
    69	        stride across experts) or ``WGradInputOrder.TensorRagged`` (per-expert
    70	        K-contiguous blocks concatenated in memory). Only the unit-stride axis
    71	        of host-side ``mat_a/mat_b`` is meaningful in ``TensorRagged`` mode;
    72	        the non-unit stride values are ignored.
    73	    """
    74	
    75	    FIX_PAD_SIZE = 256
    76	
    77	    @staticmethod
    78	    def can_implement(
    79	        ab_dtype: Type[cutlass.Numeric],
    80	        out_dtype: Type[cutlass.Numeric],
    81	        acc_dtype: Type[cutlass.Numeric],
    82	        use_2cta_instrs: bool,

    84	        cluster_shape_mn: Tuple[int, int],
    85	        m: int,
    86	        n: int,
    87	        group_k_list: list,
    88	        expert_cnt: int,
    89	        a_major: str,
    90	        b_major: str,
    91	        weight_mode: MoEWeightMode,
    92	        input_order: WGradInputOrder,
    93	    ) -> bool:
    94	        """Check whether a BF16 wgrad testcase is supported."""
    95	        result = True
    96	
    97	        if ab_dtype != cutlass.BFloat16:
    98	            result = False
    99	        if out_dtype not in (cutlass.BFloat16, cutlass.Float16, cutlass.Float32):
   100	            result = False
   101	        if acc_dtype != cutlass.Float32:
   102	            result = False
   103	
   104	        if a_major not in ("k", "m") or b_major not in ("k", "n"):
   105	            result = False
   106	        if weight_mode not in (MoEWeightMode.DENSE, MoEWeightMode.DISCRETE):
   107	            result = False
   108	        if input_order not in (WGradInputOrder.Tensor2D, WGradInputOrder.TensorRagged):
   109	            result = False
   110	
   111	        if m <= 0 or n <= 0 or expert_cnt <= 0:
   112	            result = False
   113	        if group_k_list is None:
   114	            return False
   115	        if len(group_k_list) != expert_cnt:
   116	            result = False
   117	
   118	        tokens_sum = 0
   119	        for k_val in group_k_list:
   120	            if k_val < 0 or k_val % MoEGroupedGemmWgradBF16Kernel.FIX_PAD_SIZE != 0:
   121	                result = False
   122	            tokens_sum += k_val
   123	
   124	        if len(mma_tiler_mn) != 2 or len(cluster_shape_mn) != 2:
   125	            return False
   126	
   127	        tile_m, tile_n = mma_tiler_mn
   128	        cluster_m, cluster_n = cluster_shape_mn
   129	        if not ((not use_2cta_instrs and tile_m == 128) or (use_2cta_instrs and tile_m == 256)):
   130	            result = False
   131	        if tile_n not in range(64, 257, 64):
   132	            result = False
   133	        if cluster_m % (2 if use_2cta_instrs else 1) != 0:
   134	            result = False
   135	
   136	        def is_power_of_2(x: int) -> bool:
   137	            return x > 0 and (x & (x - 1)) == 0
   138	
   139	        if cluster_m * cluster_n > 16 or not is_power_of_2(cluster_m) or not is_power_of_2(cluster_n):
   140	            result = False
   141	
   142	        def is_16b_aligned(dtype: Type[cutlass.Numeric], contiguous_elems: int) -> bool:
   143	            elems_per_16b = 16 * 8 // dtype.width
   144	            return contiguous_elems % elems_per_16b == 0
   145	
   146	        a_contiguous_elems = tokens_sum if a_major == "k" else m
   147	        b_contiguous_elems = tokens_sum if b_major == "k" else n
   148	        c_contiguous_elems = n
   149	        if not (
   150	            is_16b_aligned(ab_dtype, a_contiguous_elems) and is_16b_aligned(ab_dtype, b_contiguous_elems) and is_16b_aligned(out_dtype, c_contiguous_elems)
   151	        ):
   152	            result = False
   153	
   154	        return result

{"body":"Reworks the ragged all-to-all expert-parallel MoE backend into a replacement for the pooled-wave hero transport. In an A/B at the hero shape — both arms restored from the live hero's step-6000 checkpoint on real data, one NVL72 rack, transport the only variable — ragged delivers:\n\n- **matching-to-slightly-ahead throughput**: **22.87 vs 22.71 MFU**, with the two arms run back to back on the same rack so placement differences cannot account for the gap (standard deviation across the scored steps: 0.11 for ragged, 0.59 for pooled-wave; three earlier runs of the ragged configuration ranged 22.34–22.58)\n- **~150× lower drop rate**: **0.018%** vs 2.67% of expert assignments under the trained router, with the loss at the scored step correspondingly lower (1.4727 vs 1.4777)\n- **~12 GiB lower runtime device peak**: **137.9 vs 149.9 GiB** at identical steady-state footprint\n\nThis PR does not change the default backend: the `moe_hero_ep` entry points keep `fixed_pooled_wave_all_to_all`, and the ragged backend is opt-in via `moe_implementation=\"ragged_all_to_all\"`.\n\nKey changes:\n\n- **Expert-granular transport data path** — one `ragged_all_to_all` update per (peer, local expert): senders read each expert group's accepted prefix in place and rows arrive grouped by expert, replacing ~1.1 s/step of repeat/sort/compact permutes. With chunking, **+1.5 MFU** over the prior ragged path.\n- **Sequential expert chunks** — local experts run in two chunks with per-chunk capacity, halving the transport buffers XLA cannot rematerialize. Not a tuning choice: the unchunked graph needs 192–194 GiB against 184 GiB HBM and OOMs at the first hero step.\n- **QuACK SM100 grouped GEMMs + cuDNN grouped weight gradients** for the expert MLP — the core of the earlier **16.1% → 21.9%** stack. Those two figures were measured before the current protocol and are not directly comparable to the numbers above. SM100 + SiLU only; everything else keeps XLA's `ragged_dot`.\n- **Device-initiated transport** — the ragged backend engages XLA's device-initiated (NCCL LSA) ragged-all-to-all kernel through `XLA_FLAGS` defaults it sets itself. The kernel partitions copy work across CTAs by bytes, so splitting a peer transfer into several updates buys no load balance and only adds granularity cost (21.12 MFU when we measured it at 64 splits, against 22.34–22.58 unsplit). The backend therefore exposes no splitting option, and the two flags are not overridable: the host-launched kernel would need both flags cleared together plus the update splitting this backend does not produce, so a partial override would silently run a configuration nothing here measures.\n- **Fused combine gather + weighted sum** and a backend-specific scheduling posture (latency-hiding scheduler off, collective overlap 1) — part of the stack above. The scheduler is off for memory, not scheduling: its longer live ranges fail NCCL's first-step allocations at the current HBM budget, and a follow-up that offloads layer activations to pinned host re-enables it at a measured gain (#8317).\n- **`--master-params` option** — fp32 weights on device instead of a pinned-host master: **~+0.4 MFU**.\n- **Validation harness** — the 4-GPU `ragged_ep_check` gates forward and gradients against an exact fp32 dense reference, both at a capacity high enough that nothing is clipped and in the drop regime the hero actually trains in. For the latter it computes which assignments survive in NumPy — accepted rows are the prefix of each expert group under a greedy first-sender-wins gate, so the surviving set is a pure function of the routing and the capacity — and requires the transport to equal dense over exactly the rows it kept. It also records which kernels the run selected, since that depends on the device and the installed packages. Nothing runs it on a schedule, and it sits under `experiments/` rather than `tests/cluster/`, because the repository has no marker, fixture, or workflow for a test that needs particular accelerators (#8704). That same gap silences the two unit tests that exercise this backend end to end: both skip under CI's single CPU device, and `addopts` carries no `-rs`, so the skips do not appear in the output. Separately, a d768 ablation pair (10.8k steps, identical settings) has ragged ahead of pooled-wave on train loss (**1.939 vs 1.956**), eval bpb (**0.975 vs 1.033**), and steady-state drop rate (**~0.03% vs ~2.7%** at that scale).\n\nContext: pooled-wave is the hero default but drops a low-single-digit percentage of expert assignments at steady state. The goal here is at-least-parity throughput with materially fewer drops, without touching the model or precision. That trade matters most for long-context training, where a batch holds fewer, longer examples: per-shard token pools average over fewer documents, routing skew grows, and capacity clipping bites harder. Memory is a second operational motivation. The hero's intermittent OOMs traced to the step peak overshooting the cuda_async release threshold (#8490), and main now holds the production pooled-wave hero under that threshold by shrinking the train-step arena (#8507, slop factor 85) with the master kept on pinned host. Ragged reaches the same safety with ~12 GiB to spare: in that same paired run, where both arms carry the heavier fp32-on-device master, pooled-wave still peaks 11.7 GiB over the threshold (149.9 vs 138.2 GiB) while ragged sits just under it (137.9 GiB) — headroom that loosens the arena and master-placement constraints the pooled posture needs.\n\nCaveat — **quoted throughput depends on an XLA patch, shipped separately.** The device kernel itself runs on stock XLA (jax ≥ 0.11.1 defines the flags; older jaxlibs abort at import on unknown `XLA_FLAGS` entries), but its stock CTA assignment starves under trained-router skew and measures ~19.4% MFU at this shape. The quoted numbers use a one-commit balanced-CTA-assignment patch, [mcwitt/xla@d6d3132a90](https://github.com/mcwitt/xla/commit/d6d3132a90dada14d570b66da38eccb7f6d774a3) (2.35× on the standalone transport benchmark; being upstreamed). This PR does not ship a wheel; the pinned build lands in a follow-up. {"body":"Issue is to describe the Hero Run scaling ladder, config, and track its performance.\n\nTracking: https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/reports/535B-A23B-18T-Token-Hero-Run-Scaling-Ladder--VmlldzoxNzc2MDM5Ng\n\nDetails on the full model spec is in the comment below.\n\n### Why run a scaling ladder?\n\n1. This lets us project the model performance and compare it to the scaling projections of our prior recipes. If our projection looks meaningfully worse, then we know we need to go back to the drawing board on some aspect of the model or data. This step can catch a lot of bugs!\n2. We can look at how training dynamics change as we scale, in particular the gradient norms and token dropping. In our last run, the scaling ladder caught gradient norm growth to over 4 as we scaled out token horizon, which caused us to find a fix with logit z loss. Later ablations showed that without this fix, runs under certain conditions like high batch size would completely blow up mid-run.\n3. We can project our evals across the entire trajectory of the run. This means that across the entire ~100 day run, we know exactly how we are doing compared to the projection. If at any point we fail to match the projection, it can prompt early investigation into training dynamics.\n4. If something strange start to happen in the Hero run, we can reference the smaller scales runs to see if its actually normal. For instance, in prior scaling ladders we saw the grad norm grow heavily up to 40% of the run, then decrease as the LR decays. When we saw this on the hero run, having the small scale reference gave us confidence we didn't need to intervene, as long as the gradient followed the same pattern (steady growth for 40% of run).\n5. It only costs 1% of total compute.\n### What is our EP hardware implementation?\nDescribed in detail here: https://storage.googleapis.com/marin-public/rav/moe-fixed-wave-a2a-384/2026.08.17/index.html.\nWe are hand-rolling our own EP implementation, props to @ravwojdyla, since we have not found a more performant variant on JAX XLA on GPU. \n\n### What is our long context extension plan?\nOur last run was 8k seqlen pretrain, followed by 65k extension for 1T tokens, followed by 262k extension (to occur end of Aug). Prior to that run we have used 4k seqlen pretrain. For this run we are going back to 4k seqlen pretrain to start, to enable better expert balancing (twice as many sequences per batch). We wanted to minimize risk here because our EP token dropping implementation is more experimental. (our last run was dropless FSDP). Prior tests showed token dropping grow from ~7% to ~40% when extending from 4k to 65k seqlen. Our new pooled/wave EP drops about half as many tokens (3%) at 4k seqlen; however the token dropping is likely still excessively high at 65k seqlen.\n\nWe will spend 1-2 days to do an early cooldown at roughly 10-20 days into the run, to enable RL experiments, which will be our first full scale data point at how longer context influences dropping. A nice property of this test is that the cooldown will not contaminate or impact the main run, so we have some flexibility to collect data on how an extension approach impacts dropping. Our options will be:\n1. If we have landed a Jax Mixture of Kittens or dropless ragged all-to-all, then we can swap to that for the cooldown. Prior small scale tests showed the model was robust from swapping from small amounts of dropping (5%) to dropless mid-run.\n2. Otherwise, we can increase our capacity factor, and accept some amount of dropping.\n3. If we find that neither of these options are suitable, the next option would be to introduce sequence level balancing mid-run (though forcing the experts to re-specialize mid-run will likely be worse than accepting some amount of dropping). \n\nExtending context will involve updating qk_mult according to mscale=X⋅ln(new_seqlen/old_seqlen)+1, testing coefficients near 0.1 (can quickly eval a range during extension on 1 rack). If the data from the first cooldown looks smooth, will plan on 4k-\u003e8k at 50 pct into run, then 8k-\u003e65k at about 95 pct, then a targeted 262k phase near end, based on data we collect from taking the 67B-A2B from 65k to 262k.\n\nHave further derisked token dropping by staying at 2 shared experts, each at half width. 8 active experts are also at half width. However due to latent MoE 2x compression on active experts, we are effectively running at hidden_dim width neurons shared, and 2x hidden_dim neurons routed. Having 1/3 of our neurons come from shared expert will provide a stronger backbone in the event of high dropping. We see learning still progress with zero loss spikes even at 40 pct dropping.\n\n### What if we see delays, beyond our buffer (hardware failure, MFU degradation)?\nUp to roughly 25% of the token budget, the default approach will be to compensate by decreasing the token horizon of the run. Data is the two-phase Harrier mixture on the fuzzy-deduped datakit store. Below: model, optimizer, training/topology, the MFU optimizations, the scaling ladder, and outputs.\n\n## 1. Model\n\n### Hyperparameters\n| | |\n|---|---|\n| hidden_dim | 6144 |\n| num_layers | 48 |\n| num_heads | 48 · head_dim 128 |\n| num_kv_heads | 12 stored — **local 12 / global 6** (GQA 4:1 local, 8:1 global) |\n| num_experts / top-k | **384 / 8** |\n| intermediate_dim (expert FFN) | 3072 (= hidden/2) |\n| latent_dim (LatentMoE) | 3072 (= hidden/2) |\n| shared experts | 2 dense SwiGLU, width 3072 |\n| vocab_size | 128,256 |\n| max_seq_len | 4096 · sliding_window 2048 · global_every 4 |\n| capacity_factor / transport cf | 1.15 / 1.15 · num_expert_waves 3 |\n| qk_mult | 1.3 · rope θ=10000 (fused, half-RoPE) |\n| sconv | sites k/attn/mlp, kernel 4 |\n| init | 0.5/√hidden = 0.006379 (uniform, truncated normal) |\n| active / total params | 22.76B / 535.3B |\n\n### Features\nAll structural (always on) unless noted.\n- **All-MoE**: every block's MLP is a QB-routed `MoEMLP`; no dense-only layers.\n- **GQA, split local/global KV**: sliding-window (local) layers keep 12 KV heads, full-causal (global) layers 6; K/V are sliced/aligned per layer via `lax.cond`, so global layers pay less KV compute.\n- **QB routing (histogram estimator)**: router takes top-(K+1) on biased logits; the (K+1)-th logit is the per-token threshold `alpha`, the first K are selected. Each expert's threshold `beta` is the **(1−K/E) upper quantile of the margins `score−alpha`**, read from a **10k-bin histogram over the live global `[min, max]` range** (a `pmin`/`pmax` this step sets the grid; a summed-histogram cumulative count gives the per-expert quantile). The router bias `−beta` is applied on the **next step** as a zero-mean stop-gradient offset — balances expert selection without touching gradients. The histogram estimator is a smoother global quantile than a per-device top-k.\n- **Sigmoid combine weights**: combine weights are `sigmoid(unbiased selected logits)`, rescaled so the K weights sum to a fixed 2.5 (not softmax).\n- **LatentMoE + learnable latent RMS-norm**: tokens are compressed `hidden→latent (3072)`, passed through a **learnable RMSNorm (`latent_norm`, per-dim gain)** to decouple the expert-input scale from the down-projection init, then dispatched to experts **entirely in latent space**, and projected `latent→hidden` after the weighted combine. The router still reads the full-width token. (Also halves the all-to-all payload — see §4.)\n- **Shared experts**: 2 dense SwiGLU experts run on every token in parallel with the routed path; their output is added before the residual.\n- **RMSNorm on embeddings and readout**: a learnable-gain [`RMSNorm`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/12d8b6f09f96ad4f0277445765c1a00dbc81d5be/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/model.py#L594) is applied to the token embeddings ([`embed_norm`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/12d8b6f09f96ad4f0277445765c1a00dbc81d5be/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/model.py#L1223)) and before the untied `lm_head` ([`final_norm`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/12d8b6f09f96ad4f0277445765c1a00dbc81d5be/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/model.py#L1165)), in addition to the per-block `rms_attn`/`rms_mlp`; the GatedNorm below wraps each of these.\n- **GatedNorm**: learnable `x·sigmoid(silu(x·w_down)·w_up)` gate (rank-128 bottleneck) applied after **every** RMSNorm (attn, mlp, embed, final).\n- **XSA (Exclusive Self-Attention)**: per head, subtract the component of the attention output parallel to its own value vector: `z = y − (yᵀv/‖v‖²)v` — removes the copy-through component so each head learns new information rather than passing V unchanged.\n- **Attention head gate**: each head's attention output is scaled by a learned `2·sigmoid(x·attn_gate)`, one scalar per head; `attn_gate` is zero-initialized (gate starts at 1).\n- **RMS qk-norm**: Q and K are RMS-normed (non-parametric) per head before RoPE.\n- **Partial (half) RoPE, fused**: rotary is applied to **only the first half of head_dim**; the second half is rope-free on every layer. Single-pass fused kernel (θ=10000).\n- **Rope-free global layers**: every 4th layer + the last are full-causal and **rope-free** (NoPE, qk_mult-only); the others are sliding-window with RoPE. One per-layer boolean drives mask, KV-head count, and rope together.\n- **ShortConv (SConv)**: depthwise causal 1-D conv (kernel 4), identity-init, packed-document segment-masked, at three sites — after K, on the attention-branch output, on the MoE-branch output.\n- **Embeddings**: `token_embed` fully replicated + shard-local lookup; `lm_head` (`output_proj`) FSDP+model-sharded; **untied**.\n- **Logit z-loss**: the final-logit logsumexp is penalized (`logsumexp_weight = z_loss_weight = 1e-4`) and **added to the training loss** (fused into the CE) — controls gradient-norm growth at long token horizons (the fix the prior scaling ladder surfaced). Distinct from the router z-loss, which is logging-only.\n- **Monitoring** (logged, not in loss): per-layer routing entropy, load-balance loss, router z-loss, and sender/receiver token-drop fractions.\n\n## 2. Optimizer — MuonH / AdamH / Adam (compute-scaled)\n\nThree groups via `optax.multi_transform` + a path mask:\n- **MuonH** — attention, expert-MLP, shared-expert, latent, and GatedNorm **matrices**. Newton–Schulz orthogonalization (bf16, `backend_steps=5`, quintic coeffs, nesterov momentum 0.95) → **Frobenius-hyperball** scale-invariant step (moves along the direction, projects back onto the param's Frobenius sphere; norms in fp32). Orthogonalization is distributed **intra-rack only** (never crosses DCN); 4D expert stacks are handled without gathering the matrix dims.\n- **AdamH** — the **lm_head readout**: Adam moments give the direction, then the same norm-preserving hyperball projection. Gets the MuonH LR, not `adam_lr`.\n- **Adam** — `token_embed`, router, router_bias, `attn_gate`, 1-D norm gains, and the tiny SConv kernels.\n\n### Hyperparameters (@ 18T budget)\n| | |\n|---|---|\n| MuonH LR | 0.003291 |\n| Adam LR | 0.000759 (MuonH = 13/3 × Adam = 4.33×) |\n| beta1 / beta2 | **0.90** / 0.95 |\n| epsilon | 6.04e-15 (Adam) · muon_epsilon 1e-8 |\n| momentum / nesterov | 0.95 / true |\n| use_syrk | true (Blackwell SM100 symmetric GEMM for X·Xᵀ) |\n| LR schedule | linear · warmup 1% · min_lr_ratio 0.05 |\n| max_grad_norm | none (no global clip) |\n| z_loss_weight | 1e-4 (logit z-loss, fused into CE) |\n\nThe MuonH/AdamH groups carry **no decoupled weight decay** — they regularize purely through the norm-preserving hyperball projection. LR / beta2 / epsilon are compute-scaled from the Aug hero refit (issues #7856 / #8003, R²=0.978, seq_len=8192): `adam_lr = 0.087571 · tokens^-0.3461 · hidden^-0.3448 · √(tokens_per_batch)`, `beta2 = clip(0.999^(tpb/131072), 0.95, 0.9999)`, `epsilon = 9.676e-18 · √(tokens/tpb)`.\n\n## 3. Training \u0026 topology\n- **Hardware**: 11× GB200 NVL72 racks. **EP64 within each rack** (expert axis = 16 nodes × 4 GPUs), **data-parallel replication across the 11 racks over DCN**. Mesh `(replica_dcn=11, data, expert=64, model)`; token/batch sharded over `(replica_dcn, data, expert)`.\n- **batch_size** 11,264 seqs (1024 × 11 racks) · **seq_len** 4096 · **num_train_steps** 390,139 · **total_tokens 18.0T** · **791 tokens/active-param**.\n- **compute_budget** ≈ 2.70e24 FLOPs (analytic, fwd+bwd, latent-corrected).\n- **mixed_precision** `params=bf16, compute=bf16, output=bf16`, with **fp32 pinned-host master params** + **offloaded optimizer state** (see §4). Router path kept fp32 before top-k/softmax/QB stats.\n- **data**: two-phase Harrier mixture (15T pretrain + 3.75T cooldown, phase-1 at 80% of steps) on the fuzzy-deduped datakit store, marin tokenizer; simulated epoching against the 18.75T reference with a ≤8-epoch cap (max cell exposure ~2.1). 4k-seq pretrain deliberately (2× sequences/batch for expert balancing; token-drop grows sharply at longer context).\n\n## 4. MFU / performance optimizations\n- **Hand-rolled fixed pooled-wave all-to-all EP** — every device packs sends into one fixed `[expert_shards, pool_capacity]` pool and receives into fixed per-wave `[local_experts, receiver_cap, H]` buffers; all sizes are compile-time constants so the `all_to_all` runs on fully static shapes. Chosen over `ragged_all_to_all` to avoid a metadata/offset collective and dynamic shapes; **expert IDs ride in-band** as packed header rows in the same activation collective (no separate metadata collective). [EP writeup](https://storage.googleapis.com/marin-public/rav/moe-fixed-wave-a2a-384/2026.08.17/index.html)\n- **Static waves (3)** stripe each destination pool round-robin by rank, shrinking per-wave buffers; each wave is rematerialized to cap activation memory. **Round-robin receiver allocation** keeps overflow drops unbiased across senders.\n- **LatentMoE halves EP transport bytes** — the all-to-all carries latent-width (3072) rows both directions instead of hidden (6144). FLOP accounting is corrected for this so MFU isn't overstated.\n- **gpu_fa4_cute FA4 attention** — bf16 CuTe segmented flash attention with per-token key lower bounds (no materialized `[B,S,S]` mask, no THD compaction), real GQA, custom CUTLASS backward, grug-tuned 64×64 tiles for B200/head_dim-128. **Sliding-window vs full-causal is just a different lower-bound array feeding the same kernel** → cuts attention FLOPs on the ~3/4 local layers. Bounds are precomputed **outside** the layer scan.\n- **Fused linear-softmax cross-entropy (bf16 backward)** — `implementation=\"xla_fast_bwd\"`: streams the whole 65,536-token rank shard over `v_block=4096` vocab blocks with online logsumexp (never materializes the `[B,128k]` logits), and runs both **backward GEMMs in bf16 on tensor cores** (vs fp32/TF32) for ~2.3× on the hero CE shape; the logit z-loss is fused as `logsumexp_weight·lse²`. `v_block=4096` is the dominant MFU lever for the 128k vocab.\n- **Fused depthwise causal ShortConv (Pallas)** — the SConv sites dispatch to a fused **Pallas Triton depthwise causal conv** kernel on GPU (forward and `dx` bit-identical to the pad-and-shift reference, `dw` as accurate; pad-and-shift fallback off-GPU). Shard-local (depthwise, no cross-channel/cross-shard term → no collectives); the channel dim is FSDP-sharded so its gradient reduce-scatters.\n- **Muon symmetric-GEMM (QuACK SM100) Newton–Schulz** — the two `X·Xᵀ` products in each Newton–Schulz iteration go through a **QuACK symmetric CuTe GEMM** (`use_syrk`) that computes only one triangle of the symmetric output (`A = X·Xᵀ`, then `B = b·A + c·(A·Aᵀ)`) instead of a full dense matmul — roughly halves the matmul FLOPs per iteration on the batched 4D expert stacks, where orthogonalization is the bulk of the optimizer's compute.\n- **Padded + resharded distributed Muon (intra-rack)** — the stacked leaves are orthogonalized in parallel across the rack instead of gathered to one device: 3D non-expert stacks **zero-pad the leading (layer) axis** so it divides the intra-rack shard count, then reshard the padded stack over the batch mesh axes (one matrix per shard, `vmap`'d, resliced back after); 4D expert stacks `[layers, experts, fan_in, fan_out]` reshard over the `expert` axis (or the largest batch-axis subset that divides `layers·experts`) and run under a `shard_map` **without ever gathering the `fan_in×fan_out` matrix dims**, then reshard back to the parameter's own spec. All of this is pinned **intra-rack only** — the reshards deliberately exclude the `replica_dcn` axis so Newton–Schulz never runs a collective over the slow inter-rack DCN link.\n- **ArrayStacked + `jax.lax.scan`** — all 48 blocks are one compiled body scanned over the layer axis, cutting compile time and HBM; router/QB collectives are structured around the scan.\n- **Heterogeneous global/local layers under one homogeneous scan** — `lax.scan` needs a single compiled body, so the ways global (full-causal, rope-free) and local (sliding-window) layers differ can't be Python branches — each rides in as a traced per-layer scalar and is selected *inside* the body:\n  - **RoPE diff** — global layers run rope-free. Rather than branch, RoPE is **always computed** and then selected with `jnp.where` on a per-layer `disable_rope` scalar, so both layer kinds compile to the same body.\n  - **GQA diff** — local layers keep 12 KV heads, global layers 6. K/V are stored at the max (12) width and sliced-then-`align_kv_heads`'d to the per-layer count via `lax.cond(is_global, …)`, so global layers pay less KV compute without changing the stacked parameter shape.\n  - **Mask diff** — the full-causal and sliding-window FA4 bound arrays are precomputed **outside** the scan and the per-layer one is picked with `jnp.where` (the sliding window is a static mask field the body can't vary), so the window rides in as the selected bounds.\n- **remat `recompute_all`** — the whole block is recomputed in backward (lowest memory); a `save_moe` mode is available to keep the MoE dispatch tensors and skip re-running the EP collectives.\n- **Capacity-factor token dropping (1.15)** bounds expert compute and transport buffers regardless of routing imbalance; drops are counted/logged as sender/receiver fractions.\n- **use_syrk** routes the optimizer's `X·Xᵀ` through QuACK's SM100 symmetric GEMM; Newton–Schulz runs in bf16 (halved all-gather bytes) and **intra-rack only**.\n- **offload_opt_state + FP32_PINNED_HOST master** — optimizer state and fp32 master weights live in pinned host RAM, shuttled device↔host each step, to leave HBM for the pooled all-to-all buffers. (The pinned-host restore is fixed in [#8443](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/8443) and memory-bounded in [#8480](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/8480); the hero now writes an hourly temporary checkpoint and resumes from it after a preemption.)\n- **XLA/runtime flags** — latency-hiding scheduler on, collective-overlap limit 4, CUDA async allocator, 192GB host-memory limit, PGLE off, GPU command buffers disabled.\n\n## 5. Scaling ladder (why, and the rungs)\nRuns at 5 widths on one iso-ratio recipe (**791 tokens/active-param**, same mixture + simulated epoching + per-cell epoch structure), ≈1% of total compute, to (a) project performance vs prior recipes and catch bugs, (b) watch grad-norm and token-drop dynamics across scale (the last ladder caught grad-norm growth → the logit z-loss fix), and (c) project evals across the ~100-day trajectory.\n\n| rung | racks | batch | steps | tokens | active |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| d768 | 1 | 1024 | 11,420 | 48B | 61M |\n| d1024 | 2 | 2048 | 15,276 | 128B | 162M |\n| d1536 | 6 | 6144 | 15,128 | 381B | 481M |\n| d2048 | 11 | 11,264 | 20,072 | 926B | 1.2B |\n| **d6144 (hero)** | 11 | 11,264 | 390,139 | **18.0T** | 22.8B |\n\n## 6. I have a question regarding the motivation behind LatentMoE. Since the training system uses GB200 NVL72 with high-bandwidth NVLink, I am curious why a latent representation is introduced before expert dispatch. Is LatentMoE mainly motivated by reducing communication overhead at larger scales (e.g., beyond a single NVLink domain), or does it also provide benefits beyond communication optimization, such as improving model capability? Thanks!\n\nOn its own, LatentMoE halves the comms cost. We found that putting a learnable RMSNorm on the latent projection improved model capability as well, so LatentMoE w/ norm performed better than no latent MoE. Without this learnable RMSNorm, we run into activation scaling issue and see 30 percent worse quality. We also found going from top 4 of 192 to top 8 of 384 (half sized) gave 15 percent quality gain. But it doubles comms cost. So one way to view latentMoE is it enables 4/192-\u003e8/384 without change to either comms or compute.","createdAt":"2026-08-25T06:53:00Z","url":"https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8435#issuecomment-5406648997"},{"body":"Thanks for the detailed reply! At very small scale if I do an exact active:total replica (dense 3x width hidden instead of 1x), I get same quality and 20% better MFU than our baseline. We never ended up doing large scale ablation here, since I was more worried about token dropping dynamics. Also the way we are using jax scan makes it a awkward to have different behavior per layer. I am less optimistic about alternating dense/moe long term, because with mature mixture-of-kittens kernels the MFU hit of MoE is probably not that high anyways.\n2. Hmm I separately saw some early positive results from Inkling relative position embedding that gave lower loss. But our kernel was not quite fast enough to justify. And perhaps more importantly, the kernel was a bit buggy if I changed sliding window length. I think it should be good on global layers too, since its limited to just the most recent X (512 or 1024) positions. I am more bullish on relative position embedding + MLA. Since MLA has very janky approach to RoPE, which requires replicating 64 head dims across every head. Relative position embedding fixes this. Have to be a bit careful with ablations here because at very small scale RoPE on global looks much better than NoPE on global. (but this fades with scale)\n3. So initial AdamH on embed looked good. But later I did learning rate sweep, and if LR was 40% too high, was seeing grad spikes up to 20. I think what was happening (guessing) was rare tokens were having their norm driven to near zero, and then getting massive grad when they finally ended up in the batch. (we have rms_norm on embed that will apply high growth multiplier to small vocab embeds) Dont want any features in the model that require perfectly optimal hypers. So reverted it.\n\n\u003cimg width=\"874\" height=\"552\" alt=\"Image\" src=\"https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/096aaa54-f17f-4e96-8a8e-a1a825f84270\" /\u003e","createdAt":"2026-08-27T01:23:04Z","url":"https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8435#issuecomment-5433154702"},{"body":"Thanks, this is really helpful.\n\nMy motivation for alternating dense/MoE is less about the current MFU gap and more about separation of concerns: dense layers handle common computation, while MoE layers handle specialization. Keeping them as two clean execution patterns seems to leave more room for independent kernel, scheduling, and parallelism optimization, even if MoE kernels improve substantially.\n\nFor position encoding, my preference for learned relative PE on local layers + NoPE on global layers is mainly to avoid positional extrapolation entirely. With a fixed local window, the relative-position range never changes as context grows, while global attention stays purely content-addressed. I agree this probably needs larger-scale ablations to judge properly.\n","createdAt":"2026-08-27T02:50:16Z","url":"https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8435#issuecomment-5433737400"},{"body":"Is there a way to see interim model generations from the ongoing run?","createdAt":"2026-08-28T23:14:07Z","url":"https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8435#issuecomment-5458731192"}],"number":8435,"state":"OPEN","title":"[Hero Run] 535B-A23B on 18T tokens","url":"https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8435"}
