    30	    def __init__(
   130	        def discard(_reference, *, cache=cache, key=key):
   131	            cache.pop(key, None)
   132	
   133	        cache[key] = (weakref.ref(tensor, discard), int(tensor._version), extra)
   134	
   135	    @staticmethod
   136	    def _validate_offset_sequence(values: Tuple[int, ...], *, expert_cnt: int, tokens_sum: int) -> Tuple[int, ...]:
   137	        if len(values) != expert_cnt:
   138	            raise ValueError(f"sample_offsets length mismatch: expected {expert_cnt}, got {len(values)}")
   139	        groups = []
   140	        previous = 0
   141	        for index, value in enumerate(values):
   142	            if value < previous:
   143	                raise ValueError("sample_offsets must be a non-decreasing cumulative sum; " f"index {index} is {value} after {previous}")
   144	            group_k = value - previous
   145	            if group_k % MoEGroupedGemmWgradBF16Kernel.FIX_PAD_SIZE != 0:
   146	                raise ValueError(f"sample_offsets group {index} must be 256-aligned, got {group_k}")
   147	            groups.append(group_k)
   148	            previous = value
   149	        if not values or values[-1] != tokens_sum:
   150	            raise ValueError(f"sample_offsets last value must equal total tokens {tokens_sum}, " f"got {values[-1] if values else None}")
   151	        return tuple(groups)
   152	
   153	    def _validate_offsets_once(self, offsets: torch.Tensor, *, tokens_sum: int) -> None:
   154	        extra = (self.expert_cnt, tokens_sum)
   155	        if self._is_validation_cached(self._validated_offsets, offsets, extra):
   156	            return
   157	        values = self._copy_values_to_host(offsets)
   158	        self._validate_offset_sequence(values, expert_cnt=self.expert_cnt, tokens_sum=tokens_sum)
   208	        raise ValueError(f"B tensor must use a supported K-major or N-major layout, got stride {desc.stride}")
   209	
   210	    @staticmethod
   211	    def _expect_device(desc: TensorDesc, device: torch.device, name: str) -> None:
   212	        if desc.device != device:
   213	            raise ValueError(f"{name} must be on {device}, got {desc.device}")
   214	
   215	    def check_support(self) -> bool:
   216	        if self.a_desc.ndim != 2:
   217	            raise ValueError(f"sample_a must be rank-2, got {self.a_desc.shape}")
   218	        if self.b_desc.ndim != 2:
   219	            raise ValueError(f"sample_b must be rank-2, got {self.b_desc.shape}")
   220	        m, tokens_sum = self.a_desc.shape
   221	        tokens_b, n = self.b_desc.shape
   222	        if tokens_b != tokens_sum:
   223	            raise ValueError(f"sample_a and sample_b token dimensions must match, got {tokens_sum} and {tokens_b}")
   224	        self.a_major = self._infer_a_major(self.a_desc)
   225	        self.b_major = self._infer_b_major(self.b_desc)
   226	        self._check_dtype(self.a_desc, torch.bfloat16, "sample_a")
   227	        self._check_dtype(self.b_desc, torch.bfloat16, "sample_b")
   228	        self._check_dtype(self.offsets_desc, torch.int32, "sample_offsets")
   229	        self._check_dtype(self.wgrad_dtype, _OUTPUT_DTYPES, "wgrad_dtype")
   230	        if self.acc_dtype != torch.float32:
   231	            raise ValueError(f"acc_dtype must be torch.float32, got {self.acc_dtype}")
   232	        if any(control is not None for control in self._scale_controls):
   233	            raise ValueError("BF16 wgrad forbids scale and global-scale tensors")
   234	        if self.sf_vec_size != 16:
   235	            raise ValueError(f"BF16 wgrad requires sf_vec_size=16, got {self.sf_vec_size}")
   236	        if self.offsets_desc.shape != (self.expert_cnt,):
   237	            raise ValueError(f"sample_offsets must have shape {(self.expert_cnt,)}, got {self.offsets_desc.shape}")
   238	        if self.offsets_desc.stride != (1,):
   239	            raise ValueError("sample_offsets must be contiguous")
   240	
   241	        if self.weight_mode == MoEWeightMode.DENSE:
   242	            if self.wgrad_desc.ndim != 3:
   243	                raise ValueError(f"sample_wgrad must be rank-3, got {self.wgrad_desc.shape}")
   244	            if self.wgrad_desc.shape != (self.expert_cnt, m, n):
   245	                raise ValueError(f"sample_wgrad shape mismatch: expected {(self.expert_cnt, m, n)}, got {self.wgrad_desc.shape}")
   246	            if self.wgrad_desc.stride != (m * n, n, 1):
   247	                raise ValueError("sample_wgrad must be contiguous in expert/M/N order")
   248	            output_desc = self.wgrad_desc
   249	        else:
   250	            if self.wgrad_shape != (m, n):
   251	                raise ValueError(f"wgrad_shape mismatch: expected {(m, n)}, got {self.wgrad_shape}")
   252	            output_desc = self.single_expert_wgrad_desc
   253	            if output_desc.shape not in ((m, n), (m, n, 1)):
   254	                raise ValueError(f"sample_wgrad_expert shape mismatch: expected {(m, n)}, got {output_desc.shape}")
   255	            expected_stride = (n, 1) if output_desc.ndim == 2 else (n, 1, 1)
   256	            if output_desc.stride != expected_stride:
   257	                raise ValueError("sample_wgrad_expert must be contiguous in M/N order")
   258	            self._check_dtype(output_desc, self.wgrad_dtype, "sample_wgrad_expert")
   259	
   260	        device = self.a_desc.device
   261	        for desc, name in (
   262	            (self.b_desc, "sample_b"),
   263	            (self.offsets_desc, "sample_offsets"),
   264	            (output_desc, "sample_wgrad"),
   265	        ):
   266	            self._expect_device(desc, device, name)
   267	        for name, pointer in self._sample_data_ptrs.items():
   268	            alignment = 4 if name == "sample_offsets" else 16
   269	            if pointer % alignment:
   270	                raise ValueError(f"{name} data pointer must be {alignment}-byte aligned")
   271	
   272	        groups = self._validate_offset_sequence(
   273	            self._sample_offset_values,
   274	            expert_cnt=self.expert_cnt,
   275	            tokens_sum=tokens_sum,
   276	        )
   277	        sample_offsets = self._sample_offsets_ref()
   278	        if sample_offsets is not None and int(sample_offsets._version) == self._sample_offsets_version:
   279	            self._remember_validation(
   280	                self._validated_offsets,
   281	                sample_offsets,
   282	                (self.expert_cnt, tokens_sum),
   283	            )
   284	        elif sample_offsets is not None:
   285	            self._validate_offsets_once(sample_offsets, tokens_sum=tokens_sum)
   286	
   287	        if not self._kernel.can_implement(
   288	            _convert_to_cutlass_data_type(torch.bfloat16),
   289	            _convert_to_cutlass_data_type(self.wgrad_dtype),
   290	            _convert_to_cutlass_data_type(self.acc_dtype),
   291	            self.use_2cta_instrs,
   292	            self.mma_tiler_mn,
   293	            self.cluster_shape_mn,
   294	            m,
   295	            n,
   296	            list(groups),
   297	            self.expert_cnt,
   298	            self.a_major,
   299	            self.b_major,
   300	            self.weight_mode,
   301	            self.input_order,
   302	        ):
   303	            raise ValueError("Unsupported BF16 grouped GEMM wgrad configuration: check mma_tiler, cluster, and alignment")
   304	        if not torch.cuda.is_available():
   305	            raise RuntimeError("CUDA is not available")
   306	        major, minor = torch.cuda.get_device_capability(self.a_desc.device)
   307	        capability = major * 10 + minor
   308	        if capability < 100:
   309	            raise RuntimeError(f"GroupedGemmWgradSm100 requires SM100+, found SM{capability} on {self.a_desc.device}")
   310	        self._is_supported = True
   311	        return True
   312

   314	        self._ensure_support_checked()

    58	class MoEGroupedGemmWgradBF16Kernel:
    59	    """BF16 grouped GEMM kernel for MoE weight gradient (2Dx2D).
    60	
    61	    :param acc_dtype: Accumulator data type (Float32).
    62	    :param use_2cta_instrs: Use 2-CTA MMA instructions.
    63	    :param mma_tiler_mn: MMA tile shape (M, N).
    64	    :param cluster_shape_mn: Cluster shape (M, N).
    65	    :param accumulate_on_output: Use TMA reduce for atomic accumulation.
    66	    :param expert_cnt: Number of experts.
    67	    :param weight_mode: ``MoEWeightMode.DENSE`` or ``MoEWeightMode.DISCRETE`` for output.
    68	    :param input_order: ``WGradInputOrder.Tensor2D`` (default, single global K
    69	        stride across experts) or ``WGradInputOrder.TensorRagged`` (per-expert
    70	        K-contiguous blocks concatenated in memory). Only the unit-stride axis
    71	        of host-side ``mat_a/mat_b`` is meaningful in ``TensorRagged`` mode;
    72	        the non-unit stride values are ignored.
    73	    """
    74	
    75	    FIX_PAD_SIZE = 256
    76	
    77	    @staticmethod
    78	    def can_implement(
    79	        ab_dtype: Type[cutlass.Numeric],
    80	        out_dtype: Type[cutlass.Numeric],
    81	        acc_dtype: Type[cutlass.Numeric],
    82	        use_2cta_instrs: bool,
    83	        mma_tiler_mn: Tuple[int, int],
    84	        cluster_shape_mn: Tuple[int, int],
    85	        m: int,
    86	        n: int,
    87	        group_k_list: list,
    88	        expert_cnt: int,
    89	        a_major: str,
    90	        b_major: str,
    91	        weight_mode: MoEWeightMode,
    92	        input_order: WGradInputOrder,
    93	    ) -> bool:
    94	        """Check whether a BF16 wgrad testcase is supported."""
    95	        result = True
    96	
    97	        if ab_dtype != cutlass.BFloat16:
    98	            result = False
    99	        if out_dtype not in (cutlass.BFloat16, cutlass.Float16, cutlass.Float32):
   100	            result = False
   101	        if acc_dtype != cutlass.Float32:
   102	            result = False
   103	
   104	        if a_major not in ("k", "m") or b_major not in ("k", "n"):
   105	            result = False
   106	        if weight_mode not in (MoEWeightMode.DENSE, MoEWeightMode.DISCRETE):
   107	            result = False
   108	        if input_order not in (WGradInputOrder.Tensor2D, WGradInputOrder.TensorRagged):
   109	            result = False
   110	
   111	        if m <= 0 or n <= 0 or expert_cnt <= 0:
   112	            result = False
   113	        if group_k_list is None:
   114	            return False
   115	        if len(group_k_list) != expert_cnt:
   116	            result = False
   117	
   118	        tokens_sum = 0
   119	        for k_val in group_k_list:
   120	            if k_val < 0 or k_val % MoEGroupedGemmWgradBF16Kernel.FIX_PAD_SIZE != 0:
   121	                result = False
   122	            tokens_sum += k_val
   123	
   124	        if len(mma_tiler_mn) != 2 or len(cluster_shape_mn) != 2:
   125	            return False
   126	
   127	        tile_m, tile_n = mma_tiler_mn
   128	        cluster_m, cluster_n = cluster_shape_mn
   129	        if not ((not use_2cta_instrs and tile_m == 128) or (use_2cta_instrs and tile_m == 256)):
   130	            result = False

    83	
    84	# The maximum allowed relative deviation between the ragged and dense kernels.
    85	#
    86	# Gradients are gated on a median rather than the max. Both paths compute the same mathematical
    87	# gradient, so every difference is bf16 reduction-order noise: the two orders leave most entries
    88	# bit-identical, while a few cancellation-heavy entries lose their leading digits and push the
    89	# relative max to around 0.5 on a correct run. Gate on the max and a correct transport fails.
    90	#
    91	# Take the median per slice of the leading axis and gate the worst slice. A tensor-wide median
    92	# tolerates corruption confined to under half the entries, which is the shape of the faults worth
    93	# catching: one expert's weight gradient is an eighth of `w13`, one shard's token block a quarter
    94	# of the `x` gradient. Neither moves a tensor-wide median; both move their own slice's.
    95	TOLERANCE = 5e-2
    96	
    97	
    98	class TransportKernel(StrEnum):
    99	    """Which ragged all-to-all kernel the run exercises.
   100	
   286	        jnp.asarray(x, jnp.float32), jnp.asarray(w13, jnp.float32), jnp.asarray(w2, jnp.float32)
   287	    )
   288	    return np.asarray(out), grads
   289	
   290	
   291	def _maxdiff_vs_dense(out, dense) -> float:
   292	    denom = float(np.max(np.abs(dense))) + 1e-6
   293	    return float(np.max(np.abs(np.asarray(out, np.float32) - dense))) / denom
   294	
   295	
   296	def _graddiff(a, b) -> GradDiff:
   297	    """Compare a gradient tuple against the reference, worst tensor wins each statistic.
   298	
   299	    Slices run along the leading axis: expert for the two weight gradients, token for the
   300	    activation gradient. See the ``TOLERANCE`` comment for why the gate reads a per-slice median.
   301	    """
   302	    maxes, medians, slice_medians = [], [], []
   303	    for u, v in zip(a, b, strict=True):
   304	        u = np.asarray(u, dtype=np.float32)
   305	        v = np.asarray(v, dtype=np.float32)
   306	        denom = float(np.max(np.abs(u)) + np.max(np.abs(v))) + 1e-6
   307	        absdiff = np.abs(u - v)
   308	        maxes.append(float(np.max(absdiff)) / denom)
   309	        medians.append(float(np.median(absdiff)) / denom)
   310	        per_slice = np.median(absdiff.reshape(absdiff.shape[0], -1), axis=1)
   311	        slice_medians.append(float(np.max(per_slice)) / denom)
   312	    return GradDiff(worst_entry=max(maxes), tensor_median=max(medians), worst_slice_median=max(slice_medians))
   313	
   314

{"body":"`cudnn_grouped_wgrad` (`lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe/cudnn_wgrad_cute.py`, introduced by PR #8081 and carried by its derived measurement branches — not yet on main) silently computes wrong weight gradients whenever a group's row offset is not 64-aligned. `pad_grouped_rows` pads groups to 8-row boundaries, but the cuDNN CuTeDSL grouped Wgrad kernel needs 64: at 8- or 32-aligned offsets the max error against a NumPy reference is 0.17-0.55 relative to the gradient peak, versus the bf16 accumulation floor of ~0.003 at 64/128/256 alignment. Measured on GB200 at production dims (k=6144 n=3072 and k=1536 n=6144, G=3, realistic routing counts); the error grows with group count (0.17 at G=2 to 0.55 at G=12 at k=512).\n\nEvery `*_cudnn_cute` MoE backend on the PR #8081 lineage routes dw13/dw2 through this kernel, so training runs on those branches computed corrupted expert weight gradients for any routing outcome whose group sizes were not 64-multiples — effectively always. Loss curves in short benchmark runs still fall, which is why it went unnoticed; existing grad conformance checks passed because their `atol` absorbed the error at small-magnitude weights.\n\nReproduce:\n1. On a GB200 pod with the gpu extra, on the PR #8081 branch: build `x [2560, 512]`, `d [2560, 1536]` bf16, `group_sizes = [900, 800, 860]`.\n2. Compare `cudnn_grouped_wgrad(x, d, gs)` against per-group `x[off:off+s].T @ d[off:off+s]` in NumPy.\n\nExpected: max error at the bf16 floor (~0.003 relative to peak), as it is when every group size is a 64-multiple.\n\nFix validated on branch `marin-ep-8081` (f2c9f702f3): raise `_GROUP_ALIGNMENT` to 64 (the smallest exact alignment; 32 still fails). Cost is at most 63 zero rows per group. With the fix, a full MoE layer's dw13/dw2 match the oracle at 0.004 rel-to-peak on 4 GPUs.\n","closedAt":"2026-08-17T19:19:05Z","comments":[{"body":"🤖 Correction: this was an integration-contract violation, not an XLA correctness bug. cuDNN Frontend 1.27.0 requires every BF16 grouped-Wgrad expert token count (offsets[e] - offsets[e - 1]) to be divisible by 256, with the final offset equal to the total token count. Marin bypassed the public facade and called the internal MoEGroupedGemmWgradBF16Kernel with 8-row padding.\n\nA direct PyTorch/cuDNN Frontend reduction on GB200 produced 0.269 relative error for 8-aligned starts, 0.217 for 32-aligned starts, and 0 for 64-aligned starts. That confirms the internal kernel silently corrupts these inputs, but the 8-, 32-, and 64-aligned cases are all outside the public cuDNN contract unless they are also 256-aligned.\n\nThe correct integration fix is to pad every group to a multiple of 256, or use another kernel whose supported contract accepts smaller groups. Raising the padding from 8 to 64 avoids the observed corruption but still violates the cuDNN Frontend contract.","url":"https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8339#issuecomment-5318708904"}],"number":8339,"state":"CLOSED","title":"[levanter] cuDNN grouped Wgrad silently wrong unless group offsets are 64-aligned","url":"https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8339"}
{"body":"Reworks the ragged all-to-all expert-parallel MoE backend into a replacement for the pooled-wave hero transport. In an A/B at the hero shape — both arms restored from the live hero's step-6000 checkpoint on real data, one NVL72 rack, transport the only variable — ragged delivers:\n\n- **matching-to-slightly-ahead throughput**: **22.87 vs 22.71 MFU**, with the two arms run back to back on the same rack so placement differences cannot account for the gap (standard deviation across the scored steps: 0.11 for ragged, 0.59 for pooled-wave; three earlier runs of the ragged configuration ranged 22.34–22.58)\n- **~150× lower drop rate**: **0.018%** vs 2.67% of expert assignments under the trained router, with the loss at the scored step correspondingly lower (1.4727 vs 1.4777)\n- **~12 GiB lower runtime device peak**: **137.9 vs 149.9 GiB** at identical steady-state footprint\n\nThis PR does not change the default backend: the `moe_hero_ep` entry points keep `fixed_pooled_wave_all_to_all`, and the ragged backend is opt-in via `moe_implementation=\"ragged_all_to_all\"`.\n\nKey changes:\n\n- **Expert-granular transport data path** — one `ragged_all_to_all` update per (peer, local expert): senders read each expert group's accepted prefix in place and rows arrive grouped by expert, replacing ~1.1 s/step of repeat/sort/compact permutes. With chunking, **+1.5 MFU** over the prior ragged path.\n- **Sequential expert chunks** — local experts run in two chunks with per-chunk capacity, halving the transport buffers XLA cannot rematerialize. Not a tuning choice: the unchunked graph needs 192–194 GiB against 184 GiB HBM and OOMs at the first hero step.\n- **QuACK SM100 grouped GEMMs + cuDNN grouped weight gradients** for the expert MLP — the core of the earlier **16.1% → 21.9%** stack. Those two figures were measured before the current protocol and are not directly comparable to the numbers above. SM100 + SiLU only; everything else keeps XLA's `ragged_dot`.\n- **Device-initiated transport** — the ragged backend engages XLA's device-initiated (NCCL LSA) ragged-all-to-all kernel through `XLA_FLAGS` defaults it sets itself. The kernel partitions copy work across CTAs by bytes, so splitting a peer transfer into several updates buys no load balance and only adds granularity cost (21.12 MFU when we measured it at 64 splits, against 22.34–22.58 unsplit). The backend therefore exposes no splitting option, and the two flags are not overridable: the host-launched kernel would need both flags cleared together plus the update splitting this backend does not produce, so a partial override would silently run a configuration nothing here measures.\n- **Fused combine gather + weighted sum** and a backend-specific scheduling posture (latency-hiding scheduler off, collective overlap 1) — part of the stack above. The scheduler is off for memory, not scheduling: its longer live ranges fail NCCL's first-step allocations at the current HBM budget, and a follow-up that offloads layer activations to pinned host re-enables it at a measured gain (#8317).\n- **`--master-params` option** — fp32 weights on device instead of a pinned-host master: **~+0.4 MFU**.\n- **Validation harness** — the 4-GPU `ragged_ep_check` gates forward and gradients against an exact fp32 dense reference, both at a capacity high enough that nothing is clipped and in the drop regime the hero actually trains in. For the latter it computes which assignments survive in NumPy — accepted rows are the prefix of each expert group under a greedy first-sender-wins gate, so the surviving set is a pure function of the routing and the capacity — and requires the transport to equal dense over exactly the rows it kept. It also records which kernels the run selected, since that depends on the device and the installed packages. Nothing runs it on a schedule, and it sits under `experiments/` rather than `tests/cluster/`, because the repository has no marker, fixture, or workflow for a test that needs particular accelerators (#8704). That same gap silences the two unit tests that exercise this backend end to end: both skip under CI's single CPU device, and `addopts` carries no `-rs`, so the skips do not appear in the output. Separately, a d768 ablation pair (10.8k steps, identical settings) has ragged ahead of pooled-wave on train loss (**1.939 vs 1.956**), eval bpb (**0.975 vs 1.033**), and steady-state drop rate (**~0.03% vs ~2.7%** at that scale).\n\nContext: pooled-wave is the hero default but drops a low-single-digit percentage of expert assignments at steady state. The goal here is at-least-parity throughput with materially fewer drops, without touching the model or precision. That trade matters most for long-context training, where a batch holds fewer, longer examples: per-shard token pools average over fewer documents, routing skew grows, and capacity clipping bites harder. Memory is a second operational motivation. The hero's intermittent OOMs traced to the step peak overshooting the cuda_async release threshold (#8490), and main now holds the production pooled-wave hero under that threshold by shrinking the train-step arena (#8507, slop factor 85) with the master kept on pinned host. Ragged reaches the same safety with ~12 GiB to spare: in that same paired run, where both arms carry the heavier fp32-on-device master, pooled-wave still peaks 11.7 GiB over the threshold (149.9 vs 138.2 GiB) while ragged sits just under it (137.9 GiB) — headroom that loosens the arena and master-placement constraints the pooled posture needs.\n\nCaveat — **quoted throughput depends on an XLA patch, shipped separately.** The device kernel itself runs on stock XLA (jax ≥ 0.11.1 defines the flags; older jaxlibs abort at import on unknown `XLA_FLAGS` entries), but its stock CTA assignment starves under trained-router skew and measures ~19.4% MFU at this shape. The quoted numbers use a one-commit balanced-CTA-assignment patch, [mcwitt/xla@d6d3132a90](https://github.com/mcwitt/xla/commit/d6d3132a90dada14d570b66da38eccb7f6d774a3) (2.35× on the standalone transport benchmark; being upstreamed). This PR does not ship a wheel; the pinned build lands in a follow-up. The 4-GPU validation has been run green on GB200 against the host-launched kernel, which exercises the expert-MLP kernels and the offset arithmetic; re-running it against the device kernel needs that build.\n\nPart of #8317. Per-arm ledgers and trace anatomy live on `research/mcwitt/8317-ragged-tune` under `autoresearch/loop-260821-leg2/` (one-shot tuning) and on `research/mcwitt/8317-dk-native` under `autoresearch/loop-260824-dkperf/` (device-kernel root-cause and the balanced-CTA result).\n\n\n\n","mergeCommit":"dc584e765d0c5cfe69700edfec880d6f174d4916","mergedAt":"2026-08-28T00:31:04Z","number":8549,"state":"MERGED","url":"https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/8549"}
{"comments":[{"body":"🤖 # Job Summary: Aug Hero Run — 535B-A23B MoE (d6144), 18T tokens\n\nFull-scale EP64 MoE pretrain: d6144, **535.3B total / 22.76B active** params, **18.0T tokens** (~**2.70e24** train FLOPs, fwd+bwd), on GB200 with our hand-rolled pooled-wave expert-parallel all-to-all. Data is the two-phase Harrier mixture on the fuzzy-deduped datakit store. Below: model, optimizer, training/topology, the MFU optimizations, the scaling ladder, and outputs.\n\n## 1. Model\n\n### Hyperparameters\n| | |\n|---|---|\n| hidden_dim | 6144 |\n| num_layers | 48 |\n| num_heads | 48 · head_dim 128 |\n| num_kv_heads | 12 stored — **local 12 / global 6** (GQA 4:1 local, 8:1 global) |\n| num_experts / top-k | **384 / 8** |\n| intermediate_dim (expert FFN) | 3072 (= hidden/2) |\n| latent_dim (LatentMoE) | 3072 (= hidden/2) |\n| shared experts | 2 dense SwiGLU, width 3072 |\n| vocab_size | 128,256 |\n| max_seq_len | 4096 · sliding_window 2048 · global_every 4 |\n| capacity_factor / transport cf | 1.15 / 1.15 · num_expert_waves 3 |\n| qk_mult | 1.3 · rope θ=10000 (fused, half-RoPE) |\n| sconv | sites k/attn/mlp, kernel 4 |\n| init | 0.5/√hidden = 0.006379 (uniform, truncated normal) |\n| active / total params | 22.76B / 535.3B |\n\n### Features\nAll structural (always on) unless noted.\n- **All-MoE**: every block's MLP is a QB-routed `MoEMLP`; no dense-only layers.\n- **GQA, split local/global KV**: sliding-window (local) layers keep 12 KV heads, full-causal (global) layers 6; K/V are sliced/aligned per layer via `lax.cond`, so global layers pay less KV compute.\n- **QB routing (histogram estimator)**: router takes top-(K+1) on biased logits; the (K+1)-th logit is the per-token threshold `alpha`, the first K are selected. Each expert's threshold `beta` is the **(1−K/E) upper quantile of the margins `score−alpha`**, read from a **10k-bin histogram over the live global `[min, max]` range** (a `pmin`/`pmax` this step sets the grid; a summed-histogram cumulative count gives the per-expert quantile). The router bias `−beta` is applied on the **next step** as a zero-mean stop-gradient offset — balances expert selection without touching gradients. The histogram estimator is a smoother global quantile than a per-device top-k.\n- **Sigmoid combine weights**: combine weights are `sigmoid(unbiased selected logits)`, rescaled so the K weights sum to a fixed 2.5 (not softmax).\n- **LatentMoE + learnable latent RMS-norm**: tokens are compressed `hidden→latent (3072)`, passed through a **learnable RMSNorm (`latent_norm`, per-dim gain)** to decouple the expert-input scale from the down-projection init, then dispatched to experts **entirely in latent space**, and projected `latent→hidden` after the weighted combine. The router still reads the full-width token. (Also halves the all-to-all payload — see §4.)\n- **Shared experts**: 2 dense SwiGLU experts run on every token in parallel with the routed path; their output is added before the residual.\n- **RMSNorm on embeddings and readout**: a learnable-gain [`RMSNorm`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/12d8b6f09f96ad4f0277445765c1a00dbc81d5be/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/model.py#L594) is applied to the token embeddings ([`embed_norm`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/12d8b6f09f96ad4f0277445765c1a00dbc81d5be/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/model.py#L1223)) and before the untied `lm_head` ([`final_norm`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/12d8b6f09f96ad4f0277445765c1a00dbc81d5be/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/model.py#L1165)), in addition to the per-block `rms_attn`/`rms_mlp`; the GatedNorm below wraps each of these.\n- **GatedNorm**: learnable `x·sigmoid(silu(x·w_down)·w_up)` gate (rank-128 bottleneck) applied after **every** RMSNorm (attn, mlp, embed, final).\n- **XSA (Exclusive Self-Attention)**: per head, subtract the component of the attention output parallel to its own value vector: `z = y − (yᵀv/‖v‖²)v` — removes the copy-through component so each head learns new information rather than passing V unchanged.\n- **Attention head gate**: each head's attention output is scaled by a learned `2·sigmoid(x·attn_gate)`, one scalar per head; `attn_gate` is zero-initialized (gate starts at 1).\n- **RMS qk-norm**: Q and K are RMS-normed (non-parametric) per head before RoPE.\n- **Partial (half) RoPE, fused**: rotary is applied to **only the first half of head_dim**; the second half is rope-free on every layer. Single-pass fused kernel (θ=10000).\n- **Rope-free global layers**: every 4th layer + the last are full-causal and **rope-free** (NoPE, qk_mult-only); the others are sliding-window with RoPE. One per-layer boolean drives mask, KV-head count, and rope together.\n- **ShortConv (SConv)**: depthwise causal 1-D conv (kernel 4), identity-init, packed-document segment-masked, at three sites — after K, on the attention-branch output, on the MoE-branch output.\n- **Embeddings**: `token_embed` fully replicated + shard-local lookup; `lm_head` (`output_proj`) FSDP+model-sharded; **untied**.\n- **Logit z-loss**: the final-logit logsumexp is penalized (`logsumexp_weight = z_loss_weight = 1e-4`) and **added to the training loss** (fused into the CE) — controls gradient-norm growth at long token horizons (the fix the prior scaling ladder surfaced). Distinct from the router z-loss, which is logging-only.\n- **Monitoring** (logged, not in loss): per-layer routing entropy, load-balance loss, router z-loss, and sender/receiver token-drop fractions.\n\n## 2. Optimizer — MuonH / AdamH / Adam (compute-scaled)\n\nThree groups via `optax.multi_transform` + a path mask:\n- **MuonH** — attention, expert-MLP, shared-expert, latent, and GatedNorm **matrices**. Newton–Schulz orthogonalization (bf16, `backend_steps=5`, quintic coeffs, nesterov momentum 0.95) → **Frobenius-hyperball** scale-invariant step (moves along the direction, projects back onto the param's Frobenius sphere; norms in fp32). Orthogonalization is distributed **intra-rack only** (never crosses DCN); 4D expert stacks are handled without gathering the matrix dims.\n- **AdamH** — the **lm_head readout**: Adam moments give the direction, then the same norm-preserving hyperball projection. Gets the MuonH LR, not `adam_lr`.\n- **Adam** — `token_embed`, router, router_bias, `attn_gate`, 1-D norm gains, and the tiny SConv kernels.\n\n### Hyperparameters (@ 18T budget)\n| | |\n|---|---|\n| MuonH LR | 0.003291 |\n| Adam LR | 0.000759 (MuonH = 13/3 × Adam = 4.33×) |\n| beta1 / beta2 | **0.90** / 0.95 |\n| epsilon | 6.04e-15 (Adam) · muon_epsilon 1e-8 |\n| momentum / nesterov | 0.95 / true |\n| use_syrk | true (Blackwell SM100 symmetric GEMM for X·Xᵀ) |\n| LR schedule | linear · warmup 1% · min_lr_ratio 0.05 |\n| max_grad_norm | none (no global clip) |\n| z_loss_weight | 1e-4 (logit z-loss, fused into CE) |\n\nThe MuonH/AdamH groups carry **no decoupled weight decay** — they regularize purely through the norm-preserving hyperball projection. LR / beta2 / epsilon are compute-scaled from the Aug hero refit (issues #7856 / #8003, R²=0.978, seq_len=8192): `adam_lr = 0.087571 · tokens^-0.3461 · hidden^-0.3448 · √(tokens_per_batch)`, `beta2 = clip(0.999^(tpb/131072), 0.95, 0.9999)`, `epsilon = 9.676e-18 · √(tokens/tpb)`.\n\n## 3. Training \u0026 topology\n- **Hardware**: 11× GB200 NVL72 racks. **EP64 within each rack** (expert axis = 16 nodes × 4 GPUs), **data-parallel replication across the 11 racks over DCN**. Mesh `(replica_dcn=11, data, expert=64, model)`; token/batch sharded over `(replica_dcn, data, expert)`.\n- **batch_size** 11,264 seqs (1024 × 11 racks) · **seq_len** 4096 · **num_train_steps** 390,139 · **total_tokens 18.0T** · **791 tokens/active-param**.\n- **compute_budget** ≈ 2.70e24 FLOPs (analytic, fwd+bwd, latent-corrected).\n- **mixed_precision** `params=bf16, compute=bf16, output=bf16`, with **fp32 pinned-host master params** + **offloaded optimizer state** (see §4). Router path kept fp32 before top-k/softmax/QB stats.\n- **data**: two-phase Harrier mixture (15T pretrain + 3.75T cooldown, phase-1 at 80% of steps) on the fuzzy-deduped datakit store, marin tokenizer; simulated epoching against the 18.75T reference with a ≤8-epoch cap (max cell exposure ~2.1). 4k-seq pretrain deliberately (2× sequences/batch for expert balancing; token-drop grows sharply at longer context).\n\n## 4. MFU / performance optimizations\n- **Hand-rolled fixed pooled-wave all-to-all EP** — every device packs sends into one fixed `[expert_shards, pool_capacity]` pool and receives into fixed per-wave `[local_experts, receiver_cap, H]` buffers; all sizes are compile-time constants so the `all_to_all` runs on fully static shapes. Chosen over `ragged_all_to_all` to avoid a metadata/offset collective and dynamic shapes; **expert IDs ride in-band** as packed header rows in the same activation collective (no separate metadata collective). [EP writeup](https://storage.googleapis.com/marin-public/rav/moe-fixed-wave-a2a-384/2026.08.17/index.html)\n- **Static waves (3)** stripe each destination pool round-robin by rank, shrinking per-wave buffers; each wave is rematerialized to cap activation memory. **Round-robin receiver allocation** keeps overflow drops unbiased across senders.\n- **LatentMoE halves EP transport bytes** — the all-to-all carries latent-width (3072) rows both directions instead of hidden (6144). FLOP accounting is corrected for this so MFU isn't overstated.\n- **gpu_fa4_cute FA4 attention** — bf16 CuTe segmented flash attention with per-token key lower bounds (no materialized `[B,S,S]` mask, no THD compaction), real GQA, custom CUTLASS backward, grug-tuned 64×64 tiles for B200/head_dim-128. **Sliding-window vs full-causal is just a different lower-bound array feeding the same kernel** → cuts attention FLOPs on the ~3/4 local layers. Bounds are precomputed **outside** the layer scan.\n- **Fused linear-softmax cross-entropy (bf16 backward)** — `implementation=\"xla_fast_bwd\"`: streams the whole 65,536-token rank shard over `v_block=4096` vocab blocks with online logsumexp (never materializes the `[B,128k]` logits), and runs both **backward GEMMs in bf16 on tensor cores** (vs fp32/TF32) for ~2.3× on the hero CE shape; the logit z-loss is fused as `logsumexp_weight·lse²`. `v_block=4096` is the dominant MFU lever for the 128k vocab.\n- **Fused depthwise causal ShortConv (Pallas)** — the SConv sites dispatch to a fused **Pallas Triton depthwise causal conv** kernel on GPU (forward and `dx` bit-identical to the pad-and-shift reference, `dw` as accurate; pad-and-shift fallback off-GPU). Shard-local (depthwise, no cross-channel/cross-shard term → no collectives); the channel dim is FSDP-sharded so its gradient reduce-scatters.\n- **Muon symmetric-GEMM (QuACK SM100) Newton–Schulz** — the two `X·Xᵀ` products in each Newton–Schulz iteration go through a **QuACK symmetric CuTe GEMM** (`use_syrk`) that computes only one triangle of the symmetric output (`A = X·Xᵀ`, then `B = b·A + c·(A·Aᵀ)`) instead of a full dense matmul — roughly halves the matmul FLOPs per iteration on the batched 4D expert stacks, where orthogonalization is the bulk of the optimizer's compute.\n- **Padded + resharded distributed Muon (intra-rack)** — the stacked leaves are orthogonalized in parallel across the rack instead of gathered to one device: 3D non-expert stacks **zero-pad the leading (layer) axis** so it divides the intra-rack shard count, then reshard the padded stack over the batch mesh axes (one matrix per shard, `vmap`'d, resliced back after); 4D expert stacks `[layers, experts, fan_in, fan_out]` reshard over the `expert` axis (or the largest batch-axis subset that divides `layers·experts`) and run under a `shard_map` **without ever gathering the `fan_in×fan_out` matrix dims**, then reshard back to the parameter's own spec. All of this is pinned **intra-rack only** — the reshards deliberately exclude the `replica_dcn` axis so Newton–Schulz never runs a collective over the slow inter-rack DCN link.\n- **ArrayStacked + `jax.lax.scan`** — all 48 blocks are one compiled body scanned over the layer axis, cutting compile time and HBM; router/QB collectives are structured around the scan.\n- **Heterogeneous global/local layers under one homogeneous scan** — `lax.scan` needs a single compiled body, so the ways global (full-causal, rope-free) and local (sliding-window) layers differ can't be Python branches — each rides in as a traced per-layer scalar and is selected *inside* the body:\n  - **RoPE diff** — global layers run rope-free. Rather than branch, RoPE is **always computed** and then selected with `jnp.where` on a per-layer `disable_rope` scalar, so both layer kinds compile to the same body.\n  - **GQA diff** — local layers keep 12 KV heads, global layers 6. K/V are stored at the max (12) width and sliced-then-`align_kv_heads`'d to the per-layer count via `lax.cond(is_global, …)`, so global layers pay less KV compute without changing the stacked parameter shape.\n  - **Mask diff** — the full-causal and sliding-window FA4 bound arrays are precomputed **outside** the scan and the per-layer one is picked with `jnp.where` (the sliding window is a static mask field the body can't vary), so the window rides in as the selected bounds.\n- **remat `recompute_all`** — the whole block is recomputed in backward (lowest memory); a `save_moe` mode is available to keep the MoE dispatch tensors and skip re-running the EP collectives.\n- **Capacity-factor token dropping (1.15)** bounds expert compute and transport buffers regardless of routing imbalance; drops are counted/logged as sender/receiver fractions.\n- **use_syrk** routes the optimizer's `X·Xᵀ` through QuACK's SM100 symmetric GEMM; Newton–Schulz runs in bf16 (halved all-gather bytes) and **intra-rack only**.\n- **offload_opt_state + FP32_PINNED_HOST master** — optimizer state and fp32 master weights live in pinned host RAM, shuttled device↔host each step, to leave HBM for the pooled all-to-all buffers. (The pinned-host restore is fixed in [#8443](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/8443) and memory-bounded in [#8480](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/8480); the hero now writes an hourly temporary checkpoint and resumes from it after a preemption.)\n- **XLA/runtime flags** — latency-hiding scheduler on, collective-overlap limit 4, CUDA async allocator, 192GB host-memory limit, PGLE off, GPU command buffers disabled.\n\n## 5. Scaling ladder (why, and the rungs)\nRuns at 5 widths on one iso-ratio recipe (**791 tokens/active-param**, same mixture + simulated epoching + per-cell epoch structure), ≈1% of total compute, to (a) project performance vs prior recipes and catch bugs, (b) watch grad-norm and token-drop dynamics across scale (the last ladder caught grad-norm growth → the logit z-loss fix), and (c) project evals across the ~100-day trajectory.\n\n| rung | racks | batch | steps | tokens | active |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| d768 | 1 | 1024 | 11,420 | 48B | 61M |\n| d1024 | 2 | 2048 | 15,276 | 128B | 162M |\n| d1536 | 6 | 6144 | 15,128 | 381B | 481M |\n| d2048 | 11 | 11,264 | 20,072 | 926B | 1.2B |\n| **d6144 (hero)** | 11 | 11,264 | 390,139 | **18.0T** | 22.8B |\n\n## 6.      6

     8	with the JAX ``cutlass_call`` signature ``(stream, *inputs, *outputs, **scalars)``
     9	that reuses QuACK's ``GemmGatedSm100`` kernel, then wrap it with

    11	pre-sorted by expert (varlen_m via ``cu_seqlens_m``; no A_idx gather).
    12	
    13	A[M,K] @ B[E,K,2N]  -> (per expert group) -> SwiGLU -> PostAct[M,N]
    14	"""

    16

    18	import jax.numpy as jnp

    35	}

    40

    45	):
    46	    """Return a ``@cute.jit`` launcher with the cutlass_call signature.
    47	
    48	    Signature: (stream, mA, mB, mCuSeqlens, mD, mPostAct)
    49	      mA:[M,K] tokens (k-major)  mB:[E,K,2N] weights  mCuSeqlens:[E+1] int32

    54	    @cute.jit
    55	    def launcher(stream, mA, mB, mCuSeqlens, mD, mPostAct):
    56	        gemm = GemmGatedSm100(
    57	            _ACC,
    58	            a_dtype,
    59	            tile_mn,
    60	            cluster_mnk,
    61	            gather_A=False,
    62	            use_clc_persistence=use_clc_persistence,
    63	        )
    64	        epi_args = GemmActMixin.EpilogueArguments(
    65	            mPostAct,
    66	            act,  # SwiGLU activation function (Constexpr)
    67	            mRowVecBroadcast=None,
    68	            mColVecBroadcast=None,
    69	        )
    70	        scheduler_args = make_scheduler_args(max_active_clusters, max_swizzle, None)
    71	        varlen_args = make_varlen_args(mCuSeqlens, None, None)
    72	        gemm(mA, mB, mD, None, epi_args, scheduler_args, varlen_args, stream)
    73	
    74	    return launcher
    75	
    76	
    77	def quack_gated_grouped_gemm(
    78	    x_sort,
    79	    w_gate_up,
    80	    cu_seqlens,
    81	    *,
    82	    activation="swiglu",
    83	    tile_mn=(256, 128),
    84	    cluster_mnk=(2, 1, 1),
    85	    max_swizzle=8,
    86	    use_clc_persistence=False,
    87	    return_preact=False,
    88	):
    89	    """Grouped SwiGLU expert GEMM via QuACK's SM100 kernel.
    90	
    91	    x_sort: [M, K] tokens sorted by expert. w_gate_up: [E, K, 2N]. cu_seqlens: [E+1] int32.
    92	    Returns postact [M, N].
    93	    """
    94	    M, K = x_sort.shape
    95	    N2 = w_gate_up.shape[2]
    96	    N = N2 // 2
    97	    a_dtype = _cute_dtype(x_sort.dtype)
    98	    if jax.default_backend() == "cpu":
    99	        max_active_clusters = _FALLBACK_MAX_ACTIVE_CLUSTERS
   100	    else:
   101	        max_active_clusters = get_max_active_clusters(cluster_mnk[0] * cluster_mnk[1])
   102	    launcher = _build_launcher(
   103	        a_dtype=a_dtype,
   104	        tile_mn=tile_mn,
   105	        cluster_mnk=cluster_mnk,
   106	        activation=activation,
   107	        max_active_clusters=max_active_clusters,
   108	        max_swizzle=max_swizzle,
   109	        use_clc_persistence=use_clc_persistence,
   110	    )
   111	    ts = cjax.TensorSpec
   112	    # divisibility is in physical-dim order (contiguous dim gets the vector width).
   113	    # B is physically [E,K,2N] but the kernel wants it as [K,2N,E] (expert = trailing
   114	    # batch/L mode); express that with mode=(1,2,0) rather than a physical transpose.
   115	    a_spec = ts(divisibility=(1, 8), static=False)  # [M,K] k-major
   116	    # B is physically [E,K,2N]; kernel wants n-major logical [2N,K,E] (leading_dim 0).
   117	    b_spec = ts(mode=(2, 1, 0), divisibility=(1, 1, 8), static=False)
   118	    cu_spec = ts(static=False)  # [E+1] int32
   119	    d_spec = ts(divisibility=(1, 8), static=False)  # [M,2N] n-major
   120	    p_spec = ts(divisibility=(1, 8), static=False)  # [M,N]  n-major
   121	    call = cutlass_call(
   122	        launcher,
   123	        output_shape_dtype=(
   124	            jax.ShapeDtypeStruct((M, N2), x_sort.dtype),
   125	            jax.ShapeDtypeStruct((M, N), x_sort.dtype),
   126	        ),
   127	        input_spec=(a_spec, b_spec, cu_spec),
   128	        output_spec=(d_spec, p_spec),
   129	        use_static_tensors=False,
   130	    )
   131	    preact, postact = call(x_sort, w_gate_up, cu_seqlens.astype(jnp.int32))
   132	    return (preact, postact) if return_preact else postact
   133	
   134	
   135	@cute_launcher_factory
   136	def _build_plain_launcher(
   137	    *, a_dtype, tile_mn, cluster_mnk, max_active_clusters, max_swizzle, use_clc_persistence=False
   138	):
   139	    """Return a ``@cute.jit`` plain grouped-GEMM launcher."""
   140	
   141	    @cute.jit
   142	    def launcher(stream, mA, mB, mCuSeqlens, mD):
   143	        gemm = GemmDefaultSm100(
   144	            _ACC, a_dtype, tile_mn, cluster_mnk, gather_A=False, use_clc_persistence=use_clc_persistence
   145	        )
   146	        epi_args = GemmDefaultEpiMixin.EpilogueArguments()
   147	        scheduler_args = make_scheduler_args(max_active_clusters, max_swizzle, None)
   148	        varlen_args = make_varlen_args(mCuSeqlens, None, None)
   149	        gemm(mA, mB, mD, None, epi_args, scheduler_args, varlen_args, stream)
   150	
   151	    return launcher
   152	
   153	
   154	def quack_grouped_gemm(
   155	    a,
   156	    w,
   157	    cu_seqlens,
   158	    *,
   159	    b_major="n",
   160	    tile_mn=(256, 128),
   161	    cluster_mnk=(2, 1, 1),
   162	    max_swizzle=8,
   163	    use_clc_persistence=False,
   164	):
   165	    """Plain grouped GEMM a[M,K] @ w -> [M,N], grouped by cu_seqlens (varlen_m).
   166	
   167	    b_major='n': w is [E,K,N] (n-major, mode (2,1,0)).  b_major='k': w is [E,N,K]
   168	    (k-major, mode (1,2,0)) for transposed/backward contractions."""
   169	    M, K = a.shape
   170	    N = w.shape[2] if b_major == "n" else w.shape[1]
   171	    _bmode = (2, 1, 0) if b_major == "n" else (1, 2, 0)
   172	    a_dtype = _cute_dtype(a.dtype)
   173	    if jax.default_backend() == "cpu":
   174	        mac = _FALLBACK_MAX_ACTIVE_CLUSTERS
   175	    else:
   176	        mac = get_max_active_clusters(cluster_mnk[0] * cluster_mnk[1])
   177	    launcher = _build_plain_launcher(
   178	        a_dtype=a_dtype,
   179	        tile_mn=tile_mn,
   180	        cluster_mnk=cluster_mnk,
   181	        max_active_clusters=mac,
   182	        max_swizzle=max_swizzle,
   183	        use_clc_persistence=use_clc_persistence,
   184	    )
   185	    ts = cjax.TensorSpec
   186	    a_spec = ts(divisibility=(1, 8), static=False)
   187	    b_spec = ts(mode=_bmode, divisibility=(1, 1, 8), static=False)
   188	    cu_spec = ts(static=False)
   189	    d_spec = ts(divisibility=(1, 8), static=False)
   190	    call = cutlass_call(
   191	        launcher,
   192	        output_shape_dtype=jax.ShapeDtypeStruct((M, N), a.dtype),
   193	        input_spec=(a_spec, b_spec, cu_spec),
   194	        output_spec=(d_spec,),
   195	        use_static_tensors=False,
   196	    )
   197	    return call(a, w, cu_seqlens.astype(jnp.int32))

    35	def _unpack_pairs_u32(x: jax.Array) -> tuple[jax.Array, jax.Array]:
    36	    """``[..., 2F]`` of a 16-bit dtype -> ``([..., F], [..., F])``, undoing ``_pack_pairs_u32``."""
    37	    pairs = x.reshape(*x.shape[:-1], x.shape[-1] // 2, 2)
    38	    packed = jax.lax.bitcast_convert_type(pairs, jnp.uint32)
    39	    lo = (packed & jnp.uint32(0xFFFF)).astype(jnp.uint16)
    40	    hi = (packed >> jnp.uint32(16)).astype(jnp.uint16)
    41	    return (
    42	        jax.lax.bitcast_convert_type(lo, x.dtype),
    43	        jax.lax.bitcast_convert_type(hi, x.dtype),
    44	    )
    45	
    46	
    47	# `bitcast_convert_type` has no AD rule, so the interleave carries its own transpose.
    48	@jax.custom_vjp
    49	def _interleave_halves(gate: jax.Array, up: jax.Array) -> jax.Array:
    50	    return _pack_pairs_u32(gate, up)
    51	
    52	
    53	def _interleave_halves_fwd(gate, up):
    54	    return _pack_pairs_u32(gate, up), None
    55	
    56	
    57	def _interleave_halves_bwd(_, ct):
    58	    return _unpack_pairs_u32(ct)
    59	
    60	
    61	_interleave_halves.defvjp(_interleave_halves_fwd, _interleave_halves_bwd)
    62	
    63	
    64	def _interleave_gate_up(moe_w13: jax.Array, moe_dim: int) -> jax.Array:
    65	    """grug w13 [E,H,2I] gate=[:I], up=[I:] -> interleaved [g0,u0,g1,u1,...] (QuACK layout)."""
    66	    # The split's width check matters here: the packed path would broadcast mismatched halves
    67	    # against each other and return a wrong-width array instead of raising.
    68	    gate, up = split_moe_w13_output(moe_w13, intermediate_dim=moe_dim, interleaved=False)
    69	    if moe_w13.dtype.itemsize != 2:
    70	        return jnp.stack([gate, up], axis=-1).reshape(moe_w13.shape)
    71	    return _interleave_halves(gate, up)
    72	
    73	
    74	def _swiglu_gate_up_backward(gu: jax.Array, dh: jax.Array) -> jax.Array:
    75	    """Cotangent of the interleaved gate/up pre-activations, given the SwiGLU output's."""
    76	    if gu.dtype.itemsize == 2:
    77	        gate, up = _unpack_pairs_u32(gu)
    78	    else:
    79	        gate, up = gu[..., 0::2], gu[..., 1::2]
    80	    sg = jax.nn.sigmoid(gate)
    81	    silu = gate * sg
    82	    dgate = dh * up * (sg + silu * (1.0 - sg))
    83	    dup = dh * silu
    84	    if gu.dtype.itemsize == 2:
    85	        return _pack_pairs_u32(dgate.astype(gu.dtype), dup.astype(gu.dtype))
    86	    return jnp.stack([dgate, dup], axis=-1).reshape(gu.shape)

   243	@functools.partial(jax.custom_vjp, nondiff_argnums=(2,))
   244	def _gather_dispatch_rows(
   245	    x_local: Float[Array, "Tlocal H"], sorted_indices: Int[Array, "TK"], topk: int
   246	) -> Float[Array, "TK H"]:
   247	    """Build the expert-sorted dispatch buffer with one gather.
   248	
   249	    Equivalent to ``jnp.repeat(x_local, topk, axis=0)[sorted_indices]`` without
   250	    materializing the repeated buffer or running a data-sized permute. The backward pass
   251	    is the transpose: each token sums the cotangent rows of its ``topk`` sorted slots.
   252	    """
   253	    return x_local[sorted_indices // topk]
   254

   256	def _gather_dispatch_rows_fwd(
   257	    x_local: Float[Array, "Tlocal H"], sorted_indices: Int[Array, "TK"], topk: int
   258	) -> tuple[Float[Array, "TK H"], Int[Array, "TK"]]:
   259	    return _gather_dispatch_rows(x_local, sorted_indices, topk), sorted_indices

   261	
   262	def _gather_dispatch_rows_bwd(
   263	    topk: int, sorted_indices: Int[Array, "TK"], cotangent: Float[Array, "TK H"]
   264	) -> tuple[Float[Array, "Tlocal H"], None]:
   265	    tokens_per_shard = sorted_indices.shape[0] // topk
   266	    positions = jnp.argsort(sorted_indices).reshape(tokens_per_shard, topk)
   267	    if sonic_gather_sum_available():
   268	        ones = jnp.ones((tokens_per_shard, topk), dtype=jnp.float32)
   269	        grad_x = sonic_gather_sum(cotangent, positions, ones)
   270	    else:
   271	        grad_x = jnp.sum(cotangent[positions], axis=1, dtype=jnp.float32)
   272	    return grad_x.astype(cotangent.dtype), None

   278	def _loop_local_zeros(
   279	    rows: int, hidden_dim: int, dtype, tie: Int[Array, "..."], site: int = 0
   280	) -> Float[Array, "rows H"]:
   281	    """Zero buffer for an in-place ``ragged_all_to_all`` output slot, built so XLA never copies it.
   282	
   283	    ``ragged_all_to_all`` writes its result in place into the output-init operand. A literal
   284	    ``jnp.zeros`` init is a trace-time constant: it gets hoisted out of the layer scan (and
   285	    identical inits CSE together), so CopyInsertion must mint a fresh multi-GB device copy of
   286	    the pristine zeros into the a2a's output slot on every scan iteration. Deriving the zeros
   287	    from ``tie`` -- a per-site, per-iteration traced value -- keeps each init inside the loop
   288	    body and distinct from every other init, so it lowers to one write-only fill kernel whose
   289	    buffer the a2a updates directly.
   290	
   291	    ``tie`` must be a non-negative integer array (group or transfer sizes): with ``site >= 0``,
   292	    ``min(tie[0], -site) + site`` is exactly zero at runtime but not foldable at compile time.
   293	
   294	    ``site`` must be distinct per call site. Two sites can hold the SAME tie tensor without it
   295	    being obvious (dispatch send_sizes and return recv_sizes are one tensor in ep_common), and
   296	    same-shape same-tie fills CSE into one value with two destructive in-place a2a consumers --
   297	    which makes CopyInsertion mint back the multi-GB copy this helper exists to prevent.
   298	    """
   299	    zero = (jnp.minimum(tie.reshape(-1)[0], -site) + site).astype(dtype)
   300	    return jax.lax.broadcast(zero, (rows, hidden_dim))
   301	
   302	
   303	@functools.partial(jax.custom_vjp, nondiff_argnums=(0, 1))
   304	def _dispatch_ragged_a2a(
   305	    capacity: int,
   306	    source_rows: int,
   307	    chunk_source: Float[Array, "TK H"],
   308	    input_offsets: Int[Array, "U"],
   309	    send_sizes: Int[Array, "U"],
   310	    output_offsets: Int[Array, "U"],
   311	    recv_sizes: Int[Array, "U"],
   312	) -> Float[Array, "C H"]:
   313	    """Dispatch-direction ``ragged_all_to_all`` into a freshly zeroed receiver buffer.
   314	
   315	    Owning the output-init here (instead of taking a caller-built ``jnp.zeros``) lets both the
   316	    primal and the transposed direction build their inits with `_loop_local_zeros`. jax's
   317	    built-in transpose rule inits the swapped a2a with plain zeros, which XLA hoists out of
   318	    the layer loop and re-copies every iteration; the custom vjp below is that same rule with
   319	    the init construction replaced. Zeros stay load-bearing: receiver rows no peer writes must
   320	    read 0 downstream, and dropped source rows must read a 0 cotangent in the backward.
   321	    """
   322	    del source_rows
   323	    output_init = _loop_local_zeros(capacity, chunk_source.shape[1], chunk_source.dtype, send_sizes, site=1)
   324	    return jax.lax.ragged_all_to_all(
   325	        chunk_source, output_init, input_offsets, send_sizes, output_offsets, recv_sizes, axis_name="expert"
   326	    )
   327	
   328	
   329	def _dispatch_ragged_a2a_fwd(
   330	    capacity: int,
   331	    source_rows: int,
   332	    chunk_source: Float[Array, "TK H"],
   333	    input_offsets: Int[Array, "U"],
   334	    send_sizes: Int[Array, "U"],
   335	    output_offsets: Int[Array, "U"],
   336	    recv_sizes: Int[Array, "U"],
   337	) -> tuple[Float[Array, "C H"], tuple[jax.Array, jax.Array, jax.Array, jax.Array]]:
   338	    result = _dispatch_ragged_a2a(
   339	        capacity, source_rows, chunk_source, input_offsets, send_sizes, output_offsets, recv_sizes
   340	    )
   341	    return result, (input_offsets, send_sizes, output_offsets, recv_sizes)
   342	
   343	
   344	def _dispatch_ragged_a2a_bwd(
   345	    capacity: int,
   346	    source_rows: int,
   347	    residuals: tuple[jax.Array, jax.Array, jax.Array, jax.Array],
   348	    cotangent: Float[Array, "C H"],
   349	) -> tuple[Float[Array, "TK H"], None, None, None, None]:
   350	    del capacity
   351	    input_offsets, send_sizes, output_offsets, recv_sizes = residuals
   352	    # The transpose of a ragged all-to-all is the reverse ragged all-to-all: swap the send and
   353	    # recv roles and exchange the offset vectors across shards, exactly as jax's transpose rule
   354	    # does. Source rows that were clipped receive no cotangent and keep the init's zeros.
   355	    output_offsets_x = jax.lax.all_to_all(output_offsets, "expert", 0, 0, tiled=True)
   356	    input_offsets_x = jax.lax.all_to_all(input_offsets, "expert", 0, 0, tiled=True)
   357	    # Tie to this side's send_sizes, not recv_sizes: the return path's passthrough fill ties to
   358	    # its own send_sizes, which is the SAME tensor as this dispatch's recv_sizes, and two fills
   359	    # with identical shape and tie CSE back into one value with a destructive consumer --
   360	    # re-minting exactly the copy this construction removes.
   361	    init = _loop_local_zeros(source_rows, cotangent.shape[1], cotangent.dtype, send_sizes, site=2)
   362	    source_ct = jax.lax.ragged_all_to_all(
   363	        cotangent, init, output_offsets_x, recv_sizes, input_offsets_x, send_sizes, axis_name="expert"
   364	    )
   365	    return source_ct, None, None, None, None
   366	
   367	
   368	_dispatch_ragged_a2a.defvjp(_dispatch_ragged_a2a_fwd, _dispatch_ragged_a2a_bwd)
   369

   371	@functools.partial(jax.custom_vjp, nondiff_argnums=(0,))
   372	def _return_ragged_a2a(
   373	    capacity: int,
   374	    out_dispatch: Float[Array, "C H"],
   375	    returned: Float[Array, "TK H"],
   376	    input_offsets: Int[Array, "U"],
   377	    send_sizes: Int[Array, "U"],
   378	    output_offsets: Int[Array, "U"],
   379	    recv_sizes: Int[Array, "U"],
   380	) -> Float[Array, "TK H"]:
   381	    """Return-direction ``ragged_all_to_all``: write expert outputs back over ``returned``.
   382	
   383	    Same construction as `_dispatch_ragged_a2a`: the primal is unchanged, and the custom vjp
   384	    replicates jax's transpose rule operation for operation, replacing only the transposed
   385	    a2a's zero init so it is built per-iteration instead of hoisted and copied.
   386	    """
   387	    del capacity
   388	    return jax.lax.ragged_all_to_all(
   389	        out_dispatch, returned, input_offsets, send_sizes, output_offsets, recv_sizes, axis_name="expert"
   390	    )
   391	
   392	
   393	def _return_ragged_a2a_fwd(
   394	    capacity: int,
   395	    out_dispatch: Float[Array, "C H"],
   396	    returned: Float[Array, "TK H"],
   397	    input_offsets: Int[Array, "U"],
   398	    send_sizes: Int[Array, "U"],
   399	    output_offsets: Int[Array, "U"],
   400	    recv_sizes: Int[Array, "U"],
   401	) -> tuple[Float[Array, "TK H"], tuple[jax.Array, jax.Array, jax.Array, jax.Array]]:
   402	    result = _return_ragged_a2a(
   403	        capacity, out_dispatch, returned, input_offsets, send_sizes, output_offsets, recv_sizes
   404	    )
   405	    return result, (input_offsets, send_sizes, output_offsets, recv_sizes)
   406	
   407	
   408	def _return_ragged_a2a_bwd(
   409	    capacity: int,
   410	    residuals: tuple[jax.Array, jax.Array, jax.Array, jax.Array],
   411	    cotangent: Float[Array, "TK H"],
   412	) -> tuple[Float[Array, "C H"], Float[Array, "TK H"], None, None, None, None]:
   413	    input_offsets, send_sizes, output_offsets, recv_sizes = residuals
   414	    output_offsets_x = jax.lax.all_to_all(output_offsets, "expert", 0, 0, tiled=True)
   415	    input_offsets_x = jax.lax.all_to_all(input_offsets, "expert", 0, 0, tiled=True)
   416	    init = _loop_local_zeros(capacity, cotangent.shape[1], cotangent.dtype, recv_sizes, site=3)
   417	    out_dispatch_ct = jax.lax.ragged_all_to_all(
   418	        cotangent, init, output_offsets_x, recv_sizes, input_offsets_x, send_sizes, axis_name="expert"
   419	    )
   420	    # Rows this a2a overwrote took their value from ``out_dispatch``, so the pass-through
   421	    # cotangent to ``returned`` is zeroed on exactly the written intervals. This mirrors jax's
   422	    # transpose rule op for op (interval marks, cumsum, integer select_n) so the behavior is
   423	    # bit-identical, including on degenerate empty-group offset patterns.
   424	    interval_marks = (
   425	        jnp.zeros(cotangent.shape[0], jnp.int32).at[output_offsets_x].set(1).at[output_offsets_x + recv_sizes].add(-1)
   426	    )
   427	    written = jnp.broadcast_to(jnp.cumsum(interval_marks)[:, None], cotangent.shape)
   428	    passthrough_zero = _loop_local_zeros(cotangent.shape[0], cotangent.shape[1], cotangent.dtype, send_sizes, site=4)
   429	    returned_ct = jax.lax.select_n(written, cotangent, passthrough_zero)
   430	    return out_dispatch_ct, returned_ct, None, None, None, None
   431	
   432	
   433	_return_ragged_a2a.defvjp(_return_ragged_a2a_fwd, _return_ragged_a2a_bwd)

    13	def _sort_activations(inputs: Float[Array, "N *tail"], sort_indices: Int[Array, "N"]) -> Float[Array, "N *tail"]:
    14	    if inputs.shape[0] != sort_indices.shape[0]:
    15	        raise ValueError(f"Expected matching leading dims, got {inputs.shape[0]} and {sort_indices.shape[0]}")
    16	    return _sort_activations_custom(inputs, sort_indices)

    20	def _sort_activations_custom(
    21	    inputs: Float[Array, "N *tail"], sort_indices: Int[Array, "N"]
    22	) -> Float[Array, "N *tail"]:
    23	    return inputs[sort_indices, ...]

    27	    inputs: Float[Array, "N *tail"], sort_indices: Int[Array, "N"]

    29	    return _sort_activations_custom(inputs, sort_indices), sort_indices

    34	) -> tuple[Float[Array, "N *tail"], None]:
    35	    sort_indices = residuals
    36	    return _sort_activations_custom(grads, jnp.argsort(sort_indices)), None

    42	def _ranks_within_groups(group_ids: Int[Array, "N"], *, num_groups: int) -> Int[Array, "N"]:
    43	    """Return the zero-based rank of each item in its group."""
    44	    order = jnp.argsort(group_ids, stable=True)
    45	    inverse_order = jnp.argsort(order)
    46	    counts = jnp.bincount(group_ids, length=num_groups).astype(jnp.int32)
    47	    starts = jnp.cumsum(counts) - counts
    48	    sorted_ranks = jnp.arange(group_ids.shape[0], dtype=jnp.int32) - starts[group_ids[order]]
    49	    return sorted_ranks[inverse_order]

    52	def _assignment_sources(
    53	    linear_indices: Int[Array, "N"],
    54	    *,
    55	    send_size: int,
    56	) -> Int[Array, "send"]:
    57	    """Map each fixed send slot to its source assignment."""
    58	    assignments = linear_indices.shape[0]
    59	    return (
    60	        jnp.full((send_size,), assignments, dtype=jnp.int32)
    61	        .at[linear_indices]
    62	        .set(jnp.arange(assignments, dtype=jnp.int32), mode="drop")
    63	    )

    66	def _token_sources(
    67	    assignment_sources: Int[Array, "send"],
    68	    *,
    69	    assignments: int,
    70	    topk: int,
    71	    tokens: int,
    72	) -> Int[Array, "send"]:
    73	    """Map send slots to token rows and use the padding row for empty slots."""
    74	    return jnp.where(
    75	        assignment_sources < assignments,
    76	        assignment_sources // topk,
    77	        tokens,
    78	    )

    81	def _prefix_cap_counts(counts: Int[Array, "E"], *, capacity: int) -> Int[Array, "E"]:
    82	    accepted = []
    83	    remaining = jnp.array(capacity, dtype=jnp.int32)
    84	    for expert in range(int(counts.shape[0])):
    85	        take = jnp.minimum(counts[expert], remaining)
    86	        accepted.append(take)
    87	        remaining = jnp.maximum(remaining - take, 0)
    88	    return jnp.stack(accepted, axis=0)
    89	
    90	
    91	def _clip_receiver_group_sizes(
    92	    global_group_sizes: Int[Array, "S E"],
    93	    *,
    94	    local_expert_size: int,
    95	    receiver_capacity: int,
    96	) -> Int[Array, "S E"]:
    97	    """Clip sender->expert group sizes so each receiver shard stays within capacity."""
    98	    num_senders = int(global_group_sizes.shape[0])
    99	    num_experts = int(global_group_sizes.shape[1])
   100	    if num_experts % local_expert_size != 0:
   101	        raise ValueError(f"num_experts={num_experts} must be divisible by local_expert_size={local_expert_size}")
   102	    num_receivers = num_experts // local_expert_size
   103	    if num_receivers != num_senders:
   104	        raise ValueError(f"sender/receiver shard mismatch: num_senders={num_senders}, num_receivers={num_receivers}")
   105	
   106	    clipped_by_receiver: list[jax.Array] = []
   107	    for receiver_index in range(num_receivers):
   108	        start = receiver_index * local_expert_size
   109	        stop = start + local_expert_size
   110	        receiver_counts = global_group_sizes[:, start:stop]
   111	        receiver_totals = jnp.sum(receiver_counts, axis=0, dtype=jnp.int32)
   112	        accepted_totals = _prefix_cap_counts(receiver_totals, capacity=receiver_capacity)
   113	        remaining = accepted_totals
   114	        accepted_rows: list[jax.Array] = []
   115	        for sender_index in range(num_senders):
   116	            # Greedy first-sender-wins: earlier shards get priority when capacity is scarce.
   117	            accepted = jnp.minimum(receiver_counts[sender_index], remaining)
   118	            accepted_rows.append(accepted)
   119	            remaining = remaining - accepted
   120	        clipped_by_receiver.append(jnp.stack(accepted_rows, axis=0))
   121	
   122	    return jnp.concatenate(clipped_by_receiver, axis=1)
   123	
   124	
   125	def _align_up_rows(values: Int[Array, "..."], alignment: int) -> Int[Array, "..."]:
   126	    """Round each row count up to a multiple of ``alignment``.
   127	
   128	    ``alignment == 1`` returns the input array itself, so a caller that leaves alignment off
   129	    emits no arithmetic at all and traces exactly the graph it traced before this existed.
   130	    """
   131	    if alignment < 1:
   132	        raise ValueError(f"alignment must be positive, got {alignment}")
   133	    if alignment == 1:
   134	        return values
   135	    return ((values + alignment - 1) // alignment) * alignment
   136	
   137	
   138	class ExpertA2aParams(NamedTuple):
   139	    """Offset/size vectors for one direction of an expert-granular ``ragged_all_to_all``."""
   140	
   141	    input_offsets: Int[Array, "U"]
   142	    send_sizes: Int[Array, "U"]
   143	    output_offsets: Int[Array, "U"]
   144	    recv_sizes: Int[Array, "U"]
   145	
   146	
   147	def _expert_granular_a2a_params(
   148	    all_group_sizes: Int[Array, "S E"],
   149	    clipped_group_sizes: Int[Array, "S E"],
   150	    shard_id: Int[Array, ""],
   151	    *,
   152	    local_expert_size: int,
   153	    receiver_alignment: int = 1,
   154	) -> tuple[ExpertA2aParams, ExpertA2aParams]:
   155	    """Build dispatch and return ``ragged_all_to_all`` parameters at (peer, expert) granularity.
   156	
   157	    One update per (destination shard, local expert). Sender reads each global-expert
   158	    group at its *unclipped* offset with its *clipped* size, so accepted rows need no
   159	    compaction: they are the prefix of each group. Receiver offsets pack arriving rows
   160	    expert-major (sender-major within each expert), so the received buffer needs no local
   161	    permute before the grouped MLP. The return direction is the exact mirror: it reads the
   162	    expert-major receiver buffer and writes valid prefixes back to the sender's unclipped
   163	    positions, leaving dropped rows at the output operand's values.
   164	
   165	    ``receiver_alignment`` rounds each receiver group's *extent* up to a multiple of that many
   166	    rows, which starts every group on an aligned row and leaves up to ``alignment - 1`` unwritten
   167	    rows between groups. It changes only where the receiver puts each group: senders read the
   168	    same rows and send the same sizes, the accepted set is untouched, and the return direction
   169	    reads the same valid prefixes back out. The receiver buffer must then hold
   170	    ``capacity + (alignment - 1) * groups`` rows, since the per-group slack is charged to the
   171	    buffer rather than to the capacity that decides drops.
   172	    """
   173	    num_shards = all_group_sizes.shape[0]
   174	
   175	    # [src, dest, e]: rows sender `src` contributes to `dest`'s local expert `e`.
   176	    clipped = clipped_group_sizes.reshape(num_shards, num_shards, local_expert_size)
   177	
   178	    # Sender side: unclipped group starts in this shard's expert-sorted buffer.
   179	    unclipped_starts = jnp.cumsum(all_group_sizes, axis=1) - all_group_sizes
   180	    my_send = clipped[shard_id]  # [dest, e]
   181	    dispatch_input_offsets = unclipped_starts[shard_id].reshape(num_shards, local_expert_size)
   182	
   183	    # Receiver side: expert-major segment starts on each destination, sender-major within.
   184	    dest_totals = jnp.sum(clipped, axis=0)  # [dest, e]
   185	    group_extents = _align_up_rows(dest_totals, receiver_alignment)  # [dest, e]
   186	    expert_starts = jnp.cumsum(group_extents, axis=1) - group_extents
   187	    senders_before_me = (jnp.cumsum(clipped, axis=0) - clipped)[shard_id]  # [dest, e]
   188	    dispatch_output_offsets = expert_starts + senders_before_me
   189	
   190	    # What each source sends this shard, source-major -- also the return direction's sends.
   191	    inbound = clipped[:, shard_id, :]  # [src, e]
   192	
   193	    dispatch = ExpertA2aParams(
   194	        dispatch_input_offsets.reshape(-1),
   195	        my_send.reshape(-1),
   196	        dispatch_output_offsets.reshape(-1),
   197	        inbound.reshape(-1),
   198	    )
   199	
   200	    # Return: read this shard's expert-major receiver buffer, write back to each original
   201	    # sender's unclipped sorted positions for the experts this shard owns.
   202	    my_expert_starts = expert_starts[shard_id]  # [e]
   203	    senders_before = jnp.cumsum(inbound, axis=0) - inbound  # [src, e]
   204	    return_input_offsets = my_expert_starts[None, :] + senders_before
   205	    my_global_experts = jnp.arange(local_expert_size, dtype=jnp.int32) + shard_id * local_expert_size
   206	    return_output_offsets = unclipped_starts[:, my_global_experts]  # [src, e]
   207	
   208	    ret = ExpertA2aParams(
   209	        return_input_offsets.reshape(-1),
   210	        inbound.reshape(-1),
   211	        return_output_offsets.reshape(-1),
   212	        my_send.reshape(-1),
   213	    )
   214	    return dispatch, ret

   631	def ragged_all_to_all(
   632	    operand, output, input_offsets, send_sizes, output_offsets, recv_sizes, *,
   633	    axis_name, axis_index_groups = None):
   634	  """Ragged version of :func:`all_to_all` collective.
   635	
   636	  We say data are "ragged" when they can be represented as a list of arrays
   637	  whose shapes differ only in the size of the leading axis. For example, these
   638	  data are ragged, comprising four component arrays::
   639	
   640	    ragged_data = [jnp.arange(3), jnp.arange(1), jnp.arange(4), jnp.arange(1)]
   641	
   642	  We often instead want a contiguous representation, e.g. for batching. But
   643	  because the shapes of the components differ, we can't apply ``jnp.stack`` to
   644	  represent these data by a single rectangular array with the leading axis
   645	  indexing the component arrays. So instead of stacking, we concatenate along
   646	  the leading axis and keep track of offsets and sizes.
   647	
   648	  That is, we can represent ragged data contiguously using a triple of dense
   649	  arrays ``(data, offsets, sizes)``:
   650	
   651	    * ``data``: the concatenated component arrays,
   652	    * ``offsets``: 1D array of indices into the leading axis of ``data``
   653	      indicating where the data for each component array begins,
   654	    * ``sizes``: 1D array of sizes of the leading axis of each component array.
   655	
   656	  We refer to this triple as a ragged array. (Offsets can't be computed from
   657	  sizes in general to allow for internal padding.)
   658	
   659	  For example::
   660	
   661	    data: f32[8,3] = jnp.array([
   662	        [a,b,c], [d,e,f], [g,h,i], [j,k,l], [m,n,o], [p,q,r], [s,t,u], [v,w,x],
   663	    ])
   664	    offsets: i32[3] = jnp.array([0, 1, 4])
   665	    sizes: i32[3] = jnp.array([1, 3, 4])
   666	
   667	    # To extract the first component array, of type f32[1,3]
   668	    data[offsets[0]:offsets[0]+sizes[0]]
   669	
   670	    # To extract the second component array, of type f32[3,3]
   671	    data[offsets[1]:offsets[1]+sizes[1]]
   672	
   673	    # To extract the third component array, of type f32[4,3]
   674	    data[offsets[2]:offsets[2]+sizes[2]]
   675	
   676	  The ``ragged_all_to_all`` collective operation communicates slices of ragged
   677	  arrays between devices. Each caller is both a sender and a receiver. The
   678	  ``input_offsets`` and ``send_sizes`` arguments indicate the slices of the
   679	  caller's ``operand`` to be sent. Received results are returned in an array
   680	  that has the same value of the argument ``output`` except with received values
   681	  written at some slices. The ``output_offsets`` argument does *not* indicate
   682	  the offsets at which all the received results are written; instead,
   683	  ``output_offsets`` indicates the offsets at which the *sent* slices are
   684	  written on their corresponding receivers. The sizes of received slices are
   685	  indicated by ``recv_sizes``. See below for details.
   686	
   687	  The arrays ``input_offsets``, ``send_sizes``,``output_offsets``, and
   688	  ``recv_sizes`` must all be the same length, and that length must be divisible
   689	  by the size of the mapped axis ``axis_name``. Moreover, ``send_sizes`` and
   690	  ``recv_sizes`` must satisfy::
   691	
   692	    jnp.all(send_sizes == jax.lax.all_to_all(recv_sizes, axis_name, 0, 0, tiled=True))
   693	
   694	  Specifically, given a call::
   695	
   696	    result = ragged_all_to_all(operand, output, input_offsets, send_sizes,
   697	                               output_offsets, recv_sizes, axis_name)
   698	
   699	  the caller sends data like::
   700	
   701	    assert len(input_offsets) == len(send_sizes) == len(output_offsets) == len(recv_sizes)
   702	    N = len(input_offsets)
   703	    slices_per_device, leftover = divmod(N, lax.axis_size(axis_name))
   704	    assert not leftover
   705	
   706	    for i in range(N):
   707	      dst_idx = i // slices_per_device
   708	      SEND(data=operand[input_offsets[i]:input_offsets[i]+send_sizes[i]],
   709	           axis_name=axis_name, to_axis_index=dst_idx)
   710	
   711	  and receives data in ``result`` like::
   712	
   713	    result = output
   714	    output_offsets_ = jax.lax.all_to_all(output_offsets, axis_name, 0, 0, tiled=True)
   715	    for i in range(N):
   716	      src_idx = i // slices_per_device
   717	      result = result.at[output_offsets_[i]:output_offsets_[i]+recv_sizes[i]
   718	                    ].set(RECEIVE(axis_name=axis_name, from_axis_index=src_idx))
   719	
   720	  where ``SEND`` and ``RECEIVE`` are pseudocode. Notice that a caller's local
   721	  ``output_offsets`` does not indicate the offsets at which its local ``result``
   722	  is updated; instead, it indicates where the corresponding sent slices are
   723	  written on their destination instances. To compute the local offsets at which
   724	  received data are written, we apply an ``all_to_all`` on ``output_offsets``.
   725	
   726	  For example, if we apply a ``ragged_all_to_all`` along an axis of size 2, with
   727	  these arguments in each mapped function instance::
   728	
   729	    axis index 0:
   730	      operand = [1, 2, 2]
   731	      output = [0, 0, 0, 0]
   732	      input_offsets = [0, 1]
   733	      send_sizes = [1, 2]
   734	      output_offsets = [0, 0]
   735	      recv_sizes = [1, 1]
   736	
   737	    axis index 1:
   738	      operand = [3, 4, 0]
   739	      output = [0, 0, 0, 0]
   740	      input_offsets = [0, 1]
   741	      send_sizes = [1, 1]
   742	      output_offsets = [1, 2]
   743	      recv_sizes = [2, 1]
   744	
   745	  then::
   746	
   747	    axis index 0:
   748	      result = [1, 3, 0, 0]
   749	
   750	    axis index 1:
   820	    return axis_index_p.bind(axis_name=axis_name)
   821	  else:
   822	    inner_size = 1
   823	    index = lax.asarray(0)
   824	    for name in reversed(axis_name):
   825	      index += axis_index(name) * inner_size
   826	      inner_size *= axis_size(name)
   827	    return index
   828	
   829	
   830	def axis_size(axis_name: AxisName) -> int:
   831	  """Return the size of the mapped axis ``axis_name``.
   832	
   833	  Args:
   834	    axis_name: hashable Python object used to name the mapped axis.
   835	
   836	  Returns:
   837	    An integer representing the size.
   838	
   839	  For example, with 8 XLA devices available:
   840	
   841	  >>> mesh = jax.make_mesh((8,), 'i')
   842	  >>> @jax.shard_map(mesh=mesh, in_specs=jax.P('i'), out_specs=jax.P())
   843	  ... def f(_):
   844	  ...   return lax.axis_size('i')
   845	  ...
   846	  >>> f(jax.device_put(jnp.zeros(16), jax.NamedSharding(mesh, P('i'))))
   847	  Array(8, dtype=int32, weak_type=True)
   848	
   849	  >>> mesh = jax.make_mesh((4, 2), ('i', 'j'))
   850	  >>> @jax.shard_map(mesh=mesh, in_specs=jax.P('i', 'j'), out_specs=jax.P())
   851	  ... def f(_):
   852	  ...   return lax.axis_size(('i', 'j'))
   853	  ...
   854	  >>> f(jax.device_put(jnp.zeros((16, 8)), jax.NamedSharding(mesh, P('i', 'j'))))
   855	  Array(8, dtype=int32, weak_type=True)
   856	  """
   857	  return _axis_size(axis_name)

   871	def _constant_reduction(prim, axis_data, arg, axes, axis_index_groups):
   872	  assert axis_data.name in axes
   873	  if axis_index_groups: raise NotImplementedError
   874	  new_axes = tuple(n for n in axes if n != axis_data.name)
   875	  if new_axes:
   876	    arg = (prim.bind(arg, axes=new_axes) if prim is psum_invariant_p else
   877	           prim.bind(arg, axes=new_axes, axis_index_groups=axis_index_groups))
   878	  if prim is psum_p:
   879	    out = lax._const(arg, axis_data.size) * arg
   880	  elif prim in (pmin_p, pmax_p):
   881	    out = arg
   882	  else:
   883	    raise Exception(f"Unrecognized reducer: {prim}")
   884	  return out, None

  1173	def test_aligned_receiver_layout_is_what_the_wgrad_pad_would_have_built():
  1174	    """The claim the pre-aligned cuDNN entry point rests on.
  1175	
  1176	    `pad_grouped_rows` turns an unaligned receiver buffer into the kernel's aligned layout by
  1177	    copying it. An aligned receiver layout is that same layout, built by the collective instead.
  1178	    Both the operand and the offsets the kernel sees must therefore agree row for row -- if they
  1179	    did not, skipping the pad would change what the kernel computes.
  1180	    """
  1181	    shards, local_experts, tokens, topk, hidden = 4, 3, 10, 2, 5
  1182	    num_experts = shards * local_experts
  1183	    assignments = tokens * topk
  1184	    capacity = int(0.7 * assignments)
  1185	    alignment = _GROUP_ALIGNMENT
  1186	
  1187	    rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
  1188	    selected = rng.integers(0, num_experts, size=(shards, tokens, topk))
  1189	    payload = rng.normal(size=(shards, assignments, hidden)).astype(np.float32)
  1190	    sorted_payload = np.stack([payload[s][np.argsort(selected[s].reshape(-1), kind="stable")] for s in range(shards)])
  1191	    group_sizes = np.stack(
  1192	        [np.bincount(selected[s].reshape(-1), minlength=num_experts) for s in range(shards)]
  1193	    ).astype(np.int32)
  1194	    clipped = np.asarray(
  1195	        _clip_receiver_group_sizes(
  1196	            jnp.asarray(group_sizes), local_expert_size=local_experts, receiver_capacity=capacity
  1197	        )
  1198	    )
  1199	    assert clipped.sum() < group_sizes.sum()  # drops actually happen
  1200	
  1201	    buffers = {}
  1202	    for receiver_alignment in (1, alignment):
  1203	        params = [
  1204	            _expert_granular_a2a_params(
  1205	                jnp.asarray(group_sizes),
  1206	                jnp.asarray(clipped),
  1207	                jnp.asarray(s),
  1208	                local_expert_size=local_experts,
  1209	                receiver_alignment=receiver_alignment,
  1210	            )
  1211	            for s in range(shards)
  1212	        ]
  1213	        rows = capacity + (receiver_alignment - 1) * local_experts
  1214	        received = [np.zeros((rows, hidden), np.float32) for _ in range(shards)]
  1215	        _simulate_ragged_a2a(sorted_payload, received, [p[0] for p in params])
  1216	        buffers[receiver_alignment] = received
  1217	
  1218	    arrivals = clipped.reshape(shards, shards, local_experts).sum(axis=0)  # [receiver, local expert]
  1219	    for receiver in range(shards):
  1220	        active = arrivals[receiver].astype(np.int32)
  1221	        padded, padded_offsets = pad_grouped_rows(jnp.asarray(buffers[1][receiver]), jnp.asarray(active))
  1222	        aligned = buffers[alignment][receiver]
  1223	        extents = -(-active // alignment) * alignment
  1224	
  1225	        np.testing.assert_array_equal(np.asarray(padded), aligned)
  1226	        np.testing.assert_array_equal(np.asarray(padded_offsets), np.cumsum(extents))
  1227	
  1228	        # ...and what the backend hands the pre-aligned entry point is exactly those extents,
  1229	        # so its `cumsum` reproduces the offsets the padding path computes.
  1230	        np.testing.assert_array_equal(np.asarray(_align_up_rows(jnp.asarray(active), alignment)), extents)
  1231

  1233	def test_expert_mlp_over_an_aligned_receiver_buffer_matches_the_packed_layout():
  1234	    """The other half of the claim: the expert MLP reads the aligned layout as if it were packed.
  1235	
  1236	    Each grouped GEMM here is row-wise, so a group's alignment slack -- zero rows the collective
  1237	    never writes -- contributes nothing and produces zeros, and every arriving row gets the same
  1238	    value it would have got packed. This is the portable `ragged_dot` path, which is what runs
  1239	    wherever the cuDNN kernels do not.
  1240	    """
  1280	    assert _resolve_receiver_alignment(None) == 1
  1281	    assert _resolve_receiver_alignment(2 * _GROUP_ALIGNMENT) == 2 * _GROUP_ALIGNMENT
  1282	    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="multiple"):
  1283	        _resolve_receiver_alignment(_GROUP_ALIGNMENT + 1)
  1284	    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="positive"):
  1285	        _resolve_receiver_alignment(0)
  1286	
  1287	
  1288	def test_receiver_alignment_routes_the_expert_mlp_to_the_prealigned_wgrad(monkeypatch):
  1289	    """An aligned receiver layout is the only thing that lets the cute path skip the pad."""
  1290	    monkeypatch.setattr(ep_ragged_all_to_all, "_quack_grouped_gemm_available", lambda: True)
  1291	    select = ep_ragged_all_to_all._select_expert_mlp
  1292	    assert select(jax.nn.silu) is ep_ragged_all_to_all._cute_expert_mlp
  1293	    assert select(jax.nn.silu, receiver_alignment=1) is ep_ragged_all_to_all._cute_expert_mlp
  1294	    assert select(jax.nn.silu, receiver_alignment=_GROUP_ALIGNMENT) is ep_ragged_all_to_all._cute_expert_mlp_prealigned
  1295	    # The portable path reads group sizes off whatever buffer it is handed, aligned or not.
  1296	    assert select(jax.nn.gelu, receiver_alignment=_GROUP_ALIGNMENT) is _ragged_dot_expert_mlp
